Add Anthropic MCP Registry REST API v0 compatibility (#178)

* Add Anthropic MCP Registry REST API v0 compatibility

Implements the standard Anthropic MCP Registry REST API specification
to enable seamless integration with downstream applications and MCP
ecosystem tooling.

New Features:
- Pydantic models for Anthropic API v0 schema (anthropic_schema.py)
- Data transformation service to bridge internal and external formats
- Three public API endpoints:
  - GET /v0/servers - List all MCP servers with pagination
  - GET /v0/servers/{serverName}/versions - List server versions
  - GET /v0/servers/{serverName}/versions/{version} - Get server details
- Session-based authentication via enhanced_auth dependency
- Permission-aware filtering (users see only authorized servers)
- Cursor-based pagination support

Implementation Details:
- Reverse-DNS naming convention (io.mcpgateway/server-name)
- Default version 1.0.0 for all servers (supports "latest" alias)
- Nginx configuration for /v0/* endpoints with CORS support
- Maintains existing security model and permission checks

Spec Reference:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/refs/heads/main/docs/reference/api/openapi.yaml

Closes #175

* Add Anthropic MCP Registry REST API v0 compatibility with JWT authentication

Implements full support for the Anthropic MCP Registry REST API v0 specification
to enable interoperability with Anthropic MCP client tools and ecosystem.

## New Features

### API Endpoints (registry/api/v0_routes.py)
- GET /v0/servers - List all MCP servers with cursor-based pagination
- GET /v0/servers/{serverName}/versions - List versions for a specific server
- GET /v0/servers/{serverName}/versions/{version} - Get server version details
- Full JWT Bearer token authentication support
- Permission-based server filtering (users see only accessible servers)

### Schema Support (registry/schemas/anthropic_schema.py)
- Complete Pydantic models matching Anthropic OpenAPI specification
- ServerList, ServerResponse, ServerDetail, Package, Transport models
- Support for _meta fields with proper field aliases
- Nested metadata structures for registry and internal info

### Data Transformation (registry/services/transform_service.py)
- Transform internal server format to Anthropic schema
- Server naming: /path -> io.mcpgateway/path
- Cursor-based pagination with configurable limits (default 100, max 1000)
- Health status and metadata integration
- Transport URL conversion for streamable-http protocol

### Authentication Integration
- nginx JWT validation via /validate endpoint
- New nginx_proxied_auth() dependency for header-based auth
- Reads X-User, X-Username, X-Scopes headers from nginx
- Falls back to session cookie auth for backward compatibility
- Supports both M2M tokens and user sessions

## Infrastructure Changes

### nginx Configuration (docker/nginx_rev_proxy_*.conf)
- Added auth_request /validate to /v0/ location blocks
- Fixed Authorization header forwarding ($http_authorization)
- Captures and forwards auth context headers to FastAPI
- Error handling for 401/403 with proper error pages

### Tests (tests/unit/)
- Unit tests for transform_service data conversion
- Unit tests for v0_routes endpoint logic
- Comprehensive test coverage for pagination and filtering

## Documentation

### Implementation Docs (docs/design/)
- anthropic-registry-api-v0-implementation.md - Full technical design
- anthropic-api-v0-test-commands.md - 20 comprehensive test scenarios
- Clear authentication setup with generate_creds.sh
- Common issues and troubleshooting guide

## Breaking Changes
- Renamed registry/models/ -> registry/schemas/ for clarity
- Removed UI service filtering from v0 API (uses MCP server scopes only)

## Configuration
- Added tests/reports/ to .gitignore (test artifacts)
- Updated build_and_run.sh for schema directory rename

## Related
- Issue #175: Support Anthropic MCP Registry REST API v0 for Interoperability
- OpenAPI Spec: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry

## Testing
All endpoints tested with JWT Bearer tokens from generate_creds.sh:
- Pagination works correctly with cursor-based navigation
- Permission filtering respects user scopes (unrestricted/restricted)
- Error handling returns proper status codes (401, 403, 404)
- Schema validation matches Anthropic specification

* Fix Anthropic v0 API implementation issues and add comprehensive testing

## Bug Fixes

### Route Path Parameters
- Added `:path` converter to handle `/` in server names
- Fixed 404 errors on `/v0/servers/{serverName}/versions` endpoints
- Server names like `io.mcpgateway/atlassian` now work correctly

### Trailing Slash Handling
- Fixed health data showing "unknown" status
- Try both with and without trailing slash when looking up servers
- Use actual path from server_info for health checks

### Permission Checks
- Fixed empty server lists for non-admin users
- Changed from `accessible_services` (UI scopes) to `accessible_servers` (MCP scopes)
- v0 API now correctly filters based on MCP server permissions

### nginx Configuration
- Fixed Authorization header forwarding in `/validate` endpoint
- Changed `$http_x_authorization` to `$http_authorization`
- Auth server now receives JWT tokens correctly

## Enhancements

### Constants Centralization
- Added `ANTHROPIC_SERVER_NAMESPACE` constant to registry/constants.py
- Replaced all hardcoded `"io.mcpgateway"` strings with constant
- Makes namespace configurable in one place

### Token Management
- Added `scripts/refresh_m2m_token.sh` for refreshing any M2M token
- Works with any client (bot-008, agent-finance-bot, etc.)
- Calculates expiration timestamps and provides usage instructions

### Documentation Updates
- Updated `docs/design/anthropic-api-v0-test-commands.md`:
  - Fixed token file path (ingress.json not bot-008-token.json)
  - Updated token expiration time (5 minutes)
  - Removed outdated limitation warnings
  - Fixed server name in examples (currenttime not current-time)
  - Added Test 21: Permission-based filtering with restricted bot
  - Sources KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD from .env (not hardcoded)
- Created new `docs/design/anthropic-v0-api-implementation.md`:
  - Accurate guide reflecting actual implementation
  - Complete authentication flow diagrams
  - All critical details (`:path`, trailing slash, constants)
  - Troubleshooting section with solutions
- Removed outdated `docs/design/anthropic-registry-api-v0-implementation.md`

## Files Modified

- `registry/api/v0_routes.py` - Route fixes, permission checks, trailing slash
- `registry/constants.py` - Added Anthropic API constants
- `registry/services/transform_service.py` - Use namespace constant
- `docs/design/anthropic-api-v0-test-commands.md` - Comprehensive updates
- `docs/design/anthropic-v0-api-implementation.md` - New accurate guide
- `scripts/refresh_m2m_token.sh` - New token refresh utility

## Testing

All changes tested with:
- Full access token (ingress.json) - sees all servers
- Restricted token (test-restricted-bot) - sees only 3 servers
- Permission-based filtering working correctly
- Health data showing proper status
- URL encoding working for server names with `/`

* Fix health checks and tool fetching for Cloudflare and streamable-http servers

This commit fixes multiple issues with health checks and automatic tool discovery:

1. Health Check - Proper MCP Session Management
   - Add proper MCP initialize flow to get session ID from server
   - Use server-generated session ID for subsequent ping requests
   - Skip URL pattern shortcut when supported_transports contains streamable-http
   - Handle auth failures during initialize by falling back to ping without auth

2. Tool Fetching - Header and URL Fixes
   - Add required Accept header: application/json, text/event-stream
   - Remove trailing slash from MCP URLs (Cloudflare rejects it)
   - Fix MCP client to properly handle Cloudflare's requirements

3. Tool Auto-Discovery - Enhanced Logic
   - Always fetch tools on first health check (previous_status == UNKNOWN)
   - Fetch tools when server transitions to healthy
   - Fetch tools if server is healthy but has empty tool_list
   - Ensures tools populate automatically on startup and registration

4. Import Script - Preserve Transport Type
   - Stop removing supported_transports field during import
   - Allows SSE servers to be registered with correct transport type
   - Fixes health checks for servers like ai.shawndurrani-mcp-merchant

* Fix Keycloak HTTPS enforcement by adding proxy address forwarding

Keycloak was enforcing HTTPS at the token endpoint even though KC_HTTP_ENABLED=true
and KC_PROXY=edge were configured. The issue was missing KC_PROXY_ADDRESS_FORWARDING
environment variable.

When Keycloak is behind an ALB:
- ALB forwards HTTP requests to Keycloak container internally
- ALB sets X-Forwarded-* headers to indicate the client protocol
- Without KC_PROXY_ADDRESS_FORWARDING, Keycloak ignores these headers
- Result: Keycloak only sees internal HTTP and defaults to HTTPS enforcement

With KC_PROXY_ADDRESS_FORWARDING=true:
- Keycloak trusts the proxy headers from the ALB
- Recognizes that clients are using HTTP (as per X-Forwarded-Proto)
- Allows HTTP connections to OAuth2 endpoints without redirect
- Enables the disable-ssl.sh script to obtain admin tokens

This fix allows the Keycloak SSL disabling script to work correctly.

* Fix Keycloak REST API parameters to use proper schema fields

Corrected the frontendUrl parameter from a top-level property to the
attributes object, which is the proper way to set it via the REST API
according to the RealmRepresentation schema.

* fix: Make build system region-agnostic using AWS_REGION environment variable

Problem:
The build-images.sh and generate-image-manifest.sh scripts were parsing
the ECR registry URL directly from build-config.yaml which had a hardcoded
us-west-2 region. This caused ECR authentication failures when deploying
to other regions even when AWS_REGION environment variable was set.

Error was:
  Error response from daemon: login attempt to
  https://605134468121.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/v2/ failed
  with status: 400 Bad Request

Root cause:
Line 50 in build-images.sh:
  ECR_REGISTRY=$(grep 'ecr_registry:' "$CONFIG_FILE" ...)
This parsed the hardcoded us-west-2 URL from build-config.yaml regardless
of the AWS_REGION environment variable.

Solution:
1. Updated scripts/build-images.sh:
   - Construct ECR_REGISTRY dynamically using AWS_REGION env var
   - Changed from parsing config to:
     ECR_REGISTRY="${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID}.dkr.ecr.${AWS_REGION}.amazonaws.com"
   - Defaults to us-west-2 if AWS_REGION not set

2. Updated scripts/generate-image-manifest.sh:
   - Same dynamic ECR registry construction
   - Now respects AWS_REGION environment variable
   - Outputs region being used for transparency

3. Updated build-config.yaml documentation:
   - Added comments explaining that region values are defaults
   - Documented that AWS_REGION env var overrides config
   - Included usage example for multi-region deployment

Usage:
  # Deploy to us-east-1
  export AWS_REGION=us-east-1
  make build-push

  # Deploy to eu-west-1
  export AWS_REGION=eu-west-1
  make build-push IMAGE=registry

  # Use default (us-west-2)
  make build-push

This allows the same codebase to deploy to any AWS region without
manually editing configuration files.

Changed account ID from real value (605134468121) to placeholder (123456789012)

This commit implements the complete backend switching architecture as
designed in the backend switching design document, enabling seamless
switching between file (FAISS) and OpenSearch backends via configuration.

## Core Changes

### Phase 1: Fix FAISS Repository Interface
- Fixed FaissSearchRepository.search() signature to match SearchRepositoryBase
- Changed from `search(query, top_k, entity_type, enabled_only)` to
  `search(query, entity_types, max_results)`
- Return type now Dict[str, List[Dict]] (grouped by entity type)
- Uses search_mixed() which already returns grouped results

### Phase 2: Refactor Main Startup
- Removed direct faiss_service import from registry/main.py
- Added repository factory pattern with get_search_repository()
- Updated lifespan() to use search_repo.initialize()
- Changed server/agent indexing to use search_repo methods
- Added dynamic backend logging (FAISS or OpenSearch)

### Phase 3: Refactor Server Service
- Removed direct faiss_service import from server_service.py
- Added self._search_repo in __init__ via factory
- Removed asyncio.create_task() wrapper for indexing
- Search indexing now synchronous part of update operation

### Phase 4: Refactor Search Routes
- Added dependency injection pattern to search_routes.py
- Created get_search_repo() dependency function
- Updated semantic_search endpoint to use injected repository
- Removed direct faiss_service import

### Phase 5: Fix OpenSearch Embeddings Client
- Updated OpenSearchSearchRepository to use embeddings abstraction
- Changed from hardcoded SentenceTransformer to create_embeddings_client()
- Now respects EMBEDDINGS_PROVIDER setting (sentence-transformers or litellm)
- Supports cloud providers: OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock, Cohere, etc.
- Fixed encode() calls to pass list and extract first element

### Phase 6: Refactor Security Scan Routes
- Updated agent_routes.py security scan to use repository pattern
- Updated server_routes.py security scan to use repository pattern
- Changed from faiss_service.add_or_update_* to search_repo.index_*
- Pass is_enabled=False for unsafe servers/agents

### Phase 7: Add CRUD Search Indexing
- Added indexing to server_service.register_server()
- Added de-indexing to server_service.remove_server()
- Added indexing to agent_service.register_agent()
- Added re-indexing to agent_service.update_agent()
- Added de-indexing to agent_service.delete_agent()
- All use best-effort pattern (log errors, don't fail operations)

## Benefits

- Backend selection now configuration-driven (STORAGE_BACKEND env var)
- Can switch between FAISS and OpenSearch without code changes
- Supports vendor-agnostic embeddings (local or cloud providers)
- Search index stays synchronized with entity CRUD operations
- Enables production deployment with scalable OpenSearch backend
- Maintains backward compatibility with file-based FAISS deployment

* Fix AOSS eventual consistency and multi-task cache synchronization

PROBLEM:
- AOSS has eventual consistency - documents not immediately queryable after write
- Multiple ECS tasks behind ALB have separate in-memory caches
- After creating/updating server, other tasks don't know about changes
- Results in inconsistent UI behavior (servers appear/disappear randomly)

ROOT CAUSE:
- create() indexed document without waiting for AOSS to make it queryable
- update(), set_state(), delete() only updated local cache of one task
- No cache reload mechanism after writes in AOSS mode

SOLUTION:
1. Added _wait_for_document_available() helper method:
   - Polls with exponential backoff until document is queryable
   - Max 5 retries with 0.5s initial delay

2. Updated all write operations for AOSS:
   - create(): Wait for document availability, then reload cache
   - update(): Reload cache after update
   - set_state(): Reload cache after toggle
   - delete(): Reload cache after deletion

3. Regular OpenSearch unchanged:
   - Still uses refresh=true for immediate consistency
   - Updates local cache directly without reload

IMPACT:
- Servers/agents now consistently visible across all ECS tasks
- Toggle operations work reliably
- Small latency increase for AOSS writes (0.5-5s depending on consistency)
- No impact on regular OpenSearch deployments

* Fix: Replace imagePullPolicy with resolveImageDigestEnabled for ECS

AWS ECS does not support imagePullPolicy parameter (that's Kubernetes-only).
Instead, ECS uses resolveImageDigestEnabled to control image pull behavior:

- resolveImageDigestEnabled=true (default): ECS resolves image tags to digests
  and caches them, causing all tasks to use the same image version
- resolveImageDigestEnabled=false: ECS uses the actual tag and pulls fresh
  images on each deployment, achieving the same effect as imagePullPolicy=always

This change ensures ECS will always pull the :latest tag from ECR instead of
caching the image digest.

* Fix ECS version consistency parameter - use versionConsistency instead of resolveImageDigestEnabled

* Fix multi-stage build to only copy necessary files

The previous version copied the entire /app directory (3.16GB) from
the backend-builder stage, which included:
- .git directory
- Build artifacts
- Test files
- Documentation
- All source code (even unused parts)

This fix copies only the necessary runtime files:
- registry/ (main application)
- auth_server/ (authentication)
- api/ (API layer)
- config/ (configuration files including scopes.yml)
- docker/ (nginx configs and entrypoint)
- pyproject.toml (for package metadata)

This should reduce the final image size significantly.

This reduces Docker build context from ~1.77GB to under 500MB for faster builds.

- Reduces mcpgw image from ~7.78GB to ~1.5GB

Improve semantic search with hybrid keyword matching and agent tool discovery (#352)

* Fix tool matching in search to use tokenized keywords

The search API was not finding matching tools when queries contained
multiple words (e.g., "get current time by timezone") because both
DocumentDB and MongoDB CE backends were matching the full query string
as a regex/substring instead of tokenizing it.

Changes:
- Add _tokenize_query() helper to split queries into keywords
- Add _tokens_match_text() helper to check if any token matches text
- Update _client_side_search() to use tokenized matching for tools
- Update hybrid search pipeline to use token-based regex (token1|token2)
- Apply same stopword filtering as FAISS implementation

Now queries like "get current time by timezone" will match tools with
names like "get_current_time" because tokens "current", "time", and
"timezone" are matched individually.

* Populate top-level tools array from matching_tools in search results

The search API was returning matching tools inside server.matching_tools
but the top-level tools[] array was empty. This caused total_tools to
show 0 even when tools were found.

Now matching tools from servers are also added to the top-level tools
array, making them available for direct iteration by clients.

* Include tool inputSchema in search results

Previously, tool schemas were not included in search results, requiring
a separate get_server_info() call to retrieve the inputSchema for each
matching tool. This added extra latency to tool discovery.

Changes:
- Store inputSchema when indexing tools in the search collection
- Return inputSchema in matching_tools from DocumentDB hybrid search
- Return inputSchema in matching_tools from MongoDB CE client-side search
- Include inputSchema in top-level tools array

Now clients can get the full tool schema from the first search response
without needing additional API calls.

* Support both inputSchema and schema field names for tool schemas

* Change token generation to use Keycloak M2M client credentials

Replace self-signed HS256 JWT tokens with Keycloak M2M tokens for the
"Get JWT Token" UI button. This ensures generated tokens are validated
the same way as other Keycloak tokens in the system.

Changes:
- auth_server/server.py: Use auth_provider.get_m2m_token() instead of
  self-signed JWT generation
- ecs-services.tf: Add KEYCLOAK_M2M_CLIENT_ID env var and

- test_server.py: Update tests to mock Keycloak provider

* Add inputSchema to tool objects in search results

Include the tool's inputSchema in the tools array when returning search
results, making the schema available to clients discovering tools.

* Refactor agent to use registry tool discovery

Rewrite agent to discover and invoke MCP tools using semantic search on
the registry. This removes Cognito authentication in favor of JWT tokens
and adds a modular registry client for tool discovery.

Changes:
- agent.py: Simplified agent with search_registry_tools and invoke_mcp_tool
- system_prompt.txt: Updated prompt for tool discovery workflow

supports session cookies. This made it inconsistent with other API
endpoints like /api/servers that use nginx_proxied_auth.

the /api/auth/me endpoint for user info.

fix: Extract full server path for peer registry MCP logging

segments: peer-name/server-name/endpoint (e.g., peer-registry-lob-1/
cloudflare-docs/mcp).

Previously, only the first segment was captured as the server name,
losing the actual MCP server identifier. Now the code correctly joins
all path segments before the MCP endpoint (mcp, sse, messages) to
capture the full server path.

This ensures audit logs show the complete server identifier for
proper tracking and compliance.

parameters (log_dir, rotation_hours, etc.) are still accepted for
backward compatibility but are ignored.

Updated tests to validate MongoDB-only behavior.

fix: Prevent SQL injection in metrics-service retention subsystem

- Add 13 regression tests for SQL injection prevention

Attack vectors blocked:
- PUT /admin/retention/policies/{table_name}
- GET /admin/retention/preview?table_name=...
- POST /admin/retention/cleanup?table_name=...

All 32 retention tests pass.

feat: Add OAUTH_STORE_TOKENS_IN_SESSION env var to prevent cookie size issues

OAuth session cookies can exceed the browser's 4096-byte limit when storing
JWT access and refresh tokens from identity providers like Microsoft Entra ID.

This adds an environment variable to optionally disable storing OAuth tokens
in the session cookie:
- Default: true (backward compatible - tokens stored)
- For Entra ID: Set to false to avoid cookie size errors

The tokens stored in the session were never actually used by any code,
so disabling storage has no functional impact.

fix: Allow admins to toggle skills without explicit UI permission

Admins should be able to enable/disable skills by default, similar to
how other resource toggles work. The toggle now shows if user is admin
OR has the toggle_skill permission.

fix: Allow admins to toggle servers and agents without explicit UI permission

Consistent with the skill toggle fix - admins should be able to enable/disable
servers and agents by default without needing toggle_service or toggle_agent
UI permissions configured.

fix: Always render dashboard sections when feature is enabled

Previously, dashboard sections (servers, agents, skills) would be hidden
entirely when filtered results were empty. This caused the page to appear
empty when users toggled items with filters active (e.g., disabling a
skill while viewing "enabled" filter in skills-only mode).

Now sections always render when their feature is enabled, and each section
handles its own empty state with appropriate messaging. This ensures users
see "No items found" within the section rather than a completely empty page.

Removes the redundant global empty state since each section now handles
its own empty state internally.

fix: Allow admins to refresh health status on servers and agents

Added admin override to canHealthCheck prop for both ServerCard and
AgentCard components. This ensures administrators can always use the
health check refresh button regardless of explicit UI permissions.

Consistent with the existing pattern used for canToggle and canDelete.

fix: Send skill toggle as JSON body instead of query parameter

The skill toggle API endpoint expects a ToggleStateRequest JSON body,
not a query parameter. This was causing the toggle to fail with a 422
error.

Changed from: POST /api/skills/{path}/toggle?enabled=true
Changed to:   POST /api/skills/{path}/toggle with { enabled: true }

fix: Correct path mismatch in skill toggle causing UI not to update

The SkillCard was passing the API path (/pdf) to onToggle, but
Dashboard was trying to match against skill.path (/skills/pdf).
This caused the state update to fail silently, so the UI didn't
reflect the toggle even though the API call succeeded.

Changes:
- SkillCard now passes skill.path (full path) to onToggle for state matching
- Dashboard converts the path to API format only when making the API call

This ensures the optimistic UI update works correctly.

fix: Include disabled skills in API requests

The skills API has include_disabled=false by default, which was hiding
disabled skills from the UI. Now both useSkills and useServerStats
request all skills including disabled ones so users can see and
re-enable them.

fix: Set DOCUMENTDB_USE_TLS=false in pytest_configure

module imports) because client.py imports settings at module level.
Setting it in test_settings fixture is too late.

This ensures the DocumentDB client sees documentdb_use_tls=False
from the very first Settings() creation.

fix: strip newlines from X-Body header to prevent scope validation bypass

Multi-line (pretty-printed) JSON request bodies break scope validation
for non-admin users with fine-grained scopes. The capture_body.lua script
sets the raw POST body as an X-Body HTTP header, but newline characters
corrupt the header. The auth server cannot parse the body, falls back to
URL-path-based method validation, and denies access.

Strip \r\n from the body before setting the header value. JSON whitespace
is insignificant per RFC 8259, so this is safe.

Based on the fix identified by @WPrintz in #487, adapted for the current
Lua file architecture.

fix: normalize leading slashes in scope server name matching

The scopes UI stores server names with a leading slash (e.g.
'/cloudflare-docs') while the URL extraction in /validate strips it
(e.g. 'cloudflare-docs'). _normalize_server_name only stripped trailing
slashes, causing all non-wildcard scope checks to fail for servers
added through the IAM Groups UI.

Change rstrip("/") to strip("/") so both leading and trailing slashes
are removed before comparison.

feat: observability pipeline with AMP, Grafana, and metrics-service for ECS (#544)

* feat: add nginx Lua metrics pipeline (emit_metrics + flush_metrics)

Add an optional metrics collection pipeline at the nginx reverse proxy layer:

- emit_metrics.lua (log_by_lua phase): captures MCP request metrics
  (server_name, method, tool_name, client_name, success, latency) from each
  proxied request and writes compact JSON entries to a lua_shared_dict buffer.
  Uses upstream_header_time for latency to avoid SSE connection duration
  inflation. Reads request body from ngx.ctx (survives auth_request subrequest
  phase boundary).

- flush_metrics.lua (init_worker_by_lua phase): background timer on worker 0
  drains the shared dict buffer every 5s and batch-POSTs metrics to a
  configurable collector endpoint via raw TCP cosocket (no external Lua
  dependencies). Disabled by default -- only starts if METRICS_COLLECTOR_URL
  is set. Gracefully handles unreachable collectors (log + retry next cycle,
  entries expire after 300s TTL).

- log_by_lua_file directive added to all 3 transport blocks in nginx_service.py
  (sse, streamable-http, direct)

- init_worker_by_lua_file directive added to both nginx conf templates

Environment variables:
  METRICS_COLLECTOR_URL - push target (e.g. http://metrics-service:8890).
                          If unset, metrics collection is fully disabled.
  METRICS_API_KEY       - sent as X-API-Key header on each POST to collector.

Ref: upstream issue #475

* fix: metrics-service OTel pipeline correctness and Grafana dashboard accuracy

AMP/Grafana observability pipeline when metrics-service runs on ECS Fargate:

* feat: add full observability pipeline to Terraform ECS deployment

Adds end-to-end metrics collection, storage, and visualization to the
Terraform ECS deployment via a new enable_observability variable (default
true) that gates all observability resources using count.

New infrastructure (observability.tf):

  Amazon Managed Prometheus (AMP):
  - aws_prometheus_workspace for time-series storage
  - Endpoints computed in locals for ADOT remote-write and Grafana query

  metrics-service ECS Service (256 CPU / 512 MB):
  - Receives metrics via POST /metrics on port 8890 (Service Connect)
  - Exposes Prometheus /metrics endpoint on port 9465 for ADOT scraping
  - SQLite storage at /tmp/metrics.db (ephemeral Fargate storage)
  - API key auth from Secrets Manager (shared key for auth-server + registry)
  - Security group allows port 8890 from auth-server and registry SGs,
    port 9465 from VPC CIDR for ADOT collector scraping

  ADOT Collector ECS Service (256 CPU / 512 MB):
  - Scrapes metrics-service:9465 every 15s via Prometheus receiver
  - Remote-writes to AMP via prometheusremotewrite exporter with SigV4
  - Config embedded via yamlencode() in AOT_CONFIG_CONTENT env var

fix: resolve ECS Service Connect dual-stack DNS failures in registry entrypoint (#548)

* fix: resolve IPv6 Service Connect issue for Lua metrics flush

ECS Service Connect assigns IPv6 virtual IPs (2600:f0f0::) alongside
IPv4 (127.255.0.x).  The nginx Lua cosocket in flush_metrics.lua
resolves hostnames via the system resolver, which returns IPv6 first,
causing "Network is unreachable" errors that silently break the
metrics pipeline.

Two fixes in registry-entrypoint.sh:

1. Pin metrics-service hostname to its IPv4 Service Connect VIP in
   /etc/hosts before nginx starts.  Skips pinning when the URL
   already contains a literal IP address.

2. Raise main-context error_log from default 'error' to 'warn' so
   Lua init_worker and timer callback messages (startup confirmation,
   connection failures) are no longer suppressed.

* fix: add FQDN aliases for Service Connect health checker resolution

Service Connect only registers short hostnames (e.g., "auth-server") in
/etc/hosts, but MCP servers may be registered with Cloud Map FQDNs
(e.g., "auth-server.mcp-gateway.local").  The Python health checker in
service.py resolves proxy_pass_url hostnames via system DNS, which only
finds /etc/hosts entries -- causing all internal servers to be marked
unhealthy and their nginx location blocks commented out (405 errors).

Fix: In registry-entrypoint.sh, when SERVICE_CONNECT_NAMESPACE is set,
augment /etc/hosts with FQDN aliases for all Service Connect entries
(127.255.0.x lines).  This makes both short names and FQDNs resolve
to the IPv4 Service Connect VIP.

The SERVICE_CONNECT_NAMESPACE env var is added to the registry container
in ecs-services.tf, referencing the Cloud Map namespace name.  The fix
is gated on this env var, so Docker Compose and Kubernetes deployments
are unaffected.

fix: handle TTL index options conflict in mongodb-init

When the audit_log TTL value changes between runs (e.g., from 365 days
to 7 days), MongoDB rejects creating an index with the same name but
different expireAfterSeconds. This fix catches the IndexOptionsConflict
error, drops the old index, and recreates it with the new TTL value.

fix: ensure audit log timestamps include UTC timezone in API responses

Motor (async MongoDB driver) returns naive datetime objects without
timezone info. This caused API responses to serialize timestamps as
"2026-02-26T22:32:21.006000" without +00:00, making the frontend
treat them as local time instead of UTC. Re-attach timezone.utc to
naive datetimes in find() and find_one() so they serialize correctly.

fix(iam): tool selector, path normalization, and UI permission sync in IAM Groups (#570)

* fix(iam): bypass scope filtering for admin users in tool catalog endpoint

The /api/tool-catalog endpoint always applied scope filtering, even for
admin users, while /api/servers correctly bypassed it for admins. This
caused the IAM Groups tool selector to show "No matches found" because
the admin token's empty scopes list filtered out servers with
required_scopes set.

* fix(iam): normalize path comparison in tool catalog for slash-insensitive matching

The IAM group server_access entries may store server paths without
leading/trailing slashes (e.g., "mcpgw") while the DB stores them
with slashes ("/mcpgw/"). The exact path match in the tool catalog
service caused the tool selector to return zero results.

* fix(iam): auto-sync UI permissions and normalize server paths in IAM Groups

Three changes to the IAM Groups form:

1. Always sync UI permissions (list_service, health_check_service,
   get_service, list_tools, call_tool) with current server_access
   entries instead of only populating when empty. Previously, adding a
   new server to server_access didn't update UI permissions, so the
   server was invisible to the user after login.

2. Normalize server paths by stripping leading/trailing slashes in
   server_access payload and UI permissions. The server dropdown
   returns paths with slashes (/cloudflare-docs/) but existing entries
   store bare names (mcpgw). Inconsistent formats caused access control
   mismatches.

3. Apply same fixes to both _buildScopeJson (JSON preview) and
   handleUpdate (save payload) for consistency.

* fix: preserve trailing slashes in endpoint URLs for servers that require them

Fixed health check failures for servers like Hydrata that require trailing
slashes in their endpoint URLs (https://hydrata.com/mcp/).

The bug was in get_endpoint_url() which was stripping trailing slashes from
all URLs. When POSTing to https://hydrata.com/mcp (no slash), the server
redirected with 301 to https://hydrata.com/mcp/ (with slash). HTTP clients
change POST to GET on 301 redirects, causing 405 Method Not Allowed errors.

Changes:
1. Only strip trailing slash if URL doesn't already contain transport path
2. Preserve trailing slashes in explicit mcp_endpoint/sse_endpoint
3. Return URLs exactly as configured when they contain /mcp/ or /sse/

This allows servers to specify their required URL format while maintaining
backward compatibility for servers that don't need trailing slashes.

Fixes health check failures for Hydrata and similar servers.

* fix: resolve CORS error on logout by using full-page redirect

Problem:
- Frontend was using axios.post() for logout, which is an XHR request
- XHR requests cannot follow cross-origin redirects due to CORS policy
- This caused "No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header" error when
  redirecting to Entra ID logout endpoint

Solution:
- Changed logout to use window.location.href for full-page navigation
- Browser can now follow the complete redirect chain:
  Registry → Auth-server → IdP (Entra/Keycloak) → Registry
- No CORS issues with full-page navigation

Technical Details:
- Backend already supports both GET and POST for /api/auth/logout
- User state is cleared immediately for responsive UI
- Full logout flow now works correctly with SSO providers

Fixes: #490

* refactor: always store id_token for OIDC logout compliance

Changes:
- Store id_token unconditionally in session (not dependent on OAUTH_STORE_TOKENS_IN_SESSION flag)
- This ensures logout always works properly with Keycloak, Entra ID, and other OIDC providers

Rationale:
- id_token is NOT a credential - it contains only identity information (username, email, roles)
- id_token CANNOT be used to access APIs (that's access_token's job)
- id_token CANNOT get new tokens (that's refresh_token's job)
- id_token is REQUIRED for proper OIDC logout via id_token_hint parameter
- OAUTH_STORE_TOKENS_IN_SESSION flag was intended for access_token/refresh_token (actual credentials)

Security:
- This change has ZERO security impact
- access_token and refresh_token are never stored (removed in previous commit)
- id_token is already in httponly, secure, samesite cookie
- id_token is designed by OIDC spec to be passed in logout URLs

Benefits:
- Logout works out-of-the-box with all OIDC providers
- No configuration flag needed for basic OIDC compliance
- Users don't need to enable a flag that sounds like it stores credentials

Optimize MCP server Dockerfiles to eliminate 100+ second chown operations:

PROBLEM:
- Creating .venv as root, then chown -R on thousands of files was very slow
- Example: "RUN chown -R appuser:appuser /app/.venv" took 116.7s

SOLUTION:
- Create appuser EARLY (before any app files)
- Install uv as root (global tool)
- Switch to appuser BEFORE creating .venv
- All package installations happen as appuser
- Use COPY --chown for files
- No expensive chown -R needed at all

OPTIMIZATION RESULTS:
- Eliminates 100+ second chown operation entirely
- Venv files created with correct ownership from the start
- Build time reduced significantly

FILES OPTIMIZED:
- docker/Dockerfile.mcp-server (generic MCP servers)
- docker/Dockerfile.mcp-server-cpu (CPU-only PyTorch servers)
- docker/Dockerfile.mcp-server-light (lightweight servers)

Pattern:
1. RUN groupadd/useradd (early)
2. RUN pip install uv (as root)
3. USER appuser
4. RUN uv venv .venv (as appuser - correct ownership)
5. USER root (for COPY operations)
6. COPY --chown=appuser:appuser (files owned correctly)
7. USER appuser (for pip installs)
8. RUN uv pip install (as appuser)
9. Final USER appuser (for runtime)

This follows Docker best practices and significantly speeds up builds.

Solution: Set UV_NO_CACHE=1 environment variable to disable caching entirely.
This matches our existing PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1 setting and is appropriate for
Docker image builds where caching isn't needed.

- Nginx proxy routes: Added Okta OAuth2 callback and login endpoints
- All docker-compose variants: Updated with OKTA_AUTH_SERVER_ID configuration

This change enables true database-driven authorization where M2M client groups are stored and queried from DocumentDB rather than being embedded in IdP tokens or hardcoded in authorization expressions.

* feat(terraform): add Okta IdP support to AWS ECS deployment

Adds complete Okta configuration support to the Terraform AWS ECS module, enabling deployment with Okta as the identity provider alongside existing Keycloak and Entra ID support.

Key changes:
- Module variables: Added 8 Okta-specific variables (domain, client IDs/secrets, API token, auth server ID)
- ECS services: Added Okta environment variables to both auth-server and registry task definitions
- Secrets Manager: Created 3 new secrets for Okta (client secret, M2M secret, API token)
- IAM policies: Updated task execution role to access Okta secrets
- tfvars.example: Added comprehensive Okta configuration section with documentation

Provider-specific tfvars templates:
- Created terraform.tfvars.keycloak (working config for Keycloak deployments)
- Created terraform.tfvars.entra (working config for Entra ID deployments)
- Created terraform.tfvars.okta (working config for Okta deployments)
- Updated .gitignore to document these files (already ignored by *.tfvars pattern)
- Users can copy these to terraform.tfvars to switch between IdP backends

This enables infrastructure-as-code deployment of the Okta IdP integration including M2M authorization, groups enrichment, and IAM management operations.

* feat(terraform): add Okta variables to Terraform configuration

Added all 8 Okta variables to variables.tf and main.tf to properly pass Okta configuration to the infrastructure module. This completes the Terraform support for Okta IdP deployment.

Changes:
- Added okta_enabled, okta_domain, okta_client_id, okta_client_secret
- Added okta_m2m_client_id, okta_m2m_client_secret, okta_api_token
- Added okta_auth_server_id for custom authorization server support
- All variables passed to module in main.tf

This allows users to deploy with Okta by setting okta_enabled=true in terraform.tfvars.

* fix(terraform): add Okta check to AUTH_PROVIDER logic

Fixed AUTH_PROVIDER environment variable to properly detect Okta configuration.
Previously, the logic only checked entra_enabled and keycloak_domain, causing
Okta deployments to incorrectly use Keycloak as the auth provider.

Updated logic (for both registry and auth-server):
  AUTH_PROVIDER = okta_enabled ? "okta" : (entra_enabled ? "entra" : (keycloak_domain != "" ? "keycloak" : "default"))

This ensures that when okta_enabled=true in terraform.tfvars, the containers will
receive AUTH_PROVIDER="okta" environment variable, matching the behavior of docker-compose.

* docs(terraform): clarify only one auth provider should be enabled

Added clear documentation to terraform.tfvars.example explaining:
- Only ONE authentication provider should be enabled at a time
- Three available options: Keycloak (default), Entra, or Okta
- Priority order if multiple are enabled: okta_enabled > entra_enabled > keycloak

This prevents confusion when users are configuring authentication and helps them understand that enabling multiple providers simultaneously is not the intended configuration.

fix: make Nginx DNS resolver configurable via environment variable (#683)

The Nginx config generated by nginx_service.py hardcodes the DNS
resolver to 8.8.8.8 8.8.4.4. This breaks proxy_pass to backend MCP
servers registered with cluster-internal hostnames (e.g.,
*.svc.cluster.local) in Kubernetes environments, since Google's
public DNS cannot resolve cluster-local names.

Add two new environment variables:
- NGINX_DNS_RESOLVER: override the resolver addresses
  (default: '8.8.8.8 8.8.4.4', preserving existing behavior)
- NGINX_DNS_RESOLVER_TIMEOUT: override the resolver timeout in seconds
  (default: '5')

Example for Kubernetes (using kube-dns):
  NGINX_DNS_RESOLVER=10.96.0.10

Also adds the missing 'import os' — the module already used
os.environ in multiple places but relied on it being imported
by other modules at runtime.

Fixes backend proxy 502 errors when MCP servers are registered
with cluster-internal URLs.

PR #624 applied cap_drop: ALL to all services for CIS Docker Benchmark

uses gosu to switch from root to the mongodb user at startup, which
requires SETUID and SETGID. Without them the container fails with:

Add Auth0 provider support to MCP Gateway Registry (#708)

* Add Auth0 identity provider support

Implement Auth0 as a new authentication provider alongside Cognito,
Keycloak, Entra ID, GitHub, and Google. Auth0 uses standard OIDC with
Auth0-specific conventions: domain-based endpoints, custom namespaced
claims for groups (configurable via AUTH0_GROUPS_CLAIM), audience
parameter for API tokens, and returnTo logout redirect.

Includes provider implementation, factory integration, OAuth2 callback
handling, YAML config, env template, test fixtures, and 36 unit tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Refactor Auth0 token handling and improve error reporting

- Delegate ID token parsing to the Auth0Provider, enhancing the extraction of user information and group memberships.
- Update error handling in Auth0Provider to include exception chaining for better debugging.
- Introduce a new method, extract_user_from_tokens, to encapsulate the logic for extracting user data from Auth0 token responses, ensuring proper validation of issuer and audience claims.

fix: decouple is_admin from server wildcard access (#663) (#717)

The user_has_wildcard_access() function checked for server: '*' in scopes
and used that result as is_admin, making it impossible to create consumer
roles with wildcard server access without granting admin privileges.

Replace is_admin determination with _user_is_admin() that checks for
mutating UI-Scopes actions (register_, modify_, toggle_, delete_,
publish_, create_) with 'all' resources. Read-only actions (list_,
get_, health_check_) do not grant admin status.

This allows consumer roles to use server: '*' for discovering all
MCP servers without gaining unintended admin privileges (audit log
access, agent deletion, peer management, admin UI badge).

Existing admin roles are unaffected since they already have mutating
UI-Scopes like register_service: [all] and modify_service: [all].

Closes #663

Fix edit server blank page, add metadata to search and skill UI (#746)

* fix: edit server modal navigates to blank page on save

The POST /edit/{path} endpoint returned a 303 RedirectResponse to "/".
When called from the React SPA via axios, the browser followed the
redirect and replaced the page with raw HTML, causing a blank screen.

Backend: return JSON when the request Accept header includes
application/json, keeping the redirect for traditional form submissions.

Frontend: send Accept: application/json header instead of overriding
Content-Type, so FormData is sent correctly and the response is JSON.

* feat: add metadata parameter to internal register endpoint

For completeness, the POST /api/internal/register endpoint now accepts
an optional metadata field (JSON string), matching the external
register and session-based register endpoints.

* fix: edit server CSRF validation and form encoding

Two issues caused the blank page on save:

1. CSRF: The edit endpoint used verify_csrf_token (form-data only) but
   the React SPA sends CSRF via X-CSRF-Token header. Switched to
   verify_csrf_token_flexible which accepts both sources.

2. Form encoding: Used URLSearchParams instead of FormData so the
   Content-Type is correctly application/x-www-form-urlencoded (FormData
   sends multipart/form-data which FastAPI Form() parameters don't
   expect). Also removed browser-noop maxRedirects option.

* fix: include metadata in search embeddings and re-index on edit

1. DocumentDB search_repository.index_server now includes custom
   metadata key-value pairs in the embedding text, so semantic search
   can find servers by metadata like team, owner, environment.

   update DocumentDB embeddings after changes, keeping the search
   index in sync with edits.

feat: add direct M2M client registration API (#851) (#866)

* feat: add direct M2M client registration API (#851)

Add admin endpoints at /api/iam/m2m-clients that let operators register
M2M client_ids and their group mappings by writing directly to the
idp_m2m_clients collection, without requiring an IdP Admin API token
(e.g., OKTA_API_TOKEN).

Endpoints:
- POST   /api/iam/m2m-clients         (admin, 201/409)
- GET    /api/iam/m2m-clients         (auth, paginated)
- GET    /api/iam/m2m-clients/{id}    (auth, 404)
- PATCH  /api/iam/m2m-clients/{id}    (admin, 403 for IdP-synced records)
- DELETE /api/iam/m2m-clients/{id}    (admin, 403 for IdP-synced records)

Key design points:
- Records created via this API are tagged with provider="manual" and
  cannot collide with IdP sync (unique index on client_id; mutations
  only allowed on manual records).
- Auth reuses nginx_proxied_auth + is_admin permission check.
- Mutations emit audit log entries via set_audit_action.
- Feature flag M2M_DIRECT_REGISTRATION_ENABLED (default true) controls
  whether the router and startup index creation run.
- Prometheus counter m2m_management_requests_total{operation, outcome}
  for dashboarding and abuse detection.

Tests: 22 service + 21 router unit tests; full unit suite still green.

feat(auth): fall through to JWT validation when static token does not match (#871) (#875)

* feat(auth): fall through to JWT validation when static token does not match (#871)

Treat REGISTRY_STATIC_TOKEN_AUTH_ENABLED as an ADDITIONAL accepted
credential on registry API paths, not an exclusive gate. Before this
change the static-token block at /validate terminated with 401/403 on
missing or mismatched bearer, which blocked valid Okta JWTs and UI-issued
self-signed JWTs whenever static-token mode was on.

Changes:
- Extract _check_registry_static_token(bearer) -> dict | None helper so
  the match decision lives in one place. Future #779 (multi-key static
  tokens) will replace the helper body with a map lookup without
  touching the /validate caller.
- Change the static-token block to call the helper, return on match,
  fall through on miss / missing-auth / non-Bearer scheme.
- Update / rename three stale tests:
    test_network_trusted_requires_auth_header
    test_network_trusted_invalid_api_token
    test_network_trusted_rejects_non_bearer_scheme
    test_network_trusted_rejects_empty_bearer_token
  to reflect fall-through semantics rather than terminal rejection.
- Add TestCheckRegistryStaticToken unit tests for the new helper.
- Add TestStaticTokenFallthrough tests proving JWT callers succeed when
  static-token mode is on, and mismatched bearers no longer yield the
  old 403 "Invalid API token" response.

Behavior change (documented in release notes): a bearer that matches
neither the static token nor any valid JWT previously returned
403 "Invalid API token" from the static-token block; it now falls
through to the JWT block which returns its own error (typically 401).

Full auth_server suite: 161 passed. Full unit suite: 2081 passed,
11 skipped. ruff + bandit clean.

* feat(auth): add multi-key static tokens with per-key groups (#779)

Replace the single REGISTRY_API_TOKEN with a REGISTRY_API_KEYS JSON array
where each key carries its own name, secret, and group list. Groups resolve
to scopes through the standard group_mappings pipeline so each key gets
exactly the privileges its groups grant.

Auth server changes:
- _RegistryApiKeyEntry Pydantic model with min_length=32 key validation
- _parse_registry_api_keys() parser with reserved-name and uniqueness checks
- _build_static_token_map() async startup builder that resolves scopes via
  map_groups_to_scopes() and merges legacy REGISTRY_API_TOKEN as "legacy" entry
- _check_registry_static_token() iterates all entries with hmac.compare_digest,
  no early return for timing safety
- Legacy entry carries mcp-registry-admin scope for backward-compatible admin

Registry side:
- Removed hard-coded is_admin=True branch for network-trusted auth method
- network-trusted now flows through standard scope resolution like all other
  auth methods, getting admin only when scopes include mcp-registry-admin

Config plumbing: .env.example, Terraform (sensitive variable), Helm
(existingSecret pattern for External Secrets Operator).

Tests: 34 new tests covering parser, builder, multi-key matching, legacy

feat(gate): add registration gate admission control webhook (#809) (#881)

* feat(gate): add registration gate admission control webhook (#809)

Add a registration gate (admission control) that calls an external
endpoint before persisting registration or update requests for servers,
agents, and skills. The gate can approve (200) or deny (403) requests
with custom error messages.

Key behaviors:
- Fail-closed design: registration is blocked if the gate is unreachable
  after configurable retries with exponential backoff
- Credential sanitization: auth_credential, tokens, passwords, and
  api_key fields are stripped from the payload sent to the gate
- Three auth modes: none, api_key, bearer
- Startup connectivity check (non-blocking)
- Config API exposure for UI visibility

Deployment surfaces wired for Docker Compose, Terraform/ECS, and
Helm/EKS. 51 unit tests at 89% service coverage.

* docs(gate): add registration gate config screenshot to docs

* feat(gate): add gate check to server edit endpoint and fix test config

Wire the registration gate into POST /edit/{path} (server update via UI)
so that server updates from the web interface are also subject to
admission control. Update docs to list the new covered endpoint.

Disable the gate by default in test conftest to prevent fail-closed
behavior from interfering with existing tests that do not mock the gate.

* fix(server): accept status field in server edit endpoint

The edit_server_submit endpoint was missing the status form parameter,
so Lifecycle Status changes from the UI were silently ignored. Add the
service_status parameter and persist it in updated_server_entry.

feat: add direct M2M client registration API (#851) (#866)

* feat: add direct M2M client registration API (#851)

Add admin endpoints at /api/iam/m2m-clients that let operators register
M2M client_ids and their group mappings by writing directly to the
idp_m2m_clients collection, without requiring an IdP Admin API token
(e.g., OKTA_API_TOKEN).

Endpoints:
- POST   /api/iam/m2m-clients         (admin, 201/409)
- GET    /api/iam/m2m-clients         (auth, paginated)
- GET    /api/iam/m2m-clients/{id}    (auth, 404)
- PATCH  /api/iam/m2m-clients/{id}    (admin, 403 for IdP-synced records)
- DELETE /api/iam/m2m-clients/{id}    (admin, 403 for IdP-synced records)

Key design points:
- Records created via this API are tagged with provider="manual" and
  cannot collide with IdP sync (unique index on client_id; mutations
  only allowed on manual records).
- Auth reuses nginx_proxied_auth + is_admin permission check.
- Mutations emit audit log entries via set_audit_action.
- Feature flag M2M_DIRECT_REGISTRATION_ENABLED (default true) controls
  whether the router and startup index creation run.
- Prometheus counter m2m_management_requests_total{operation, outcome}
  for dashboarding and abuse detection.

Tests: 22 service + 21 router unit tests; full unit suite still green.

feat(auth): fall through to JWT validation when static token does not match (#871) (#875)

* feat(auth): fall through to JWT validation when static token does not match (#871)

Treat REGISTRY_STATIC_TOKEN_AUTH_ENABLED as an ADDITIONAL accepted
credential on registry API paths, not an exclusive gate. Before this
change the static-token block at /validate terminated with 401/403 on
missing or mismatched bearer, which blocked valid Okta JWTs and UI-issued
self-signed JWTs whenever static-token mode was on.

Changes:
- Extract _check_registry_static_token(bearer) -> dict | None helper so
  the match decision lives in one place. Future #779 (multi-key static
  tokens) will replace the helper body with a map lookup without
  touching the /validate caller.
- Change the static-token block to call the helper, return on match,
  fall through on miss / missing-auth / non-Bearer scheme.
- Update / rename three stale tests:
    test_network_trusted_requires_auth_header
    test_network_trusted_invalid_api_token
    test_network_trusted_rejects_non_bearer_scheme
    test_network_trusted_rejects_empty_bearer_token
  to reflect fall-through semantics rather than terminal rejection.
- Add TestCheckRegistryStaticToken unit tests for the new helper.
- Add TestStaticTokenFallthrough tests proving JWT callers succeed when
  static-token mode is on, and mismatched bearers no longer yield the
  old 403 "Invalid API token" response.

Behavior change (documented in release notes): a bearer that matches
neither the static token nor any valid JWT previously returned
403 "Invalid API token" from the static-token block; it now falls
through to the JWT block which returns its own error (typically 401).

feat(gate): add registration gate admission control webhook (#809) (#881)

* feat(gate): add registration gate admission control webhook (#809)

Add a registration gate (admission control) that calls an external
endpoint before persisting registration or update requests for servers,
agents, and skills. The gate can approve (200) or deny (403) requests
with custom error messages.

Key behaviors:
- Fail-closed design: registration is blocked if the gate is unreachable
  after configurable retries with exponential backoff
- Credential sanitization: auth_credential, tokens, passwords, and
  api_key fields are stripped from the payload sent to the gate
- Three auth modes: none, api_key, bearer
- Startup connectivity check (non-blocking)
- Config API exposure for UI visibility

Deployment surfaces wired for Docker Compose, Terraform/ECS, and
Helm/EKS. 51 unit tests at 89% service coverage.

fix: skip CSRF validation for Bearer token clients on toggle endpoints (#894)

Resolves #891

CSRF protection in verify_csrf_token_flexible blocked OAuth M2M Bearer
token clients from calling agent and skill toggle endpoints because the
validation requires a session cookie that non-browser clients do not have.

Move the session cookie check to the top of verify_csrf_token_flexible
and return early when no session cookie is present. CSRF attacks require
a browser session with cookies, so requests without a session cookie are
not vulnerable. Browser/SPA sessions retain full CSRF enforcement.

Also add the CSRF dependency to the virtual server toggle endpoint for
consistency across all user-facing toggle endpoints.

fix(auth): include ROOT_PATH in OAuth2 redirect URIs (#926)

* fix(auth): include ROOT_PATH in OAuth2 login and logout redirect URIs (#500)

When deployed with path-based routing (routingMode=path), the registry
builds redirect URIs from the host header but omits the ROOT_PATH
prefix. Keycloak rejects these as invalid_redirect_uri.

Extract a _build_external_url() helper that centralizes scheme
detection, localhost handling, and ROOT_PATH inclusion. Both the login
redirect and the logout redirect now use this helper.

Closes #500

* fix(auth-server): remove shadowed urlparse import that broke Keycloak logout

A local `from urllib.parse import urlparse` inside a conditional branch
(line 3224) caused Python to treat urlparse as a local variable in the
entire function. When the branch was skipped (redirect_uri starts with
http), urlparse was undefined at line 3235, crashing the logout handler.

The top-level import on line 24 already provides urlparse. Removing the
redundant local imports fixes the crash and allows the auth-server to
properly redirect to Keycloak's OIDC logout endpoint.

* chore: untrack pytest report artifacts in frontend/tests/reports

These files are regenerated on every pytest run and only contain run
metadata (timestamps, exit codes). Remove them from git and add the
directory to .gitignore so future runs don't dirty the working tree.

* fix(auth-server): accept same-origin redirects when SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN is unset

The redirect_uri guard added to oauth2_logout rejected every absolute URL
when SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN was empty, which is the documented default in
.env.example for single-domain deployments. The SPA-issued logout
redirect to https://<host>/logout was blocked, so Keycloak fell back to
its own post-logout page and users bypassed the "Successfully Logged
Out" countdown. The same regression affected oauth2_callback.

Teach _is_redirect_within_cookie_domain to short-circuit True when the
redirect's (scheme, host) matches the inbound request's origin, honoring
x-forwarded-proto and x-forwarded-host so TLS-terminating upstreams
(ingress, ALB) are handled correctly. The cookie-domain check still
extends trust to additional subdomains when SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN is
configured. Both callers now pass the Request.

* fix(telemetry-collector): pin Lambda runtime to python3.12

The vendored `pydantic_core` in `lambda/collector/pydantic_core/` ships
a CPython 3.12 compiled extension
(`_pydantic_core.cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu.so`). The Lambda runtime
had been configured as `python3.13`, which caused an
`ImportModuleError: No module named 'pydantic_core._pydantic_core'`
after the collector was redeployed with the schema v2 changes from
this PR, because the 3.12 ABI does not load under 3.13.

collector is internal infrastructure for our side only, so there is no
customer impact from the runtime choice.

A future cleanup could either vendor a 3.13-compatible `.so` or build
the Lambda package in a Lambda-matching container; for now staying on
3.12 is the smaller change.

Feat/extended mongo connection string support (#947)

* feat(storage): support full MongoDB connection string override

Adds MONGODB_CONNECTION_STRING setting (env var) that, when set, is
passed verbatim to the MongoDB client and bypasses the discrete
host/port/user/password assembly. Required for MongoDB Atlas
(mongodb+srv://...) and any externally-managed MongoDB where the
caller wants to own the full URI, retryWrites, TLS, and replica-set
parameters.

When the override is set, build_client_options() and build_tls_kwargs()
return empty dicts so the URI fully owns those options.

* feat(api): safely display host in health endpoint when using URI override

Parses MONGODB_CONNECTION_STRING with urllib.parse.urlsplit to extract
the hostname without triggering DNS (pymongo's parse_uri resolves SRV
records live, which is unacceptable for a health endpoint) and without
including userinfo in the response. Falls back to a generic marker if
the URI is unparseable.

* feat(docker): support MONGODB_CONNECTION_STRING in entrypoint wait loops

When MONGODB_CONNECTION_STRING is set, both entrypoints use it verbatim
(including mongodb+srv:// for Atlas), skip the replSetGetStatus check
(the caller owns topology), and parse the hostname via urllib.parse
for log display without leaking creds.

Also adds regex-based URI redaction to the error-log path so connection
strings never leak to stdout even if pymongo echoes them in exceptions.

* feat(charts): support MongoDB connection string override

Adds mongodb.connectionString value to charts/mongodb-configure/ and
plumbs it through the stack chart. When set:

- The mongo-credentials Secret emits MONGODB_CONNECTION_STRING instead
  of the discrete DOCUMENTDB_HOST/PORT/USERNAME/PASSWORD/REPLICA_SET
  keys, so there's a single source of truth.
- The wait.py init script uses the URI verbatim, skips replSetGetStatus
  (the caller owns topology), and redacts any mongodb:// substrings
  from exception output.
- The init-mongodb-ce.py script skips replSetInitiate (MongoDB Atlas
  and other managed clusters don't grant admin access) but still runs
  collection/index/scope setup against the provided URI.

For externally-managed MongoDB (e.g. Atlas), also set mongodb.enabled=false
in the stack chart to skip the in-cluster MongoDB operator.

* feat(scripts): respect MONGODB_CONNECTION_STRING in ops scripts

Every operational script that builds a mongodb:// URI from discrete
env vars now short-circuits to MONGODB_CONNECTION_STRING when set.
Includes init-mongodb-ce.py, init-documentdb-indexes.py, load-scopes.py,
manage-documentdb.py, migrate-file-to-mongodb.py,
migrate-servers-add-is-active.py, debug-scopes.py, backfill_agent_fields.py,
init-documentdb.sh, and init-mongodb.sh.

For init-mongodb-ce.py and init-mongodb.sh, the override path additionally
skips replSetInitiate — MongoDB Atlas and other managed clusters don't
grant admin rights to initialize replica sets, and the cluster is
already configured by the provider.

* feat(compose): pass through MONGODB_CONNECTION_STRING env var

Adds MONGODB_CONNECTION_STRING to the registry and auth-server service
environments in docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.prebuilt.yml, and
docker-compose.podman.yml. When set on the host, it takes precedence
over the discrete DOCUMENTDB_HOST/PORT/USERNAME/PASSWORD vars, allowing
docker-compose deployments to target MongoDB Atlas or any externally-
managed MongoDB instance.

The in-container MongoDB init service is deliberately not updated:
users pointing at external MongoDB would disable that container entirely.

* docs(configuration): document MONGODB_CONNECTION_STRING override

Adds a section to the storage-backend guide covering the full
connection-string override: MongoDB Atlas example, precedence rules,
why STORAGE_BACKEND=mongodb-ce is correct for Atlas (not 'documentdb'),
Helm plumbing, and the mongodb-configure job's auto-skip of
replSetInitiate when the override is in use.

* fix tests

fix(config): validate STORAGE_BACKEND and accept mongodb / mongodb-atlas aliases (#954) (#957)

STORAGE_BACKEND had no allowlist validation. Any value outside
("documentdb", "mongodb-ce") silently routed every repository factory to
the file/FAISS backend. An operator who set STORAGE_BACKEND=mongodb
(intuitive when deploying against MongoDB Atlas per PR #947) would
observe the Atlas connection succeed at entrypoint but then see
FilePeerFederationRepository crash the pod with PermissionError on
/home/appuser in the non-root container.

This change:

- Adds ALLOWED_STORAGE_BACKENDS (file, documentdb, mongodb-ce, mongodb,
  mongodb-atlas) and MONGODB_BACKENDS frozensets in registry.core.config.
- Adds a Pydantic @field_validator that rejects unknown values at
  startup with a clear error message listing accepted values. Empty /
  unset coerces to "file" (historical default). Case and whitespace are
  normalized.
- Replaces every duplicated ("documentdb", "mongodb-ce") tuple across
  13 factory call sites plus telemetry, stats, scopes, main, and
  logging-setup call sites with a single MONGODB_BACKENDS reference.
- Inverts the SCRAM-SHA selection in utils/mongodb_connection.py so
  only "documentdb" picks SCRAM-SHA-1; every other MongoDB variant
  (mongodb-ce / mongodb / mongodb-atlas / future aliases) uses
  SCRAM-SHA-256. Mirrored in scripts/inspect-documentdb.py.
- Updates .env.example and docs/faq/configuring-mongodb-atlas-backend.md
  to document the allowlist and warn about the previous silent-fallback
  failure mode.
- Adds 95 new tests:
  - tests/unit/core/test_config_validation.py covers accept / reject /
    normalize / empty.
  - tests/unit/repositories/test_factory_aliases.py covers every
    MongoDB alias x every factory routing to the same class as the
    mongodb-ce baseline (the invariant that prevents the silent-fallback
    bug from recurring).
  - tests/unit/core/test_telemetry.py TestStorageBackendAliasRouting
    extends existing parametrization to cover the telemetry branching
    for every MongoDB alias.

The Terraform side (ECS variable allowlist expansion + gating
aws_docdb_cluster on storage_backend == documentdb) is tracked
separately in issue #955 for milestone v1.0.23.

Closes #954

fix(docker): pass BUILD_VERSION when publishing to Docker Hub (#919) (#958)

* fix(docker): pass BUILD_VERSION to publish_containers.sh build and bake into every image (#919)

scripts/publish_containers.sh built docker images without passing
--build-arg BUILD_VERSION, so the Dockerfile ARG default of "1.0.0" was
baked into every Docker Hub image regardless of the actual release tag.
Customers pulling mcpgateway/registry:v1.0.22 saw BUILD_VERSION=1.0.0
inside the container, which the registry then reported to the UI and
telemetry.

ECR images are fine because the GitHub Actions workflow passes
--build-arg BUILD_VERSION directly. This PR brings the Docker Hub
publish path to parity.

Changes:

- scripts/publish_containers.sh: pass --build-arg BUILD_VERSION="$VERSION"
  alongside the existing SERVER_DIR build-arg. Harmless for Dockerfiles
  that do not declare the ARG.
- docker/Dockerfile.auth, docker/Dockerfile.mcp-server,
  docker/Dockerfile.mcp-server-light, metrics-service/Dockerfile: add
  the same ARG BUILD_VERSION="1.0.0" / ENV BUILD_VERSION=$BUILD_VERSION
  pair that docker/Dockerfile.registry already has in its final stage.
  Every component image now reports its real release version via
  `docker inspect`.

Closes #919

* fix(docker): bake BUILD_VERSION into every locally-built image and stop stomping it at prebuilt runtime (#919)

Extends the publish_containers.sh fix to the three compose-based build
paths so that ALL locally-built images (registry, auth-server, three
MCP servers, mcpgw-server, metrics-service) carry the correct
BUILD_VERSION, and so that the prebuilt compose path no longer clobbers
the image-baked value at runtime.

Previously only the `registry` entry in docker-compose.yml passed
`BUILD_VERSION` as a build-arg. Every other service built via
`docker compose build` used the Dockerfile ARG default of "1.0.0" even
after the Dockerfile additions in this PR.

Separately, docker-compose.prebuilt.yml set
`BUILD_VERSION=${BUILD_VERSION:-1.0.0}` as a runtime env var, which
stomped the value baked into the pulled image whenever the operator's
.env did not set BUILD_VERSION. Removing that line lets the image-baked
value win at runtime.

Changes:

- docker-compose.yml: add `BUILD_VERSION: ${BUILD_VERSION:-1.0.0}` to
  the build.args of auth-server, currenttime-server, fininfo-server,
  realserverfaketools-server, mcpgw-server, metrics-service.
- docker-compose.podman.yml: same six services (matching the
  docker-compose.yml additions).
- docker-compose.prebuilt.yml: remove the runtime
  `BUILD_VERSION=${BUILD_VERSION:-1.0.0}` env var from the registry
  service; replace with an explanatory comment.

Verified via `docker compose config` that the build-args propagate
correctly (BUILD_VERSION=vTEST-extension flows into all 7 build
entries) and that prebuilt no longer emits BUILD_VERSION as a runtime
env var.

feat(terraform): gate AWS DocumentDB resources on storage_backend == documentdb; accept MongoDB aliases (#955) (#961)

The ECS Terraform module had two related gaps:

1. The `storage_backend` variable validation accepted only `["file",
   "documentdb"]`. Mirroring the Python-side allowlist from #954, this
   expands to accept `mongodb-ce`, `mongodb`, and `mongodb-atlas` as
   aliases. Operators can now set `storage_backend = "mongodb-atlas"` in
   tfvars and point the registry at an external MongoDB (Atlas,
   self-managed) via `mongodb_connection_string` /
   `mongodb_connection_string_secret_arn`.

2. Every AWS DocumentDB resource (cluster, subnet group, parameter
   group, instance, KMS key, KMS alias, credentials secret + version,
   secret rotation Lambda + IAM policy + CW log group + SG rules, 3 SSM
   parameters, 6 outputs, 2 CloudWatch alarms, 5 security group rules)
   was provisioned unconditionally, even for `storage_backend = "file"`
   deployments. This wasted ~$200-400/month per environment on unused
   DocumentDB infrastructure. Now gated on `local.is_aws_documentdb`.

Implementation:

- `terraform/aws-ecs/locals.tf` - new `mongodb_compatible_backends`,
  `is_aws_documentdb`, `is_mongodb_compatible`, `uses_external_mongodb`
  locals. Comment calls out the sync requirement with the Python-side
  ALLOWED_STORAGE_BACKENDS.
- `terraform/aws-ecs/variables.tf` and
  `terraform/aws-ecs/modules/mcp-gateway/variables.tf` - expand
  validation allowlist to mirror Python's.
- `terraform/aws-ecs/main.tf` - bump required_version to >= 1.2 (for
  `precondition`), gate `documentdb_endpoint` and
  `documentdb_credentials_secret_arn` passthroughs on
  `local.is_aws_documentdb`, and add a `terraform_data` resource with
  a `lifecycle.precondition` that fails `terraform plan` at plan time
  if a non-documentdb MongoDB backend is selected without a
  `mongodb_connection_string*`. (Plain `lifecycle` on `module` is not
  yet supported in Terraform 1.11.)
- `terraform/aws-ecs/documentdb.tf` - `count` gating on all 14
  DocumentDB-related resources (5 SGs/rules + KMS key + alias + 2
  secrets + subnet/parameter groups + cluster + instance + 3 SSM
  parameters). Internal cross-references updated to `[0]` indexing.
- `terraform/aws-ecs/cloudwatch-alarms.tf` - `count` on
  `kms_throttling_documentdb` and `documentdb_audit_log_failures`.
- `terraform/aws-ecs/secret-rotation.tf` - `count` on the
  DocumentDB-specific Lambda, its log group, archive, permission, and
  Lambda<->DocumentDB SG rules. Shared IAM policy uses `concat()` to
  conditionally include DocumentDB statements so the RDS rotation
  Lambda is unaffected.
- `terraform/aws-ecs/secret-rotation-config.tf` - `count` on the
  DocumentDB rotation schedule.
- `terraform/aws-ecs/ecs.tf` - refactor existing inline
  `var.storage_backend == "documentdb"` to `local.is_aws_documentdb`
  for consistency.
- `terraform/aws-ecs/outputs.tf` - 7 DocumentDB-related outputs now
  return `null` when the backend is not documentdb. Downstream
  `terraform_remote_state` consumers must handle the null case.
- `terraform/aws-ecs/terraform.tfvars.example` - new "EXTERNAL MONGODB"
  section documenting `storage_backend = "mongodb-atlas"` with the
  secret ARN, the plan-time precondition, and the destructive
  behaviour of switching away from `"documentdb"`.

Backwards compatibility:

- Existing `terraform.tfvars.{keycloak,okta,entra,auth0,auth0-cloudfront}`
  fixtures all use `storage_backend = "documentdb"` and continue to
  plan and apply unchanged (pending zero-drift verification in a
  sandbox).
- The new locals, resource `count` values, and `[0]` indexing are all
  no-ops for the `documentdb` case: Terraform state addresses for
  existing resources remain
  `aws_docdb_cluster.registry` + `[0]` index, which is how Terraform
  addresses count-gated resources. This is a state schema change and
  may cause state address moves; the provider handles this automatically
  in most cases but reviewers should inspect `terraform plan` output.
- DESTRUCTIVE BEHAVIOUR: deployments currently applied with
  `storage_backend = "file"` will see `terraform plan` want to destroy
  the previously-provisioned (unused) AWS DocumentDB cluster, KMS key
  (7-day pending-deletion), and credentials secret
  (`recovery_window_in_days = 0`, immediate delete). This is correct
  but must be called out in release notes. Operators should snapshot
  first if there's any chance the cluster was ever used ad-hoc.

Verification:

- `terraform fmt -recursive` clean on the touched files.
- `terraform init -backend=false` succeeds.
- `terraform validate` passes (pre-existing deprecation warnings on
  `data.aws_region.current.name` are unrelated).
- Precondition fires as expected when `storage_backend = "mongodb-atlas"`
  without a URI variable (verified with a test tfvars).
- Allowlist rejects `storage_backend = "mongo"` with the full list of
  accepted values in the error message.
- Full-fidelity zero-drift `terraform plan` against each of the 5 IdP
  fixtures requires AWS credentials and is noted in the PR test plan
  for a reviewer with sandbox access.

Closes #955.

feat(usage-report): add liveness analysis and per-version instance counts

Introduces analyze_liveness.py to classify customer registry instances into
activity tiers based on recent heartbeat telemetry. With heartbeats emitted
once per 24 hours, counts become a direct proxy for "is this deployment
still running" and let us distinguish genuinely-active instances from
one-off installs.

Tiers:
- Confirmed Alive (leading)  -- >= 5 heartbeats in 7 days
- Stronger Alive (trailing)  -- >= 10 heartbeats in 14 days
- Likely Alive               -- any event in 7 days
- Silent-but-recent          -- event in 7 days but < 5 heartbeats
- Dormant                    -- no event in 14 days

Outputs a markdown section (tier summary, confirmed-alive instance list,
cloud/compute/auth breakdowns) plus a JSON artifact for delta tracking in
future reports.

Also splits the version adoption table to include unique-instance counts
alongside event counts, so versions with few long-lived deployments are
visually distinguishable from versions spread across many instances.

SKILL.md documents the new Step 6c and updates the report template to
include a Liveness section after Registry Instance Lifetime.

feat(usage-report): add compute-platform timeseries chart

Parallels the cloud-provider timeseries chart but groups unique
registry_id counts by the compute platform dimension (docker,
kubernetes, ecs, ec2, etc). Scans all CSV snapshots across dated
subdirectories and produces a two-panel PNG: cumulative unique
installs and daily active installs per platform.

Surfaces platform-level growth rates that the cloud-by-cloud view
does not. In particular, Kubernetes adoption is growing substantially
faster than Docker or ECS, both in absolute and percentage terms,
which tracks with the existing liveness finding that K8s deployments
are stickier than Docker ones.

SKILL.md gains a new Step 5b2 that invokes the script, and the
output-directory layout is updated to include the new PNG.

this PR.

auth_server/server.py overrode the settings-driven resolution:

(no log_file arg), so it was not affected. mcpgw uses its own
logging_setup module with the same default pattern.

alias from pathlib. auth-server now resolves its log file via

This change gates every /internal/* route on an internal-JWT Bearer
signed with the shared SECRET_KEY, using the same contract the
/internal/reload-scopes endpoint has always enforced (see
registry.auth.internal.generate_internal_token / validate_internal_auth,
minted for /internal/reload-scopes since the prior-art addition of
that endpoint).

  prefix="/internal", dependencies=[Depends(validate_internal_auth)]).

  it. The router-level dependency makes the gate the default for any
  future /internal/* endpoint — a new handler just needs
  @internal_router.post("/foo") and the signed-Bearer check is already
  in place. Individual handlers re-declare caller: str = Depends(
  validate_internal_auth) to surface caller identity for audit logs
  and expose the Authorization header in OpenAPI; FastAPI caches
  per-request dependencies so the JWT validates exactly once.

chore(auth): tighten internal JWT leeway + add header-helper unit tests (#998) (#999)

Post-merge hardening from PR #974. Two small, self-contained changes.

1. registry/auth/internal.py: reduce pyjwt decode leeway from 30 to 5
   seconds. The internal JWT TTL is _INTERNAL_JWT_TTL_SECONDS=60, so
   leeway=30 was 50% of the TTL spent on clock-skew tolerance. Registry
   mints the token immediately before the HTTP POST to auth-server, and
   both services are co-located in the same cluster with NTP-synced
   clocks, so 5 seconds is more than sufficient realistic jitter. This
   halves the effective replay window (from 90s to 65s) at essentially
   zero operational risk.

   ::test_rejects_expired_bearer uses iat=now-600, exp=now-120 which
   clears either leeway value. No test update required.

     - Empty string header -> 401 "Missing authorization header"
     - Basic auth scheme -> 401 "Unsupported authentication scheme"

   These cases are indirectly covered by TestInternalRouterGate in the
   auth-server suite via HTTP round-trips, but a direct unit test is

feat(helm): support extraEnv and extraEnvFrom in subcharts and stack (#977)

Add `extraEnv` and `extraEnvFrom` values to auth-server, registry, and
mcpgw subcharts (and the parent stack), letting operators inject
arbitrary env vars or envFrom sources into each service without
forking the charts.

User entries are appended to the end of the container's `env:` and
`envFrom:` lists, so they win over chart-managed envFrom sources on
name collision. A template-render-time validator rejects `extraEnv`
entries that are missing a `name`, duplicate another user entry, or
collide with a chart-reserved name. Reserved names are the union of
every env: name the chart may render and every key sourced via
envFrom from stack-level and per-chart secrets/configmaps, giving
over-rejection as the safe default.

`extraEnvFrom` is intentionally not validated (Helm cannot introspect
external ConfigMap/Secret contents); the values.yaml documentation
names the catastrophic keys to avoid.

Adds helm-unittest suites for each chart (41 tests total) covering
baseline render, append ordering, reserved-name rejection, duplicate
rejection, missing-name rejection, and cross-subchart isolation at
the stack level. Wires `helm unittest` into the existing
.github/workflows/helm-test.yml so these tests gate PRs.

Updates CLAUDE.md with a Helm Chart Development section explaining
the unittest workflow and the invariant that the reserved-name list
and deployment template must be kept in sync.
