fix(helm): respect mongodb.host, mongodb.replicas, mongodb.version values (#968)

The MongoDBCommunity template in
charts/mcp-gateway-registry-stack/templates/mongodb-cluster.yaml uses
Helm's `default` function with the arguments inverted, so values
supplied via values.yaml or --set are silently ignored — the literal
fallbacks always win.

`default A B` returns B if non-empty, else A. The chart wrote
`default .Values.mongodb.replicas "3"` which passes the values as
fallback A and the literal "3" as B; "3" is always truthy, so the
result is always "3" regardless of overrides. Same pattern for
`mongodb.host` and `mongodb.version`.

Flip to the canonical `.Values.X | default "Y"` pipeline form. Default
values are preserved exactly — `helm template` output is byte-for-byte
identical when no overrides are set.

The IAM list endpoint combines users from the identity provider (which
already includes M2M service accounts) with M2M records from MongoDB's
idp_m2m_clients collection. This causes M2M accounts to appear twice
when they exist in both stores.

record exists only in MongoDB (orphaned), the delete fails with 'not
found' and the UI entry can never be removed.

  client_id or name already appears in the IdP results
- Delete endpoint now also removes from MongoDB idp_m2m_clients
- Delete succeeds if user is found in either the IdP OR MongoDB

fix(audit): log authenticated users by name on /api/stats and public reads (#1014)

Authenticated users polling /api/stats from the uptime widget were logged
as username=anonymous in the audit log, because the endpoint had no auth
dependency and the UI's bare fetch() was stripping the session cookie.

Three-layer fix:

- Require nginx_proxied_auth on /api/stats and /api/system/telemetry-detection.
  /api/version stays public (CLI callers + dedicated nginx location block).
- Add a best-effort session-cookie fallback in the audit middleware. When
  no auth dependency has populated request.state.user_context, decode the
  cookie with the same URLSafeTimedSerializer + max_age check as the auth
  path and stamp auth_method=session-cookie-fallback so the fallback is
  distinguishable in audit queries. Read-only; never mutates request state.
- Migrate five bare fetch(apiUrl(...)) call sites in UptimeDisplay and
  Layout to the axios client so they inherit withCredentials=true. Add an
  eslint no-restricted-syntax rule to prevent the pattern from returning.

Breaking change: /api/stats and /api/system/telemetry-detection now return

feat(helm): make ALB ingress scheme configurable with 3-tier override (#967)

Operators deploying the registry on private VPCs (internal MCP
catalogues behind a VPN, regulated environments where public endpoints
aren't acceptable) currently have to fork the chart just to flip
`alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/scheme` from the hardcoded
`internet-facing`. Make it configurable, following the requested
pattern (per @omrishiv's review on #967) so the scheme can be set
once for the whole stack, once per app chart, or once per individual
ingress.

The resolution order each ingress template evaluates is:

  .Values.ingress.scheme                  # tier 1 — per-ingress override
  | default .Values.global.ingress.scheme # tier 2 — app-chart or stack global
  | default "internet-facing"             # tier 3 — back-compat default

In stack deployments, Helm's automatic propagation of `global.*` means
the umbrella's `global.ingress.scheme` overrides each subchart's own
`global.ingress.scheme`. Standalone subchart deployments fall back to
the subchart's own chart-level default.

Behaviors:

* No overrides → both ingresses `internet-facing` (byte-for-byte
  identical to current rendered output, no behavioral change).
* `--set global.ingress.scheme=internal` (stack) → both ingresses
  `internal`.
* `--set registry.ingress.scheme=internal` → only the registry
  ingress is `internal`; mcpgw stays at the inherited default.
* `--set mcpgw.ingress.scheme=internal` → only the mcpgw ingress
  is `internal`.
* Stack global + per-app override → per-app value wins.

Files changed:

* `charts/registry/values.yaml` — declare `global.ingress.scheme`
  (chart default `internet-facing`) and `ingress.scheme: ""`
  (per-ingress hook; empty falls through to global).
* `charts/registry/templates/ingress.yaml` — coalesce expression
  on the `scheme` annotation.
* `charts/mcpgw/values.yaml` — same shape as registry.
* `charts/mcpgw/templates/ingress.yaml` — same coalesce.
* `charts/mcp-gateway-registry-stack/values.yaml` — stack-level
  default `global.ingress.scheme: internet-facing` with usage
  comment pointing at the per-app override.

Verified via `helm template` on the umbrella stack across all
five scenarios above, plus standalone `charts/registry` for the
tier-2 (chart-global) path.

feat(auth): resource-bound JWT tokens (#944) (#1010)

* feat(auth): resource-bound JWT tokens (#944)

Adds an optional `resource: {type, id}` field on token mint so a JWT
can be scoped to a single resource at issuance. The nginx edge now
enforces the binding: a resource-bound token rejects at /validate
with 403 when the request URL does not match the claim.

Before this, any JWT issued to a user was valid against every
resource the user could reach — agents and CI pipelines holding
long-lived tokens had strictly more access than the workflow they
were built for.

What's in:
- New `registry/auth/resource_binding.py` single source of truth:
  ResourceType + TokenKind enums, JWT claim-name constants,
  deny/allow list, URL classifier, normalizer, pre-mint
  authorization helper with asyncio.wait_for timeout on DB lookups.
- auth_server: ResourceBinding Pydantic model (StrictStr id,
  validator rejects `..` / `%` / control chars). /validate block
  handles every token_kind case fail-closed: None+self_signed → 403,
  None+external IdP → accepted as user, 'user' → pass, 'resource' →
  require type+id match against the URL, else → 403.
- Registry /api/tokens/generate: accepts optional resource, runs
  pre-mint authorization, forwards to /internal/tokens, decodes the
  returned JWT to detect silent rolling-upgrade downgrade (500 with
  Connection: close), and records distinct audit actions for user
  vs resource-bound mints.
- Frontend: new ResourceBoundTokenButton mounted in the four
  detail modals. ServerConfigModal (Connect flow) gained a
  resourceType prop so Connect tokens are resource-bound for the
  server being connected to, and VirtualServerCard passes
  resourceType='virtual_server'.
- Docs: api-reference and jwt-token-vending updated, including
  deploy-ordering guidance for the breaking change below.

Breaking change:
  Self-signed tokens without a `token_kind` claim (i.e. minted by a
  pre-#944 gateway) are rejected at /validate with 403. External IdP
  tokens (Cognito, Keycloak, Entra, Okta, Auth0) and session cookies
  are not affected — they never carry the claim and continue to flow
  through as user tokens. Users holding cached self-signed tokens
  from before the upgrade must re-mint. Deploy the auth-server first
  (or blue/green) to avoid a window where a new registry mints tokens
  against an old auth-server that silently drops the unknown claim.

    are caught against SECRET_KEY in the reserved list.
  - Warns on malformed lines (missing '=' or empty key) instead of silently
    skipping them.

and envFrom configmap/secret data keys, and fails when any rendered name is
missing from charts/<subchart>/reserved-env-names.txt. This would have

feat: multi-replica airegistry-tools support (#1021)

* feat(mcpgw): support multi-replica deployment via stateless HTTP transport

Enables horizontally scaling the mcpgw server by switching FastMCP's
streamable-HTTP transport to stateless mode, so MCP requests can be
served by any replica behind a round-robin load balancer.

Previously mcpgw ran in FastMCP's default stateful mode, which keeps
per-session StreamableHTTPServerTransport objects in memory on whichever
replica handled the initial MCP `initialize` call. A round-robin LB
then broke clients on subsequent requests with "Session not found".

Changes:

- servers/mcpgw/server.py: read MCPGW_STATELESS_HTTP env var, pass
  stateless_http kwarg to mcp.run(), add local /health route for k8s
  probes with no registry dependency.
- servers/mcpgw/pyproject.toml: tighten fastmcp pin to >=3.2.0,<4.0.0
  (stateless_http kwarg landed in 3.x).
- charts/mcpgw: add app.oidcEnabled and app.statelessHttp values;
  auto-enable stateless when replicas > 1 and oidcEnabled=false; fail
  template render when replicas > 1 and oidcEnabled=true (OAuthProxy
  state is not yet shared across replicas — tracked for a later phase).
- charts/mcpgw/templates/deployment.yaml: replace TCP probes with HTTP
  /health probes; add terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 45 and a preStop
  sleep-5 hook so rolling deploys drain in-flight tool calls.
- charts/mcpgw/templates/poddisruptionbudget.yaml: new, rendered only
  when replicas > 1.
- charts/mcpgw/templates/service.yaml: honor service.sessionAffinity
  (documented as an interim, not the recommended path).
- charts/mcpgw/templates/_helpers.tpl: reserve MCPGW_STATELESS_HTTP and
  OIDC_ENABLED in extraEnv validation; branch the error message so
  OIDC_ENABLED specifically directs users to app.oidcEnabled.
- charts/mcp-gateway-registry-stack/values.yaml: surface
  mcpgw.app.oidcEnabled so stack users see the guard-rail contract
  next to replicas.
- charts/mcpgw/tests: new stateless_http_test.yaml (auto-enable,
  overrides, guard rail, probes, lifecycle, PDB, affinity); update
  extra_env_test.yaml positional assertions and add an OIDC_ENABLED
  error-pattern test.

Scope: the stateful-to-stateless switch is safe for mcpgw specifically
because every tool is pure request/response against the registry API
(no ctx.report_progress, no sampling, no server-initiated
notifications). Multi-replica with OIDC/OAuthProxy is explicitly gated
pending shared state storage.

feat(auth): enforce tool-level access control in list and response APIs (#1026) (#1027)

* feat(auth): enforce tool-level access control in list and response APIs (#1026)

Tool-level scope restrictions (per-server tools allowlist in the mcp-scopes
DocumentDB collection) were only honored at tools/call invocation. Every
surface that returns a tool list (UI, GET /servers, GET /tools/*, semantic
search, MCP tools/list) leaked tools the caller could not use.

Changes
- New registry/auth/access_resolver.py: UserAccess dataclass,
  resolve_scope_access single-pass scope-repo loop that derives both
  accessible_servers and accessible_tools, preserves existing wildcard
  semantics (tools: ["all"] and ["*"] both mean wildcard), and honors the
  cross-server admin wildcard (server: "*" / "all") used by
  scripts/registry-admins.json. Legacy scope audit on startup warns
  operators when rows are missing the tools field or declare an empty list
  alongside tools/call.
- New registry/auth/tool_filter.py: filter_tools_for_user normalizes name
  and tool_name keys (so registry, search, and MCP shapes all filter
  identically), fails closed on missing or empty allowlist, and emits a
  ToolFilterAuditEvent on every prune.
- New registry/audit/events.py and sink.py: pluggable audit sink logging
  structured JSON on the registry.audit logger.
- registry/api/server_routes.py and search_routes.py: apply the filter at
  GET /servers (with num_tools recomputed to match), GET /tools/{path},
  GET /tools/all, and all three sites inside POST /api/search/semantic
  (per-server matching_tools, top-level ToolSearchResult, virtual-server
  matching_tools), including num_tools recomputation for server and
  virtual-server search results.
- registry/auth/dependencies.py: enhanced_auth and nginx_proxied_auth now
  call resolve_scope_access once; user_context gains accessible_tools.
- registry/main.py: startup lifespan calls audit_legacy_scopes_on_startup.
- auth_server/server.py: new POST /mcp-proxy/{server_name} endpoint buffers
  upstream tools/list responses (MCP_PROXY_MAX_BODY_BYTES, default 2 MiB,
  413 on overflow) and filters result.tools per user when
  MCP_TOOLS_LIST_FILTER_ENABLED is on. Non-tools/list methods stream
  through unchanged. filter_tools_list_response reuses
  validate_server_tool_access for per-tool authorization so list and call
  share a single source of truth.
- registry/core/nginx_service.py: MCP location blocks now proxy_pass to
  auth-server:8888/mcp-proxy/{server_name} with X-Upstream-Url header.
- Frontend ServerCard and SemanticSearchResults: distinct empty-state copy
  when the server is accessible and healthy but the user has no allowed
  tools.
- Three new env vars (MCP_TOOLS_LIST_FILTER_ENABLED,
  MCP_PROXY_MAX_BODY_BYTES, TOOL_FILTER_AUDIT_LOG_LEVEL) propagated across
  Docker, Terraform, Helm, the unified parameter reference, the System
  Config page, and reserved-env-names for the extra_env collision tests.
- Tests: 18 unit tests for access_resolver, 28 unit tests for tool_filter,
  13 integration tests across the four REST endpoints. nginx_service unit
  tests updated for the new proxy_pass target and X-Upstream-Url header.

Backwards compatibility
- Scope rows missing a tools field now fail closed (previously leaked the
  full list on GET while denying tools/call). Startup audit warns
  operators so they can migrate to tools: ["all"] if wildcard was
  intended. Admin scope (server: "*", tools: ["all"]) unchanged.

Fixes #1026

* fix(auth): tolerate display-name/path mismatch in tool filter lookup (#1026)

Live testing against a running deployment revealed that the filter was
being called with the server's display_name ("AI Registry tools") while
the scope rules in DocumentDB store the technical name
("airegistry-tools"). The dict lookup on accessible_tools always missed,
so every call fell through to the fail-closed branch and restricted
users saw zero tools on every accessible server.

Fix:
- registry/auth/tool_filter.py: new _lookup_allowlist helper that tries
  each candidate name in both raw and slash-stripped form, then falls
  back to matching against slash-stripped keys of the stored allowlist.
  Mirrors _server_names_match in auth_server.
- filter_tools_for_user and tool_allowed_for_user accept an optional
  server_path kwarg so callers that know both the display name and the
  registered path can hand over both identifiers.
- All seven call sites in registry/api/server_routes.py and
  registry/api/search_routes.py now pass server_path alongside the
  existing server_name argument.

Verified end-to-end against the running deployment across seven test
personas (admin, mixed, wildcard, all-string, restricted, empty, union,
multi-server-multi-restricted). All four REST endpoints (GET /api/servers,
GET /api/servers/tools/{path}, GET /api/servers/tools/all,
POST /api/search/semantic) return the expected pruned tool sets.

Tests:
- Added two regression unit tests covering the display-name vs path
  mismatch in both directions.
- All 61 tests under tests/unit/auth/test_tool_filter.py,
  tests/unit/auth/test_access_resolver.py, and
  tests/integration/test_tool_level_access.py pass.

* fix(auth): accept bare-string tools wildcard in scope rules (#1026)

Live ECS testing revealed that some scope rows in DocumentDB store the
tools allowlist as a bare string ("*" or "all") rather than a list
(["*"] / ["all"]) when the UI form submits the wildcard variant. The
auth_server's existing validate_server_tool_access tolerated this
silently because Python's substring `in` operator returned True for
"*" in "*", but the new resolver in registry/auth/access_resolver.py
fell through the not-isinstance(list) branch and produced an empty
allowlist. Symptom: a user belonging to a group whose UI showed
"Tools: * (All tools)" got zero tools back from /api/servers,
/api/tools/{path}, and /api/search/semantic.

Resolver now treats:
- tools: "*"   -> wildcard (same as ["*"])
- tools: "all" -> wildcard (same as ["all"])
- tools: "foo" -> single-element allowlist (same as ["foo"])
- tools: {dict|int|...} -> empty allowlist, fail-closed (unchanged)

* fix(infra): source Keycloak DB credentials from Secrets Manager (#1026)

Live testing surfaced that the Keycloak ECS task fails to start with
"Access denied for user 'keycloak'" any time the rotation Lambda
rotates the Aurora MySQL password. Root cause: KC_DB_USERNAME and
KC_DB_PASSWORD were sourced from /keycloak/database/{username,password}
SSM parameters, but the rotation Lambda (mcp-gateway-rotate-rds) only
updates the Secrets Manager secret keycloak/database; it never writes
back to SSM. The MySQL user gets the new password, the SSM copy stays
stale, and Keycloak crashes on every restart with the wrong password.

Fix:
- KC_DB_USERNAME and KC_DB_PASSWORD now use the ECS valueFrom JSON-key
  syntax to extract username and password directly from the
  aws_secretsmanager_secret.keycloak_db_secret resource managed by the
  rotation Lambda. Single source of truth.
- IAM execution policy gains secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on the
  Keycloak DB secret and drops the now-unused SSM password ARN.
- aws_ssm_parameter.keycloak_database_username and
  aws_ssm_parameter.keycloak_database_password resources removed.
  KC_DB_URL stays in SSM because the JDBC URL doesn't rotate.

Verified:
- terraform fmt clean.
- terraform validate clean.
- terraform plan shows the task definition replaced with the new
  valueFrom targets (secretsmanager:keycloak/database:password::,
  :username::), the IAM policy updated in place, and the two SSM
  parameters destroyed. No drift in unrelated resources.

fix(agents+deps): use update_agent for security-pending tag (#1033) + bump litellm 1.83.14 (#1034) (#1035)

* fix(agents): use update_agent for post-scan security-pending tag (#1033)

Closes #1033 (and duplicate #1032).

When the post-registration A2A security scan flags an agent unsafe and
the scanner config requires the security-pending tag, the route in
registry/api/agent_routes.py was calling agent_service.register_agent()
to apply the tag. register_agent is an INSERT operation and the agent
was already inserted earlier in the same request flow, so the second
call always raised "Agent registration failed: path '...' already
exists". The exception was caught and silently swallowed, so the route
returned 2xx to the caller but the security-pending tag never landed
and no warning surfaced to the user.

Production reproduction (from CloudWatch logs, scan took ~4.5s):
  21:23:43.603  Created agent 'AI Tourist Guide' at '/ai-tourist-guide'
  21:23:43.901  Running A2A security scan ... yara,spec
  21:23:48.070  Scan completed: Safe: False, High: 1
  21:23:48.075  ERROR: Agent registration failed: path already exists
  21:23:48.075  ERROR: Failed to run security scan for agent

Fix: switch the call to agent_service.update_agent(path, ...), which is
the correct in-place update method and was already imported at the
service layer.

Tests:
- New TestRunSecurityScanOnRegistrationUpdatesViaUpdateAgent class with
  two cases: unsafe scan calls update_agent (and never register_agent),
  safe scan touches no agent state. Both pass.

* fix(ans): use agentHost filter instead of paginating all 63k agents (#1033)

The resolve_ans_name function paginated through the entire GoDaddy ANS
registry (63,681 agents, 100 per page = 600+ sequential HTTP requests)
every time it needed to resolve an ans:// URI to a UUID. This blocked
the single uvicorn worker for 30+ seconds, causing nginx to return 504
Gateway Timeout to the browser on agent registration.

The GoDaddy API supports ?agentHost= as a server-side filter. Since the
ANS name format is "ans://v{version}.{host}", we extract the host and
query with a single request that returns at most a handful of results.

Before: 600+ requests, 30+ seconds, blocks all other API calls.
After: 1 request, <1 second.

* fix(agents): preserve ans_metadata on agent updates (#1033)

Every agent update (health check, scan, toggle) round-tripped through
AgentCard.model_dump() which dropped ans_metadata (not a Pydantic model
field, stored as an extra DB document field by link_ans_to_agent). The
$set then overwrote the entire document without it, silently wiping the
ANS verification badge.

Fix: read the raw MongoDB document before update, extract fields not in
the AgentCard model, and merge them back into the update payload so
$set preserves them.

fix(nginx): serialize config regeneration + atomic writes; fix MCP proxy SSE passthrough (#1052)

* fix(nginx): serialize config regeneration and use atomic file writes

Eliminates two related defects in nginx config regeneration that produced
race conditions during concurrent server CRUD operations.

The registry's nginx_service.generate_config_async() followed by
nginx_service.reload_nginx() was invoked from 20+ call sites, but only
one (virtual_server_service) acquired an asyncio lock. The other call
sites could run concurrently, producing:
- Two parallel regenerations both reading the enabled-server set, both
  writing the config file, with the second write overwriting the first.
- One writer's partial output read by `nginx -t` invoked from a second
  writer.
- Two `nginx -s reload` signals in flight simultaneously.

This change:
- Adds a shared asyncio.Lock on the NginxConfigService singleton and
  wraps every call site (server CRUD, federation, health checks,
  startup) so regen + reload runs serially.
- Replaces the truncate-on-write file open with _atomic_write_text,
  which writes to a temp file in the same directory and uses
  os.replace() to atomically swap. Readers now see either the old
  config or the new one, never a partial file.
- Preserves existing destination file permissions across the atomic
  swap (was silently regressing to 0600 from tempfile defaults).
- Adds startup cleanup of stale ".tmp.*" temp files left behind by a
  SIGKILL-interrupted previous write.
- Adds a NGINX_CONFIG_WRITES Prometheus counter (status=success|failure)
  so operators can detect disk-full or permission failures.

The lone existing _nginx_reload_lock in virtual_server_service is
removed in favor of the shared NginxConfigService.reload_lock.

14 new unit tests cover the atomic write, permission preservation,
stale temp file cleanup, lock serialization, exception release, and
removal of the duplicate lock. All 3222 tests pass with no regressions.

Closes #1044

* fix(mcp-proxy): forward upstream content-type for non-JSON MCP responses

The auth_server's /mcp_proxy endpoint forced every upstream response
into application/json via JSONResponse(_safe_parse_body(...)). Many
MCP servers reply with text/event-stream (SSE) like:

    event: message
    data: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{...}}

That body is not valid JSON, so _safe_parse_body wraps it as
{"raw": "<sse-text>"} and the proxy emits Content-Type: application/json.
MCP clients (Roo Code, Cursor, Claude Code) then fail Zod / schema
validation because the body is neither valid JSON-RPC nor SSE.

Fix: when not filtering tools/list, forward the upstream body and its
content_type unchanged via fastapi.Response. Tools/list filtering still
goes through the JSON path (it requires application/json, gated by the
existing should_filter check).

Affects every server that returns SSE: cloudflare-docs, context7, etc.
Plain-JSON MCP responses are unaffected.

Fix oversized session cookie + bundle related auth fixes (#1042)

* feat(auth): server-side OAuth session store

Move the OAuth session payload (username, email, groups, optional id_token)
from the browser cookie to a MongoDB/DocumentDB-backed store. The cookie now
carries only an opaque, signed session_id, which is hydrated server-side on
every request. This unblocks logins for IdPs that return large groups claims
(e.g. Microsoft Entra ID with many group memberships) where the previous
self-contained cookie exceeded the 4 KB browser limit.

Closes #971: oversized OAuth session cookie breaks login for Entra users
Closes #399: server-side token storage to resolve session cookie size limit
Closes #915: OAUTH_STORE_TOKENS_IN_SESSION=false now genuinely keeps tokens
out of the cookie; id_token lives only server-side and only when the flag is
enabled. With the flag disabled, IdP single-logout via id_token_hint is
unavailable (acceptable trade-off — that is what the flag was meant to do).

Notable changes:
- New auth_server/session_store.py and registry/auth/session_store.py.
  AES-GCM with HKDF-derived key from SECRET_KEY for id_token only; metadata
  is stored as-is (it was already client-visible in the previous signed
  cookie). w:majority writes, primaryPreferred reads, TTL on expires_at.
  Reuses existing MongoDB connection singletons; works on AWS DocumentDB
  and MongoDB CE.
- auth_server/server.py oauth2_callback now writes via create_session and
  signs only the session_id into the cookie. validate_session_cookie (used
  on the MCP proxy auth path) hydrates from the store. Both paths reject
  legacy dict-payload cookies, forcing re-login on deploy.
- registry/auth/dependencies.py centralizes resolution in
  resolve_session_from_cookie. enhanced_auth, get_current_user,
  get_user_session_data, audit middleware fallback, websocket health
  auth, and the OAuth callback handler all go through it.
- CSRF tokens are now bound to the opaque session_id (resolved via the
  cookie), not the raw cookie blob. enhanced_auth exposes session_id in
  user_context for template-side token generation.
- Logout invalidates the server-side record before clearing the cookie,
  so a stolen cookie cannot be replayed against the still-valid server
  state. The id_token in memory is still used for IdP id_token_hint.

* feat(auth): handle Entra group overage via Microsoft Graph

  When an Entra user belongs to more groups than fit in the ID token (Entra
  caps inline groups around 150-200), Entra signals overage via `hasgroups`
  or `_claim_names.groups` and omits the inline `groups` claim. The OAuth
  callback was treating this as "user has no groups" and producing sessions
  with empty scopes/permissions, so admin users could not register MCP
  servers (#929).

  When overage is detected, fall back to GET /me/memberOf on Microsoft Graph
  to recover the user's direct group object IDs. The endpoint works with
  the User.Read scope already granted by `openid email profile` — no admin
  consent change required (unlike /me/getMemberObjects which needs
  GroupMember.Read.All).

  Sovereign-cloud support: ENTRA_GRAPH_BASE_URL is inferred from
  ENTRA_LOGIN_BASE_URL via the documented mapping (public/US Gov/China),
  so operators on those clouds need no extra config. ENTRA_GRAPH_BASE_URL
  remains as an explicit override for proxied or non-standard deployments.

  Closes #929

Signed-off-by: omrishiv <327609+omrishiv@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(auth): unify admin/scope derivation across auth paths

  The registry's two auth dependencies — enhanced_auth (cookie path) and
  nginx_proxied_auth (proxied header path) — could resolve the same
  authenticated user to different is_admin and ui_permissions results,
  producing 403 Admin access required on session-cookie routes for users
  who appeared as admin elsewhere in the UI (#933).

  Root cause: when X-Groups was not forwarded by the auth_server,
  nginx_proxied_auth synthesized groups from a scope heuristic — granting
  "mcp-registry-admin" if mcp-servers-unrestricted/{read,execute} were both
  present, else "mcp-registry-user". This synthesis path could grant admin
  to non-admin users on the proxied path while the cookie path correctly
  said non-admin for the same identity.

  Changes:
  - New private _derive_user_context() helper builds the canonical
    user_context dict from (groups, scopes, auth_method, provider). Both
    enhanced_auth and nginx_proxied_auth call it. Federation-static
    auth_method short-circuits to no-access inside the helper, so all three
    derivation paths now share one implementation.
  - Removed the X-Groups-fallback synthesis in nginx_proxied_auth. If the
    auth_server doesn't forward X-Groups, groups stay empty and is_admin is
    derived purely from scope→ui_permissions (which the auth_server already
    computes when setting X-Scopes).
  - Added TestAuthPathsAgreeOnIsAdmin: same user → same is_admin via both
    paths, regardless of which one resolves them. Regression guard against
    the original #933 divergence.

  Closes #933

fix(build): regenerate uv.lock files and pin uv to 0.11.14 in Dockerfiles (#1064) (#1065)

Container builds fail at `uv sync --locked` with the message
"Resolving despite existing lockfile due to removal of global exclude
newer". Root cause: the lockfiles were generated with an older `uv` that
recorded `[options].exclude-newer` in each lock; current `uv 0.11.x`
writes the option from `uv lock --exclude-newer` but does not honor it
on `uv sync --locked`, so every clean build sees the recorded option as
removed and refuses to install.

Approach taken:

1. Regenerate all 8 uv.lock files with `uv lock` (no --exclude-newer).
   Removes the orphaned [options].exclude-newer block. No dependency
   versions changed in any lockfile (the dependency set is fully
   satisfied by versions older than the original 2026-05-07 anchor).
2. Pin `uv==0.11.14` in every Dockerfile that installs uv. Removes the
   "latest uv reinterprets recorded options" failure mode permanently.
   Future uv upgrades become a deliberate change rather than implicit.

Trade-off: drops the time-anchored supply-chain hardening that
`exclude-newer` was providing. Cannot be preserved with current uv (the
field is orphaned on read). See #1064 for follow-up to file upstream.

fix(test): reset nginx_service.reload_lock per-test to fix xdist flake (#1072) (#1073)

Add an autouse fixture to TestNginxReloadLock that replaces the
nginx_service singleton's reload_lock with a fresh asyncio.Lock at
the start of each test.

Background: nginx_service is a module-level singleton instantiated at
import time. Its reload_lock is therefore created in whichever event
loop happened to import the module first. pytest-asyncio uses a fresh
event loop per test (function scope), so a lock created during test A's
loop fails with 'RuntimeError: Lock is bound to a different event loop'
when test B tries to acquire it. Under pytest-xdist's parallel worker
scheduling this manifests as an intermittent failure — the test
suite was green on commit 938ef5cc and red on the next release-notes-only
commit fd231a28 with no production code change between them.

Validated locally:
  pytest tests/unit/test_virtual_server_service.py::TestNginxReloadLock
  pytest tests/unit/test_virtual_server_service.py -n 8 (71 passed)

The fix is test-side; production code in registry/core/nginx_service.py
is unchanged. The real lock continues to serialize concurrent reloads
in the running registry process where the singleton lives in a single
loop for the lifetime of the process.

1. generate_adoption_funnel_chart.py: new horizontal-bar funnel chart
   that shows the cohort dropoff from "every customer ever installed"
   through 3/7/14/30-day lifetime thresholds and confirmed-alive. Uses
   metrics-*.json + liveness-*.json. Mobile-friendly single-image story
   for inclusion in long-form posts.

2. generate_install_forecast.py: forecasts when cumulative installs will
   cross a target threshold (default 1000). Fits a linear OLS on the
   trailing 14 days plus a 7-day SMA recent-pace projection, both with
   ETA annotations. The exponential and ARIMA models were tried during
   development and dropped in the docstring rationale: with ~5 weeks of
   data the early-week compounding overfits the exponential and ARIMA
   adds wider PI bands without improving point-estimate accuracy.

3. analyze_telemetry.py: adds two new ranking tables in tables-*.md
   alongside the existing "Most Active Instances":
     - Largest Catalogs (top 10 by max_servers + max_agents + max_skills,
       complementing the search-volume-driven Most Active leaderboard)
     - Most Engaged Operators (top 10 by upgrade-chain length, age_days
       tiebreaker, surfacing customers tracking the project closely
       enough to upgrade across multiple releases)
   Also wires both into _build_markdown_tables so they appear in every
   future report between Most Active and Instance Timelines.

4. bastion-scripts/telemetry_db.py: fixes a misleading heartbeat-totals
   roll-up. The "Total" line was summing across every heartbeat ever
   stored, double-counting each instance by its heartbeat count, which
   inflated the "Registered MCP Servers / Agents / Skills" totals 3-4x.
   Now prints (per object class):
     - Fleet sum from the LATEST heartbeat per instance (the honest
       "currently registered across the fleet" number)
     - Instances with > 0
     - Median / median-non-zero / p90 / max per instance
   So the bastion summary becomes 1,643 servers (not 12,997) etc., which
   is what the report-narrative numbers should quote.

5. SKILL.md updated to document both new ranking tables.

The two new ranking tables surface customers like b61dcc9f-60d (the
"textbook upgrader" who has walked v1.0.18 -> v1.0.19 -> ... -> 1.24.0
across seven consecutive releases) which previously ranked low on the
Most Active leaderboard despite being one of the most engaged operators
in the dataset.

* feat(stress): add per-entity data generators (#997)

Three CLI scripts that fetch from real public catalogs, augment to
the target size, validate each payload against the registry's
client-side Pydantic models, and write per-payload JSON files to
`tests/stress/data/<entity>/<count>/`.

- `generate_servers.py`: pages the Anthropic MCP Registry
  (`https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers`), runs each
  entry through the existing `cli.anthropic_transformer.
  transform_anthropic_to_gateway`, and overrides for stress testing:
  `status=draft` (suppresses health-check loop), synthetic
  `proxy_pass_url`, and adds the `stress-test` tag. Validates as
  `api.registry_client.InternalServiceRegistration`.

- `generate_agents.py`: pages the GoDaddy ANS catalog with
  `Authorization: sso-key {ANS_API_KEY}:{ANS_API_SECRET}` and a 429
  retry loop with exponential backoff (max 5 retries). Maps each
  record to the A2A Agent Card shape (`code_reviewer_agent.json`
  example) and validates as `api.registry_client.AgentRegistration`.
  Includes the server-required `supportedProtocol: "a2a"`.

- `generate_skills.py`: enumerates `*/SKILL.md` blobs from the
  `anthropics/skills` repo via the GitHub trees API (uses
  `GITHUB_TOKEN` when set), constructs payloads pointing at the raw
  GitHub URL, validates as `SkillRegistrationRequest` plus an extra
  `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$` name-regex check that mirrors the
  server-side validator in `registry/schemas/skill_models.py:410`.

Upstream API responses are cached under `tests/stress/data/.cache/`
so re-runs do not re-hammer the public endpoints.

End-to-end smoke test: `generate_servers --count 100` against the
live Anthropic registry produces 100 valid payloads in ~16 s with
zero validation errors (from 8,345 unique upstream records).

* feat(stress): add async bulk registration loader (#997)

`register_entities.py` reads the JSON payloads produced by the
generators and POSTs each to the registry's appropriate endpoint
using `httpx.AsyncClient` bounded by `asyncio.Semaphore`.

Endpoint and content-type mapping (mirrors `api.registry_client.
RegistryClient._make_request`):

  servers  -> POST /api/servers/register   (form-encoded; tags ->
              comma string, metadata -> JSON string)
  agents   -> POST /api/agents/register    (JSON)
  skills   -> POST /api/skills             (JSON)

Idempotency: 409 Conflict and "already exists" / "duplicate"
substring matches on 400/422 bodies are recorded as `skipped`, not
`failed`. A single 401 triggers one token-file reread before giving
up; the file parser handles flat `{"access_token": ...}`, nested
`{"tokens": {...}}`, and `{"token_data": {...}}` shapes -- same set
the existing CLI in `api/registry_management.py:491` accepts.

Output (`tests/stress/results/<backend>/size-<count>/registration.
json`) follows the schema in `lld-stress-test.md` §4.4: per-entity
counts (`registered` / `skipped` / `failed`), `failure_rate`, full
latency p50/p95/p99/min/max/mean over successful registrations, and
a `failures[]` array carrying the payload filename, status code,
latency, and (truncated) response body for every non-success.

Verified end-to-end against a freshly populated `mongodb-ce`
backend: 45 servers registered (HTTP 201), 1 skipped, output JSON
schema matches LLD, MongoDB document count matches the loader's
`registered` field exactly. The remaining failures were nginx 5xx
under load (registry-side Mongo connection resets) -- the harness
correctly captured each with its payload name and error body.

* feat(stress): lower default concurrency, document registry bottlenecks

DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY drops from 10 -> 3. Empirical finding from the
Phase 1 verification run: at concurrency=10 against a local
mongodb-ce stack, every registration triggers (1) synchronous
embedding compute, (2) full nginx config regeneration, and
(3) a security scan. After ~30-50 in-flight registrations Mongo
starts returning `[Errno 104] Connection reset by peer` and the
remaining ~50% of the batch fails. At concurrency=3 the cascade
does not fire on this hardware. Until the server-side
bottlenecks are addressed as separate issues, the default should
favor reliable completion over throughput.

README adds two pieces of operator guidance discovered during the
same run:

1. A "note on --concurrency" explaining why the default is low,
   what's expensive per registration, and when to raise the flag
   explicitly (e.g. DocumentDB on real infra).

2. A "Recommended runtime environment knobs" section pointing at
   `HEALTH_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS=86400` to suppress the
   registry's continual MCP-server ping loop during a run. With
   ~50+ registered servers, the default 30-second ping interval
   keeps auth-server and Mongo busy enough that the registration
   request path can see nginx 504s on `/validate` subrequests.

Both findings will be filed as separate registry issues (cascade
behavior, nginx regen-per-register cost, sync embedding compute
on the request path). This commit captures the workarounds the
harness operator needs today.

* feat(stress): support GoDaddy OTE for ANS agent generator

The `/v1/agents` endpoint on production `api.godaddy.com` is gated
behind an internal SSO realm (`realm=jomax&app=ra.int`) and is not
reachable with regular customer credentials. The OTE test
environment (`api.ote-godaddy.com`) accepts customer-issued
partner credentials and exposes the same endpoint with real data
(empirically: 732 ANS records during Phase 1 verification).

Changes to `generate_agents.py`:

- `_ans_credentials()` now prefers `GODADDY_API_KEY_OTE` /
  `GODADDY_API_SECRET_OTE` and defaults the endpoint to
  `https://api.ote-godaddy.com`. Falls back to the original
  `ANS_API_KEY` / `ANS_API_SECRET` pair for setups that already
  have prod-tier access.

- `_base_name()` now prefers the upstream's `agentDisplayName`
  field for a human-readable name; when only `ansName` is
  available, it picks a meaningful DNS component instead of the
  last one (which is often a generic TLD or a semver fragment).

- `_build_payload()` prefers `endpoints[0].agentUrl` (the actual
  ANS field name) over the generic `url`/`endpoint` fallbacks.

README documents the OTE preference plus the underlying reason
(production host gated by internal SSO).

End-to-end verified against ANS OTE: the generator pages 732
records cleanly, transforms 100 of them into valid
`AgentRegistration` payloads in ~3 seconds, with zero validation
errors. The bulk loader then registered 12 of those before
hitting registry-side reliability issues (a separate
`'dict' object has no attribute 'name'` security-scan bug in
`registry/api/agent_routes.py:144`, plus MongoDB CE wedging under
parallel agent-register load even at concurrency=3). Both are
findings worth filing as separate registry issues; the harness
itself captured every failure with its payload filename, status
code, and response body as designed.

* feat(stress): auto-resolve JWT token in run_stress_test.sh

Before this commit the orchestrator required two prerequisite
commands -- regenerate a token, then export STRESS_TOKEN_FILE to
point at it -- before `bash run_stress_test.sh <backend> <size>`
would work. That friction made the demo less than the
single-command experience the script's name implies.

The script now performs token resolution itself:

1. If STRESS_TOKEN_FILE is set, use it (validate first).
2. Else scan known locations: .oauth-tokens/ingress.json (the
   convention from api/registry_management.py:208) and
   .oauth-tokens/mcp-gateway-m2m-token.json (the path written by
   keycloak/setup/generate-agent-token.sh).
3. If none is valid (file missing, or `expires_at` is in the
   past), regenerate one via the bundled keycloak setup script.
4. Pass the chosen file explicitly to register_entities.py via
   --token-file, so the loader does not silently fall back to a
   stale default.

A new STRESS_SKIP_TOKEN_REFRESH escape hatch lets CI / deployed
runs disable the auto-regeneration step when the bundled Keycloak
generator is not reachable.

README quick-start is simplified to a single command for the
local case and adds an explicit example of the deployed-instance
case (`STRESS_BASE_URL` + `STRESS_TOKEN_FILE` overrides).

* feat(stress): Phase 2 commit 2 -- list-endpoint measurement (#997)

Adds `tests/stress/measure_api_performance.py` with the list-endpoint
measurement loop. Semantic-search operations land in the next commit.

What it measures per entity type (servers, agents, skills):

  - list_<type>_first_page: GET /api/<type>?limit=50&offset=0
  - list_<type>_max_page:   GET /api/<type>?limit=500&offset=0
  - list_<type>_paginated:  walks /api/<type>?limit=50&offset={0..N-1}*50
                            for each iteration

Each operation issues `--iterations + 1` requests (default 51); the
first sample is the warmup discard per the locked Phase 2 plan. Output
JSON carries `warmup_strategy: "discard_first_iteration"` at the top
level and per-operation latency p50/p95/p99/min/max/mean over the
surviving samples. Methodology, warmup rationale, concurrency choice
(serial, per LLD §5.4), and token-refresh policy (401-only) are
documented in the module docstring.

Discovered during the smoke test: the registry's list handlers cap
`limit` at 500 via a Pydantic Field constraint. LLD §5.2 called for an
"all rows" variant; that operation is now `list_<type>_max_page` with a
`notes` field explaining this is "as much as a single request can
return" rather than the full corpus at sizes > 500. The paginated
walkthrough operation is the one that traverses everything.

Token refresh: on a 401 the script invokes
`keycloak/setup/generate-agent-token.sh` once and retries; subsequent
401s fail the request. This matches the resolver convention already in
`run_stress_test.sh`.

Smoke-tested at iterations=5 against the running local stack: 9

For each curated query in `queries.json`, the script issues

  arrays (`servers`, `agents`, `skills`, `tools`, `virtual_servers`).
  `expected_hits` sums the lengths of the arrays whose
  `EXPECTED_TYPE_TO_RESPONSE_KEY` mapping matches the query's expected
  types -- so a `["mcp_server", "skill"]` query reports the union of
  `servers` and `skills` array lengths in the response.

  failing request.

embedding model. If the content is unchanged and an embedding exists,

* fix(terraform): allow auth server to reach mcpgw on port 8003

The mcp-proxy hop (PR #1026) requires auth server to forward MCP
requests to backend servers. For internal services like mcpgw
(ai-registry-tools), a security group ingress rule is needed.
Without this, auth server's connection to mcpgw times out through
Service Connect.

Refs: #1023

* fix(auth): append MCP sub-path to upstream URL in mcp-proxy

The mcp-proxy hop receives server_name as "airegistry-tools/mcp" (the
full path after /mcp-proxy/). The first segment is the registered server
name, everything after the first "/" is the sub-path the client actually
requested (e.g. /mcp, /sse). Append this sub-path to X-Upstream-Url so
the backend receives the correct route.

Without this, auth server would POST to http://mcpgw-server:8003/
instead of http://mcpgw-server:8003/mcp, causing 404s on the backend.

Refs: #1023

* fix(auth): forward Mcp-Session-Id header from upstream through mcp-proxy

The mcp-proxy was returning the response body but stripping all upstream
headers. The MCP streamable-http protocol requires the client to include
the Mcp-Session-Id from the initialize response in all subsequent
requests. Without forwarding this header, clients get "Missing session
ID" errors on their second request (tools/list).

Refs: #1023

* fix(terraform): decouple mcpgw replica count from autoscaling min capacity

mcpgw must run as a single replica because the MCP SDK stores sessions
in per-process memory. Multiple replicas break session affinity when
requests are round-robined by Service Connect. Use the dedicated
mcpgw_replicas variable (default: 1) instead of autoscaling_min_capacity.

The mcpgw server calls registry APIs internally (search, list servers,
list agents, list skills) which require broader scopes than a
resource-bound token provides. Skip the resource binding for the
airegistry-tools server so the Connect button issues a user-scoped
token that has access to all required APIs.

Refs: #1023

* fix(mcpgw): add limit=2000 to list API calls (was defaulting to 20)

* fix(auth): try self-signed token validation before provider-specific

The /validate endpoint was routing directly to the configured auth
provider (Entra, Okta, etc.) without first checking if the token was
minted by this auth server. Tokens generated by the Connect button are
locally-signed JWTs (HS256, iss=mcp-auth-server) that cannot be
validated by external providers (missing 'kid' header, wrong signing
algorithm).

Now the validation checks for self-signed tokens first (by inspecting
the iss claim). If it matches mcp-auth-server, validate locally. Only
fall through to the provider if the token is not self-signed.

When proxy_pass_url already ends with /mcp (e.g. cloudflare docs) and

sub_path and skip appending if the upstream URL already ends with it.

fix(skills): derive SSRF allowlist from github_extra_hosts for GHES

The SKILL.md fetch path enforces an SSRF private-IP check that previously
hard-coded its trusted-domain set to four public hosts (github.com,
gitlab.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, bitbucket.org). GitHub Enterprise
Server (GHES) instances typically resolve to RFC1918 addresses, so even
when GITHUB_EXTRA_HOSTS was configured for auth header injection, every
SKILL.md fetch, health check, and content request to a GHES host failed
SSRF validation before leaving the process.

Replace the static frozenset with _trusted_domains(), which merges the
built-in defaults with hosts parsed from settings.github_extra_hosts.
Reusing that existing setting keeps the trust model consistent: an
operator who has authorised the registry to send GitHub credentials to a
host has, by the same act, declared that host trustworthy enough to skip
the private-IP check.

Refs #938.

test(skills): replace 'in domains' assertions with set ops to silence CodeQL

CodeQL's py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization flags hostname literals
on the right side of `in`, even when the left operand is a frozenset of
trusted hosts rather than a URL. Rewrite assertions in terms of set
equality (==) against _DEFAULT_TRUSTED_DOMAINS, set union (|), and
subset (<=). The new shape is also stricter: equality catches accidental
additions or omissions that per-host membership checks would miss.

No production behaviour changes; tests still cover the same cases.

GitHub.com and GitHub Enterprise Server, completing the resource
discovery feature scaffolded by previous work. Skills with companion
files now have populated resource manifests instead of always-null.

What changed:
- _resolve_tree_api: parses both blob and raw SKILL.md URLs (public
  github.com or GHES), extracts (owner, repo, ref, skill_dir), and
  returns the GitHub Trees API URL with recursive=1.
- _api_base_for_skill_host: maps SKILL.md hostname to its REST API
  base. Public maps to https://api.github.com; GHES maps to the
  configured github_api_base_url only when the host matches.
- _classify_resource: extracted helper with two-tier classification:
  (1) subfolder convention (references/scripts/agents/assets), then
  (2) flat-skill fallback by file extension when files live directly
  under skill_dir. Solves the real-world case where skills (like the
  in-tree usage-report) keep all files at the skill root rather than
  in Anthropic-style subfolders.
- _discover_skill_resources: reads payload["tree"] from the GitHub
  envelope shape (the existing code expected a bare list and would
  bail). Logs a warning when the Trees API truncates. Filters hidden
  files (.DS_Store, __pycache__) within the skill folder without
  rejecting paths in skill_dir itself (e.g. ".claude/skills/...").
  Merges GitHub auth headers via _github_auth.get_auth_headers so
  private repos and rate-limited public repos work.
- Added api.github.com to _DEFAULT_GITHUB_HOSTS so the Trees API call
  receives the configured PAT or GitHub App token.

Live verification against agentic-community/mcp-gateway-registry:

Foundation for the gateway's RFC 9728 / RFC 8414 discovery surface.

* Keycloak ships the real implementation: fetches OIDC config from the

  these in (Cognito needs path-rehoming, Entra v1 scope handling waits on
  sub-issue F / #990).
* New registry/auth/oauth_metadata.py provides pure helpers for the
  upcoming PRM and AS-metadata routes: canonical-URL builder, HTTPS

* New mcp_https_required and mcp_resource_documentation_url settings.

feat(oauth): publish PRM and AS-metadata discovery endpoints (#989)

Adds the two MCP 2025-06-18 / RFC 9728 / RFC 8414 routes:

* GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource returns the gateway's PRM
  document built via the active provider's protected_resource_metadata().
* GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server returns the IdP's RFC 8414
  document via the active provider's authorization_server_metadata().

Both routes:
* Cache for 5 minutes (Cache-Control: public, max-age=300).
* Surface NotImplementedError as 501 (stub providers Cognito/Auth0/Okta/Entra
  remain stubs until commit 4) and upstream IdP failures as 502.
* Enforce HTTPS for the canonical resource URL in non-local environments
  via the new mcp_https_required setting.

Tests cover required RFC 9728 fields, trailing-slash normalization,
HTTPS enforcement, cache-control header, 501 on stub providers, 502 on
upstream failures, and the byte-for-byte match between the PRM `resource`
field and the future WWW-Authenticate `resource_metadata` URL.

feat(oauth): emit WWW-Authenticate on MCP-facing 401s (#989)

Closes the spec gap from RFC 9728 §5.1 + MCP 2025-06-18: a 401 from any
MCP-facing endpoint must point discovery clients at the gateway's PRM
document via the WWW-Authenticate header.

Two emission paths, since 401s come from two layers:

* FastAPI 401s (registry app, /oauth/token + /oauth/authorize when those
  ship in #991): new WWWAuthenticateMiddleware in registry/middleware
  patches the response header on 401s to MCP-facing paths only. Built
  once at startup with the canonical resource_metadata URL so it matches
  the PRM endpoint's `resource` field byte-for-byte. Registered before
  CORSMiddleware so Starlette's LIFO ordering preserves our header.

* Nginx 401s (auth_request failures on /<server>/mcp): @auth_error
  named-location now adds the WWW-Authenticate header. The PRM URL is
  templated via {{MCP_RESOURCE_METADATA_URL}} and substituted at config
  render time in registry/core/nginx_service.py. Both nginx confs
  (http+https and http-only) get the same patch. The placeholder is also
  added to the registry-entrypoint.sh wait loop.

Tests cover: header on 401 for /<server>/mcp, /oauth/token, /oauth/authorize;
no header on 200; no header on 401 for /api/auth/me (out-of-scope path);
no header on 403; byte-for-byte equivalence with the URL passed at init.

test(oauth): spec-faithful end-to-end discovery chain (#989)

Drives the full MCP 2025-06-18 discovery sequence in-process so it runs in
normal CI without docker-compose / live Keycloak:

* Step 1: unauthenticated GET /<server>/mcp returns 401 with
  WWW-Authenticate pointing at the gateway's PRM URL.
* Step 2: client follows resource_metadata to /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource;
  receives the RFC 9728 PRM doc with all required fields.
* Step 3: client follows the gateway's RFC 8414 passthrough at
  /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server; receives a valid AS metadata doc.
* Step 4: client extracts authorization_endpoint and is ready for the
  PKCE auth-code flow (steps 5+ belong to the IdP, out of scope for #989).

Cross-cutting assertion: the PRM `resource` field equals the
WWW-Authenticate `resource_metadata` URL byte-for-byte (acceptance criterion).

Live Keycloak via docker-compose is deliberately deferred. The issue allows
"a fake client that exercises the same sequence" and that's what this is.

fix(oauth): route virtual-server 401s through @auth_error (#989)

Virtual-server location blocks (e.g. /virtual/dev-essentials/mcp) had
auth_request /validate; but were missing the error_page 401 = @auth_error;
directive that regular MCP-server blocks already have. Result: 401s from
the auth_request fell back to nginx's default 401 page, missing the
RFC 9728 WWW-Authenticate header with resource_metadata.

Now virtual-server blocks emit the same WWW-Authenticate header as
regular MCP-server blocks, so spec-compliant clients (Claude Code,
Claude.ai connectors) can auto-discover the gateway's PRM document
when they probe a virtual server.

fix(auth): return 401 not 500 when token validation fails (#989)

The blanket `except Exception` on the provider validation path turned
ValueError (the documented signal that a token is bad: missing kid,
expired, signature mismatch, audience mismatch) into a 500 with
"Authentication provider configuration error".

The 500 broke MCP discovery: nginx propagated the 500 to the client
without going through @auth_error, so spec-compliant clients
(Claude Code, Claude.ai connectors) never saw WWW-Authenticate and
couldn't re-trigger the OAuth flow when their cached token went stale.

Now ValueError -> 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer, which lets
nginx's auth_request 401 handling fire @auth_error and emit the
RFC 9728 header. Other exceptions (network failure, provider
misconfig) remain 500 since those genuinely indicate the gateway
is not in a state where it can ever validate.

Test asserts the regression: a ValueError from validate_token()
surfaces as 401 with a Bearer-scheme WWW-Authenticate header.

fix(oauth): Keycloak URL form, scope override, Entra app-uri allowlist (#989)

Live-testing #989 against Keycloak 25 and Entra v2 surfaced three real
bugs in the discovery surface that this commit fixes.

* Keycloak OIDC discovery URL: Keycloak 25+ serves the spec-correct
  `.well-known/openid-configuration` (hyphen) form; the legacy
  `openid_configuration` (underscore) form returns 404. Without this,
  PRM and AS-metadata 502 on any modern Keycloak deployment.

* New `mcp_advertised_scopes` setting overrides the PRM `scopes_supported`
  array. Required when the IdP performs RFC 7591 Dynamic Client
  Registration and rejects registration requests containing scope names
  it doesn't recognize (e.g. registry-internal group names like
  `mcp-registry-admin`). Operators set it to a space-separated list of
  scopes the IdP knows: `MCP_ADVERTISED_SCOPES="profile email offline_access"`.
  When unset, behavior is unchanged (full union from registry config).

* New `mcp_prm_resource_override` setting allows the PRM `resource` field
  to be set independently of `resource_metadata` URL. Reserved for future
  CIMD work and operators with non-default audience identifiers; the
  default behavior (resource = canonical gateway URL) is RFC 8707-correct.

* Entra audience validation: read `ENTRA_APPLICATION_ID_URI` env var and
  add it to the accepted audience list in addition to the existing
  `[client_id, api://client_id]` pair. Lets operators register the gateway
  URL as an Entra Application ID URI when their tenant supports it.

* Tests: 4 new tests covering the override path; existing tests updated
  to patch the new setting. 91 tests pass in the #989 suite.

Validated live against Keycloak 25 with DCR end-to-end:
  PRM discovery -> AS metadata fetch -> registration_endpoint POST (201) ->
  /authorize -> user login -> Keycloak issues auth code.

fix(oauth): aud-claim fallback for DCR'd Keycloak clients; drop unused override (#989)

Two changes from this afternoon's live testing against Keycloak:

1. Soften `auth_server/providers/keycloak.py` token validation: when the
   strict `aud`-checked decode fails with `MissingRequiredClaimError` or
   `InvalidAudienceError`, fall back to issuer-only validation. This is
   needed because Keycloak does NOT include an `aud` claim on tokens minted
   for RFC 7591 dynamically-registered clients by default, and our PRM-driven
   DCR flow with Claude Code produces exactly such tokens. Safe because the
   issuer match already proves the token came from our trusted realm, and
   the `azp` claim identifies which DCR'd client minted it. Production
   deployments that want strict audience binding can configure a Keycloak
   audience mapper and the strict-decode path will be taken.

2. Remove the unused `MCP_PRM_RESOURCE_OVERRIDE` setting. We added it
   earlier today as scaffolding for an Entra `api://<app-id>` workaround,
   but Claude Code rejects PRM `resource` values that aren't the canonical
   gateway URL or origin (RFC 9728 §3.1). The setting had no remaining
   use case and added a misconfiguration surface.

Live-tested end-to-end against Keycloak with Claude Code on Windows:
DCR -> /authorize -> login -> /token -> POST /airegistry-tools/mcp ->
gateway validates groups-claim -> per-user scope gate passes -> tools
listed. With the `roles` client-scope's groups-mapper enabled
(operator-side Keycloak config), `MCP_ADVERTISED_SCOPES` is reduced to
just OIDC standards (`profile email offline_access`); per-user
authorization comes from the existing `map_groups_to_scopes` path that
the session-cookie validator already uses.

feat(keycloak): DCR support in init-keycloak + upgrade script + 100/200/300/400 doc (#989)

The afternoon's live testing surfaced three Keycloak realm config items
required for MCP Dynamic Client Registration to actually work end-to-end:

1. Groups protocol mapper on the `basic` client-scope (the only scope that's
   reliably attached to every DCR'd client)
2. Anonymous DCR `Allowed Client Scopes` policy widened to include all realm
   scopes
3. Anonymous DCR `Trusted Hosts` policy with IP check off, URI check on,
   `localhost` allowed

These three changes are now applied automatically:

- `keycloak/setup/init-keycloak.sh` gets three new functions

  `configure_dcr_trusted_hosts`) called from main() so fresh installs work
  out of the box
- `keycloak/setup/upgrade-realm-for-dcr.sh` is a new standalone idempotent
  script that applies the same three changes to an existing realm. Tested
  idempotent against the live deployment

`docs/keycloak.md` is a new four-level explanation of how the entire
discovery + DCR + OAuth + per-user-authorization flow works on Keycloak,
with sequence diagrams and real captured payloads (PRM doc, AS metadata,
DCR registration request/response, authorize URL, callback URL, token
request/response, decoded access_token claims). Levels 100 and 200 are the
mental model; level 300 is the wire sequence; level 400 covers every
Keycloak knob and gateway code path with pointers to where to look when
things break.

The doc explicitly captures what is NOT production-safe (anonymous DCR with
relaxed Trusted Hosts, the aud-fallback in the validator, the leftover
realm-default scope grants from earlier in the session) so future hardening

test(cognito): use parsed-host equality, not substring `in` (CodeQL #1115)

CodeQL flagged test_cognito.py:67 under py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization
because the assertion `"...amazoncognito.com" in metadata["token_endpoint"]`
matches the same anti-pattern that lets attackers craft URLs like
`https://evil.com/...amazoncognito.com/foo` to bypass naive substring checks.
Static analysis can't tell the test from production code, so the rule
fires regardless of context.

Fixed by parsing each URL with `urllib.parse.urlsplit` and comparing the
hostname for exact equality. Also preemptively converted the `startswith`
host checks in test_endpoints_rehomed_onto_cognito_domain to the same
parsed-host pattern, since `startswith` against an unparsed URL has the
same logical weakness even when CodeQL doesn't flag it today.

Test semantics are stricter, not weaker: a malformed URL or a host-spoofing
variant that satisfied the old `in`/`startswith` check would now fail.

feat(observability): native OTel meter modules + path-3 counter migration (#1122)

Phase A of the OTel-native metrics migration. Introduces a new pair of
meter modules (registry/observability/meters.py and auth_server/observability/
meters.py) that own the global OpenTelemetry MeterProvider for each service
and declare every instrument at module scope.

The 19 in-process Prometheus counters/gauges scattered across
registry/core/metrics.py, registry/auth/routes.py, registry/auth/session_store.py,
and registry/api/m2m_management_routes.py are migrated to native OTel
Counter / Histogram / ObservableGauge instruments. Existing call sites that
use METRIC.labels(k=v).inc() or .set(value) keep working unchanged via the
_CounterAdapter / _HistogramAdapter / _UpDownCounterAdapter shims in
registry/observability/_compat.py.

Names are preserved verbatim so existing Grafana dashboards and PromQL
alerts continue to function.

Notable changes:
- peer_token_missing_total Gauge was confirmed dead at migration time (zero
  call sites). Removed rather than migrated. Follow-up #1124 covers naming-
  convention enforcement if a real call site is added later.
- DEPLOYMENT_MODE_INFO is now an OTel ObservableGauge whose callback reads
  the current deployment mode on every export cycle. The legacy Gauge import
  is preserved as a no-op shim for backward compatibility.
- peer_sync_duration_seconds was a Prometheus Gauge whose only call sites
  used .labels().set(duration). Migrated to an OTel Histogram (correct
  semantics) with the _HistogramAdapter translating the legacy API.

Two new config settings:
- METRICS_LEGACY_HTTP_POST (default false): one-release transition flag.
  When true, services dual-write to metrics-service and the OTel SDK.

fix(observability): bootstrap OTel SDK + Prometheus exporter when OTLP_ENDPOINT is unset (#1122)

Real bug surfaced by Compose smoke test: the :9464/metrics listener never
started, ``curl registry:9464/metrics`` returned ``Connection refused``,
and Prometheus failed to scrape any of the three services.

Root cause: the docker entrypoints only enable ``opentelemetry-instrument``
when ``OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`` is set. When unset (the default for
Option 1 / Prometheus pull), the OTel SDK is never bootstrapped at all,
so ``metrics.get_meter_provider()`` returns ``_ProxyMeterProvider`` and
the env vars ``OTEL_EXPORTER_PROMETHEUS_HOST`` / ``_PORT`` are read by
nothing. Phase A's meter modules were emitting into the void.

Fix: in both ``registry/observability/meters.py`` and
``auth_server/observability/meters.py``, add a module-import-time
``_init_meter_provider_if_needed()`` helper. When
``OTEL_EXPORTER_PROMETHEUS_HOST`` is set AND no real ``MeterProvider``
is already installed:

1. Start the prometheus_client HTTP server on host:port.
2. Install a ``PrometheusMetricReader`` on a real ``MeterProvider``.
3. Set it as the global provider.

This is a no-op when:
- ``OTEL_EXPORTER_PROMETHEUS_HOST`` is unset (operator hasn't opted in).
- A real ``MeterProvider`` is already installed (e.g., by
  ``opentelemetry-instrument`` doing its job).

The existing OTLP-push code path is unchanged: when
``OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`` is set, the entrypoint wraps uvicorn with
``opentelemetry-instrument`` which installs its own provider; the helper
detects that real provider and bows out. Both paths can also run together
(Prometheus pull + OTLP push) with no conflict.

Also fixes the ``_log_otel_state()`` helper in registry/main.py and
auth_server/server.py to recognize ``_ProxyMeterProvider`` as the
"OTel disabled" state and emit a WARNING (was incorrectly emitting INFO
in that case).

holds.

feat(observability): HTTP auto-instrumentation + per-tool metrics for mcpgw (#1122)

Two follow-on enhancements after the registry middleware fix:

1) Programmatic FastAPI auto-instrumentation in registry and auth-server
   (Option A from the design discussion). Calls
   ``FastAPIInstrumentor.instrument_app(app)`` once after each FastAPI
   app is created. Emits the OpenTelemetry HTTP semantic-convention
   metrics (``http.server.duration`` Histogram, ``http.server.active_requests``
   UpDownCounter) and per-route spans with attributes including
   ``http.route`` (template form, low cardinality), ``http.method``,
   ``http.status_code``. Works whether or not opentelemetry-instrument
   is wrapping uvicorn at startup.

   PromQL examples enabled by this:

   - rate per route:
     sum by (http_route)(rate(http_server_duration_milliseconds_count[5m]))
   - p95 latency per route:
     histogram_quantile(0.95,
       sum by (le, http_route)(rate(http_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket[5m])))
   - 5xx error rate:
     sum(rate(http_server_duration_milliseconds_count{http_status_code=~"5.."}[5m]))

2) Per-tool metrics for mcpgw via a new ``track_tool`` decorator in
   ``servers/mcpgw/observability_bootstrap.py``. Applied underneath each
   ``@mcp.tool()`` decorator on all six mcpgw tools (list_services,
   list_agents, list_skills, get_skill_content, intelligent_tool_finder,
   healthcheck). Emits:

   - mcpgw_tool_invocations_total{tool, success}  Counter
   - mcpgw_tool_duration_ms{tool, success}        Histogram

   ``success`` is "True" on normal return, "False" if the tool raised.
   Cardinality is bounded: one series per (tool_name × {True, False}).

   PromQL examples enabled by this:

   - Tool QPS:        rate(mcpgw_tool_invocations_total[5m])
   - Tool error rate: sum by (tool)(rate(mcpgw_tool_invocations_total{success="False"}[5m]))
   - Tool p95:        histogram_quantile(0.95,
                        sum by (le, tool)(rate(mcpgw_tool_duration_ms_bucket[5m])))

Both layers are no-ops when the OTel SDK isn't initialized, and both
share the OTel-Prometheus pipeline already wired in by Phase A and the
OTLP push pipeline omrishiv's PR #1099 added. No new env vars introduced.

fix(observability): drop unit suffix from histogram names to avoid double suffix (#1122)

The OTel-to-Prometheus exporter appends the OTel ``unit=`` annotation to
the metric name when exporting (e.g. ``unit="ms"`` -> ``_milliseconds``).
Our histograms had ``_ms`` / ``_seconds`` already in the name AND a
``unit=`` annotation, producing doubled-suffix Prometheus names like
``mcpgw_tool_duration_ms_milliseconds_bucket`` and
``auth_request_duration_ms_milliseconds_bucket``.

Per OTel semantic conventions, the unit lives in the ``unit=`` annotation,
not in the name. Drop the redundant suffix from each histogram declaration
across all three services. The Prometheus exporter still appends the unit
once during export, so operators see a single, clean ``_milliseconds`` /
``_seconds`` suffix.

Renames (declaration -> Prometheus exposition):

- auth_request_duration_ms       -> auth_request_duration_milliseconds_*
- tool_execution_duration_ms     -> tool_execution_duration_milliseconds_*
- protocol_latency_ms            -> protocol_latency_milliseconds_*
- registry_operation_duration_ms -> registry_operation_duration_milliseconds_*
- tool_discovery_duration_ms     -> tool_discovery_duration_milliseconds_*
- peer_sync_duration_seconds     -> peer_sync_duration_seconds_* (idempotent
                                    in the wire form because the exporter's
                                    suffix matches the convention)
- mcpgw_tool_duration_ms         -> mcpgw_tool_duration_milliseconds_*

Python attribute names (e.g. ``auth_request_duration_ms``) are kept as-is
to avoid touching every call site. Only the OTel ``name=`` argument
changes. Counters are unaffected (their ``unit="1"`` produces no
exporter-side suffix).

No dashboards or alerts reference the doubled-suffix form yet, so this
is a safe rename. PromQL queries documented in the LLD and PR body now
target the canonical single-suffix names.

Tests: 26 unit tests pass; the renames are visible only at the
Prometheus exposition layer, not in the Python API surface that tests
exercise.

fix(observability): add OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* env vars to compose service blocks (#1122)

Without these in the environment block, putting OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
in .env had no effect — Docker Compose only injects env vars into a
service's process environment if they appear in the service's
``environment:`` list (or are sourced from env_file). The OTel SDK reads
the standard OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT name from the process
environment, so the var has to be wired into all three application
service blocks to activate the OTLP push exporter.

Adds three env vars to the registry, auth-server, and mcpgw blocks:

- OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (default empty; setting it activates OTLP push)
- OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL (default grpc; alternative is http/protobuf)
- OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS (default empty; for backends that need auth tokens)

Verified end-to-end: with OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4317
in .env and the new collector container running, the otel-collector log
shows metrics + traces (MongoDB spans, FastAPI HTTP spans, custom
counters and histograms) arriving from all three services within ~15s of
the OTel SDK flush interval.

This was the missing wire-up between the .env line and the containers —
the env var reached compose-config but not the running processes until
each service's environment block listed it.

KC23 DCR does not auto-attach the 'basic' client-scope to dynamically
registered clients, so tokens lack the 'aud' claim. KC25 fixes this.
Also migrates deprecated KC23 env vars (KC_PROXY=edge, KC_HOSTNAME_URL,

KC_HOSTNAME, KC_HTTP_ENABLED). The DCR realm setup script is made

fix(docker): add IPv4 precedence for Service Connect dual-stack resolution (#1122)

ECS Service Connect injects both IPv4 (127.255.0.x) and IPv6
(2600:f0f0::x) entries in /etc/hosts. glibc RFC 6724 default prefers
IPv6 which is unreachable, causing nginx proxy_pass and httpx calls to
fail with 'network unreachable'. Adding 'precedence ::ffff:0:0/96 100'
to /etc/gai.conf at build time forces IPv4 preference. Also moves the
nginx pid path fix from entrypoint to Dockerfile build time.

fix(registry): async federation sync with timeout and nginx reload retry (#1122)

Federation sync on ECS was blocking the lifespan startup past nginx
health-check timeout (Anthropic endpoint ~30s/server). Wraps sync in
asyncio.wait_for with 60s timeout and asyncio.to_thread for the blocking
httpx calls. Also adds a retry loop in nginx_service.reload_nginx() for
the 'invalid PID number' race when nginx has not yet written its pidfile.

feat(dedup): advisory cross-entity registration deduplication (#913)

Adds an advisory duplicate-check pre-flight to MCP server, A2A agent,
and skill registration. When a user submits a new entity, the registry
surfaces likely duplicates so the user can pick the existing one,
edit, or proceed anyway. The check never blocks: /check-duplicates
always returns 200 and /register never invokes the service.

1. URL collision: the entity's identity URL (proxy_pass_url for
  servers, url for agents, skill_md_url for skills) is normalized
  per each target repo's rule and looked up in all three. With the
  indexed sidecar field (see below), each lookup is one $eq query.
2. Similarity: a single semantic-search call returning hits across
  all three entity types, ranked, threshold-filtered, visibility-
  filtered, capped at dedup_max_suggestions.

Each ExistingEntity in the response carries its own entity_type so
the UI can route the View button to the correct dashboard tab.

Each DocumentDB document stores _identity_url_normalized populated
from the user-facing URL field at insert/update time. A sparse index
on the sidecar makes find_by_identity_url an O(1) indexed $eq lookup
— no scan, no client-side normalization loop. The user-facing URL
fields are untouched, so the document shape returned to API consumers
is unchanged.

The shared work (populate, ensure-index, backfill, find) lives in a
new _identity_url_sidecar module so the three repos don't carry
identical 80-line blocks.

Existing documents are backfilled lazily on first collection
acquisition, guarded by an asyncio.Lock so concurrent first calls
don't both run the cursor. The sidecar is projected out server-side
in the lookup helper so a future raw-doc API can't accidentally
expose it.

When the caller cannot view a colliding entity, the entry's
path/name/owner are blanked but the entry still appears so the user
knows a collision exists. Advisory matches the caller can't view
are dropped silently. Missing visibility on a doc is treated
as private, not public; the rare legacy/externally-inserted row
without the field stays hidden until an operator re-saves it.

Two paths: callers can pass self_path explicitly (the UI does this
for re-registration), and the service auto-excludes when the
matching document was registered by the same user. The owner-based
exclusion makes the API robust for external callers (CLI,
federation, CI) that don't track their own paths.

Three env vars (collapsed from the 8 in the original PR draft):

- DEDUP_REGISTRATION_HINT_ENABLED (bool, default true) — frontend
  opt-out for the pre-flight. Endpoints stay reachable regardless.
- DEDUP_SCORE_THRESHOLD (float, default 0.7) — minimum semantic-
  search score for advisory matches.
- DEDUP_MAX_SUGGESTIONS (int, default 3) — cap on advisory
  suggestions.

Wired across .env.example, all four Helm charts (registry +
auth-server + mcpgw + parent stack including reserved-env-names.txt
and secret.yaml), and Terraform (root + module variables,
ecs-services container env, tfvars example).

New entity-agnostic useDuplicateCheck hook + DuplicateCheckModal
component. The hook returns one of three outcomes per call:

- show-modal: matches found, render modal.
- proceed: caller invokes /register. Covers no-hits, flag-off, and
  network failure.
- cancelled: another runCheck superseded this one or the component
  unmounted. Caller MUST NOT proceed (prevents stale registration
  POSTs after navigation).

AbortController cancels in-flight requests on unmount and supersede.
The modal title and copy describe the actual matches' entity types,
not the registering type, so a server registration surfacing a skill
hit reads "Similar 1 skill found" rather than "Similar 1 server".
Heterogeneous lists fall back to entity-agnostic copy ("2 entries").

The DuplicateCheckModal layers above z-50 host modals (z-[60]) so
the dedup hint fires correctly from inside the skill registration
modal. Picking a cross-entity match navigates with both ?highlight=
and ?tab= so the dashboard switches to the matched entity's list,
and closes the host registration modal so the user isn't stranded
on a stale draft.

Server, agent, and skill registration UIs are all wired through the
hook. Skill edits skip the check (only saves of new skills go
through it).

Worker ownership uses MongoDB leases (claimed_by + lease_expires_at) renewed
by heartbeat, replacing orphan recovery. Any number of replicas may run the
worker concurrently and cooperatively drain the queue; a lapsed lease lets
another worker reclaim a job and resume from next_index.

Patch items drop None fields instead of relying on exclude_unset: a job is
persisted to and reloaded from MongoDB before the worker runs, and a model
rebuilt from a full dict has every field marked "set", which would otherwise
null out required fields on the existing card during the merge.

Also adds PATCH /api/agents/{path} (RFC 7396 merge patch) and weak ETags
(RFC 7232) on agent GET/PATCH for optimistic concurrency.

Configurable via BATCH_* settings (worker enabled, max ops/job, concurrency
per user, retention, poll interval, lease TTL/heartbeat, max request bytes)
across config, Helm, Docker Compose, and Terraform/ECS surfaces.

feat(gitlab): translate GitLab /-/raw/ URLs to API v4 for private repos

GitLab's /-/raw/ web URLs require session cookies, so they cannot be
fetched from a private repository with only a Personal Access Token.
The API v4 raw file endpoint (/api/v4/projects/:id/repository/files/
:path/raw) accepts a PRIVATE-TOKEN header instead, which is what the
registry already configures via auth_credential.

This change adds a new optional helper module, registry/utils/
gitlab_url_utils.py, that:

  * parses both /-/raw/ web URLs and API v4 raw-file URLs into their
    base, project, ref and filepath components;
  * translates a /-/raw/ URL to the equivalent API v4 raw-file URL so
    that PRIVATE-TOKEN auth works for private projects;
  * derives sibling resource URLs (e.g. files referenced from a
    SKILL.md) using the same API v4 endpoint and proper percent
    encoding; and
  * builds a recursive tree API URL so multi-file skill discovery
    works against GitLab the same way it does against GitHub.

The hook points in skill_service._build_fetch_headers,
skill_service._resolve_tree_api and url_utils.derive_resource_url
import gitlab_url_utils defensively (try/except ImportError) and fall
through to the existing GitHub / raw URL behaviour when the helper is
absent or the URL is not GitLab-shaped. Removing gitlab_url_utils.py
therefore leaves the upstream GitHub features fully functional.

Tests:
  * tests/unit/utils/test_gitlab_url_utils.py — 20 unit tests covering
    parsing, translation, sibling-resource derivation, tree API
    construction, idempotency on API v4 input, and None fall-through
    for empty / non-GitLab / blob-style URLs.

fix(search): replace broken additive scoring with Reciprocal Rank Fusion

The existing hybrid search formula saturated all relevance scores to 1.0
because cosine similarity (0-1) and uncapped text_boost (0-40+) were
added together and clamped. This made search results indistinguishable
and caused documents without embeddings to be invisible.

Replace with RRF (k=60), the industry standard used by Elasticsearch,
OpenSearch, MongoDB Atlas, and Azure AI Search. RRF combines independent
vector and keyword ranked lists by ordinal position, avoiding all
normalization issues and handling missing embeddings gracefully.

Add SEARCH_FUSION_METHOD config (default "rrf", set to "legacy" to
revert) so deployments can A/B test without code changes.
