feat(nginx): optional IPv6 listeners for IPv6-only clusters

The in-pod nginx reverse proxy ships IPv4-only listen directives
(listen 8080; / listen 8443 ssl;). An IPv4 socket never accepts IPv6
connections, so on IPv6-only Kubernetes clusters the load balancer and
kubelet readiness probe (which reach the pod over its IPv6 address on
:8080) cannot connect and the registry never becomes Ready.

uvicorn already supports IPv6 via BIND_HOST=::, but nginx did not. Add
an opt-in NGINX_ENABLE_IPV6 env var (default false) handled in
registry-entrypoint.sh: when true, the entrypoint appends
'listen [::]:8080;' (and [::]:8443 ssl;) to the generated config after
the template is copied and before nginx starts.

Default false means no behavior change for existing IPv4-only hosts,
where binding [::] would fail. Document the new var in .env.example and
docs/unified-parameter-reference.md.

fix(ui): handle strict-canonical server.json on JSON upload (#1178)

The upstream MCP Registry server.json detector only fired on a $schema
field containing 'modelcontextprotocol/registry'. $schema is optional in
the spec, so a strictly-canonical file (reverse-DNS name, remotes[],
namespaced _meta) without it slipped through and the form left Path,
Proxy URL, Tags, and Auth Scheme empty.

Widen the detector to also fire on structural signals: reverse-DNS name
match, Array.isArray(remotes) or Array.isArray(packages), or any _meta
key containing '/' (reverse-DNS namespacing).

Add a _meta unpacking step: any _meta key ending in '/internal' (e.g.
ai.agenticshelf.registry/internal, com.example.registry/internal) is
treated as the registry's own previously-exported state. Fields inside
it (path, tags, license, deployment, proxy_pass_url,
supported_transports, auth_scheme, auth_provider, visibility,
allowed_groups, status, provider_organization, provider_url) populate
the form when the upload doesn't already specify them at the top level.
Nested vendor metadata flows into the form's metadata textarea on the
same condition.

Top-level values in the upload always win over _meta values — caller
intent beats round-trip state.

No regression on:
- Files with $schema set (existing transform still runs).
- The hybrid example cli/examples/standard_server_example.json (its
  _meta keys end in /publisher-provided, not /internal).
- The registry's own bespoke shape on re-upload (no name match, no
  remotes, no _meta -> detector returns false, legacy path runs).

fix(api): order generic /servers/{path} PUT/PATCH after specific subpaths

registered before the more specific routes
PATCH /servers/{path:path}/auth-credential and
PUT /servers/{path:path}/versions/default. FastAPI matches routes in
registration order, so the broad routes captured every request and
returned 422 (extra-field validation) for the dedicated endpoints.

Move both new handlers to immediately before the catch-all
GET /servers/{path:path} so all specific subpath routes are evaluated
first. Caught by integration testing of backwards-compat (Test 2.1.3
in testing.md).

fix(api): persist visibility=public on /servers/register and normalize absent on GET (#1181)

POST /api/servers/register had two related defects:

1. Silent drop of the default value. When the caller sent
   visibility="public" (the form default and the most common value),
   the handler omitted the field from the persisted document. GET
   responses then surfaced "visibility": null, leaking a storage
   optimization into the API contract and looking broken to clients.

2. No validation. Unlike the legacy POST /register handler, this one
   never called _validate_visibility_and_groups(). visibility=garbage
   was stored verbatim, and visibility=group-restricted with no
   allowed_groups was accepted without an error, producing a broken
   access-control state.

Write-side fix: call _validate_visibility_and_groups() to normalize
the value, reject unknown values with HTTP 400, and enforce that
group-restricted carries at least one allowed_group. Always persist
the validated visibility. The allowed_groups parsing and storage
rule (only store when non-empty) is unchanged; the variable is just
renamed to match the legacy handler.

Read-side fix: GET /api/servers/{path} and GET /api/servers default
absent visibility to "public". This mirrors the existing pattern
already in place for agents, search, and federation responses, and
corrects the response for servers registered before the write-side
fix landed so no data migration is needed.

Tests:
- TestServerRegisterVisibility covers all four write-side acceptance
  criteria from #1181 (persist public, reject garbage, reject
  group-restricted without groups, persist group-restricted with
  groups).
- TestServerGetVisibilityNormalization covers both read-side
  endpoints with legacy docs that lack the field.

Fixture extension: mock_faiss_service.save_data is now AsyncMock so
the POST handler's asyncio.create_task(save_data()) post-success
hook doesn't 500 the request under test.

fix(api): canonicalize agent_access wildcards so "all agents" actually grants access (#1189)

The original PR #1189 added a "* (All agents)" entry to the IAM group
Agent Access picker with value="*". On the server side,
_normalize_agent_paths_in_scope_config ran every agent_access entry
through _normalize_agent_path, which unconditionally prepends "/" to
non-leading-slash inputs. Result: "*" was stored as "/*" — a literal
path no agent has. The downstream filter at agent_routes.py:374 and
the visibility check at visibility.py:76 both only match the literal
string "all", so the group silently filtered every agent.

Confirmed live against the running stack:

  scope:        test-all-agents
  agent_access: ["/*"]                  <- stored, broken
  ui_permissions.list_agents: ["/*"]    <- stored, broken
  log line:     "User ashdpras listed 0 agents (total: 0)"

Two changes pin this down:

1. Normalizer: any spelling of the agent wildcard ("all", "*", "/*")
   collapses to the canonical "all" before storage. ui_permissions
   already special-cased "all" only; that path now uses the same
   helper and recognizes "*"/"/*" too. Wildcard duplicates are
   deduped so ["*", "all"] -> ["all"], not ["all", "all"].

2. Frontend dropdown: value changes from "*" to "all" so the picked
   value already matches the canonical form on the wire. The label
   ("* (All agents)") and description are unchanged.

Existing broken scopes (e.g. test-all-agents itself) self-repair on
the next save through the management API; the operator can also fix
them in place with a one-shot Mongo update.

Tests in TestAgentWildcardNormalization cover the helper directly
plus the four-shape matrix (all, *, /*, literal path) across both
agent_access and ui_permissions, including the dedup case and the
mixed-input case.

* feat(pingfederate): docker compose integration with init script

- Switch PingFederate server profile to baseline/pingfederate (working
  HTML Form adapter, simple PCV, JWT ATM out of the box)
- Mount custom run.properties to enable HTTP on port 9032 (avoids
  self-signed cert plumbing in dev)
- Add init-pingfederate.sh to configure OAuth client, scopes, test
  users, auth policy, and access token mapping idempotently
- Parameterize nginx PingFederate proxy blocks with PINGFEDERATE_SCHEME
  /HOST/PORT placeholders, wrapped in {{PINGFEDERATE_LOCATIONS_*}}
  conditional markers (mirrors Keycloak pattern)
- Strip PingFederate location blocks from nginx config when
  AUTH_PROVIDER != pingfederate
- Add /as/, /assets/, /pf/, /ext/, /.well-known/openid-configuration
  proxy locations gated on AUTH_PROVIDER=pingfederate
- Gitignore the runtime-generated PingFederate CA bundle

* feat(pingfederate): user-group fallback, PF admin-API M2M client creation, deployment surface wiring

Builds on issue #1127. Adds the user-side mirror of idp_m2m_clients
(idp_user_groups) so PingFederate users whose JWTs come back with
empty groups can still be authorized, and wires the registry to call
PF's admin API to create OAuth clients and Simple PCV users from the
IAM admin UI.

Backend:
- New idp_user_groups MongoDB collection, Pydantic schemas, service,
  and admin-only CRUD at /api/iam/user-groups, mirroring the m2m
  pattern. Auth-server enrichment reads it when an IdP in the
  IDP_USER_GROUP_FALLBACK_ENABLED_PROVIDERS allowlist returns empty
  groups; default allowlist is just pingfederate so other IdPs are
  unaffected. Provider-specific scope re-mapping after enrichment is
  also gated on data.provider == "pingfederate".
- New PingFederateIAMManager wired into get_iam_manager() so the
  "Create M2M Account" admin flow works against PF (creates an
  OAuth2 CLIENT_CREDENTIALS client via the PF admin API). Group
  membership for M2M tokens lives in idp_m2m_clients (existing
  pattern, no PF-side group attachment needed).
- New POST /api/iam/user-groups/{username}/pingfederate-user
  endpoint upserts a Simple PCV user via the PF admin API, gated on
  AUTH_PROVIDER=pingfederate and the fallback allowlist.
- /api/config now returns auth_provider,
  idp_user_group_fallback_enabled_providers,
  user_group_management_enabled, and
  pingfederate_user_management_enabled so the frontend can gate the
  IAM tab and checkbox without baking provider names into the UI.

Frontend:
- New IAM > User Groups tab with paginated CRUD over
  idp_user_groups and an opt-in "Also create this user in
  PingFederate (Simple PCV)" checkbox in the Register form. The
  whole tab is hidden unless the active provider is in the fallback
  allowlist; the checkbox is hidden unless the active provider is
  exactly pingfederate. M2M page help text updated to include
  PingFederate alongside the other admin-API providers.

Deployment surfaces (4 surfaces, 1:1 parameter parity):
- .env.example, docker-compose{,.podman,.prebuilt}.yml: registry
  service block now reads PF_ADMIN_URL/USER/PASS and
  IDP_USER_GROUP_FALLBACK_ENABLED_PROVIDERS.
- charts/registry: new pingfederateAdmin.{url,user,password,
  passwordExistingSecret*} values; chart-managed secret emits
  PF_ADMIN_PASS when password is set, deployment uses secretKeyRef

- terraform/aws-ecs: new pf_admin_url/user/pass variables, a

  parameters.

CLI / SDK:
- api/registry_client.py: new IdPUserGroup,
  UserGroupListResponse, PingFederateUserCreateResponse models and
  six SDK methods on RegistryClient (register/list/get/patch/delete
  user-group, create_pingfederate_user). get_config docstring
  updated.
- api/registry_management.py: matching CLI subcommands
  user-group-{create,list,get,update,delete} and
  pingfederate-user-create (password via getpass; never on the
  command line).

Operations:
- nginx config: /idp/ proxy block added inside the
  PINGFEDERATE_LOCATIONS_START/END fence so PF's startSLO.ping
  works; fence is stripped when AUTH_PROVIDER != pingfederate.
- pingfederate/setup/init-pingfederate.sh: Step 8 seeds
  idp_user_groups for the bundled admin and testuser test users
  (admin -> registry-admins, testuser -> public-mcp-users). Step
  counters updated 7 -> 8.
- docs/idp/pingfederate.md: replaces docs/pingfederate.md;
  restructured around the three deployment modes (Docker Compose
  with bundled PF, Terraform/ECS BYO, Helm BYO) with a single
  cross-surface variable reference table at the top. mkdocs.yml
  updated; in-code doc references updated to the new path.

Out of scope: bundled PingFederate Pod/Task on Helm or ECS. Both
modes are BYO PingFederate; only Docker Compose can run a local PF
container, behind the existing pingfederate Docker Compose profile.

* test(management-api): use idp group cmds and direct get lookups in e2e script

Switch the e2e script to the create-group/delete-group --idp command names so
the group is created in and removed from Keycloak, matching the user steps that
add members to it. Replace the paginated list/agent-list checks with direct
server-get/agent-get lookups by path, which avoids false failures when a freshly
registered server or agent is not on the first page of results.

* docs(readme): add What's New entry for PingFederate IdP support

* fix(nginx): always parse KEYCLOAK_URL and guard PingFederate URL parsing

The PingFederate branch inverted the Keycloak config logic: KEYCLOAK_URL was
only parsed when the active provider was PingFederate, so Keycloak deployments
fell back to the http://keycloak:8080 default and lost their configured URL in
the generated nginx config. Decouple the two concerns so the PingFederate
location blocks are stripped based on AUTH_PROVIDER while KEYCLOAK_URL is always
parsed to fill the Keycloak template placeholders.

Also wrap the PingFederate URL parsing in the same try/except fallback used for
Keycloak so a malformed PINGFEDERATE_BASE_URL cannot crash config generation,
and drop the redundant local os/urlparse imports in favor of the module-level
ones.

* fix(build): fail loudly when build-config.yaml parsing fails

The image parser ran inside a command substitution, so the python3 heredoc's
exit status was discarded. When the active python3 lacked PyYAML (e.g. a
non-project virtualenv/conda env on PATH), the import error went to stderr but
the loop simply read no input, leaving the image list empty. That surfaced as a
misleading 'Image not found: registry' / 'Available images:' (blank) instead of
the real cause.

Capture the parser output and exit status separately, abort with a clear error
if parsing fails or yields no images, and add an explicit PyYAML import guard
that names the offending interpreter and how to fix it.

* docs(pingfederate): correct Terraform provider switch (no auth_provider var)

The Terraform/ECS module selects the auth provider via boolean *_enabled flags,
not an auth_provider string variable (that name only exists on the Docker .env
and Helm values.yaml surfaces). The pingfederate.md guide told readers to set
auth_provider = "pingfederate" in terraform.tfvars, which fails terraform plan
with an undeclared-variable error.

- pingfederate.md: drop the auth_provider line from the Terraform example, fix
  the variable-reference table row, and add a note explaining the Docker/Helm
  string vs Terraform boolean distinction.
- terraform.tfvars.example: rewrite the auth-provider header to state there is
  no auth_provider variable, list all five providers (was three), correct the
  precedence order (pingfederate > auth0 > okta > entra > keycloak), and add a
  provider-selector block with every *_enabled flag commented out so only the
  default Keycloak provider is active.

* docs(pingfederate): clarify single-provider model, drop precedence chain

Reframe the Terraform auth-provider guidance around the actual operating model:
enable exactly one provider via its *_enabled flag, and if none are enabled
Keycloak is the default. Removes the 'pingfederate > auth0 > okta > entra >
keycloak' precedence phrasing, which read as if multiple providers were
expected. Keeps a short footnote that the Keycloak default applies when a
Keycloak domain is configured (which the standard use_regional_domains setup
does).

* fix(nginx): defer DNS for unresolvable virtual-server backends (#1206)

A virtual server backend whose proxy_pass_url host is not resolvable in the
current environment (e.g. a docker-compose service name like currenttime-server
on ECS) was emitted as a literal proxy_pass. Nginx resolves literal upstream
hosts at config load and aborts with 'host not found in upstream', which takes
down the registry container (nginx is its main process) in an endless restart
loop. One bad backend crashed the whole gateway.

_generate_virtual_backend_locations now emits a literal proxy_pass only for
hosts that are safe to resolve at startup (FQDNs with a dot, or IP literals),
keeping the zero-per-request-DNS fast path for the common external-host case.
Bare hostnames are passed through a variable with a resolver so nginx resolves
them at request time; an unresolvable backend then degrades to a per-request
502 for that backend instead of crashing the gateway at boot.

Regular (non-virtual) server blocks were never affected: they proxy_pass to the
fixed auth_server host and carry the real backend only in the X-Upstream-Url
header, which nginx does not resolve at config load.

Adds a _is_host_resolvable_at_startup helper (replaces an inline substring
check) with direct unit tests, plus a test for the bare-hostname deferred-
resolution path.

* feat(terraform): add Amazon Cognito as an auth provider for aws-ecs

Wire Cognito (bring-your-own User Pool) into the aws-ecs module alongside
the existing external IdPs (Entra, Okta, Auth0, PingFederate):

- New cognito_* root + module variables (enabled, user_pool_id, client_id,
  client_secret, domain). Region reuses the already-injected AWS_REGION.
- Client secret stored in Secrets Manager with ignore_changes on the value.
- Task role granted read access to the Cognito secret.
- COGNITO_* env vars injected into both registry and auth-server containers,
  with COGNITO_CLIENT_SECRET via valueFrom; AUTH_PROVIDER ternary now resolves
  to cognito when cognito_enabled is set.

Validated with terraform fmt and terraform validate.

* docs(idp): add Amazon Cognito deployment-surfaces guide

Add docs/idp/cognito.md covering how to point Docker Compose, Terraform/ECS,
and Helm at a bring-your-own Cognito User Pool, modeled on the PingFederate
guide. Documents the variable mapping across surfaces and clarifies the
groups-not-scopes model: Cognito owns group membership (cognito:groups claim),
while group-to-scope mappings live in DocumentDB (IAM > Groups / Scopes UI).
Added to the mkdocs nav.

* docs(cognito): fix stale references in Cognito setup guide

- Replace scopes.yml references with the DocumentDB / IAM UI model (mappings
  are no longer file-based).
- Replace the dead map_cognito_groups_to_scopes debug snippet with the IAM UI
  plus an auth-server log check.
- Fix the agent env setup step (agents/.env.template no longer exists;
  cli_user_auth.py loads agents/.env.user directly).
- docker-compose -> docker compose; cross-link the new deployment guide.

* feat(iam): add read-only Cognito IAM manager

When AUTH_PROVIDER=cognito, the IAM manager factory had no Cognito case and
fell through to the Keycloak manager, so the registry's IAM > Groups / Users
pages failed with a 502 (Unable to list IAM groups) against a Cognito
deployment.

- Add CognitoIAMManager: list_groups, list_users, and group_exists are
  implemented via boto3 (cognito-idp) in registry/utils/cognito_manager.py;
  write operations raise NotImplementedError with a clear message pointing to
  the AWS console / CLI (read-only first).
- Wire provider == 'cognito' into get_iam_manager().
- Terraform: add a conditional cognito_iam_read policy granting
  cognito-idp:ListGroups, ListUsers, and AdminListGroupsForUser scoped to the
  User Pool, attached to the registry task role when cognito_enabled = true.
  The task role previously had no cognito-idp permissions.

* test(iam): cover Cognito IAM manager

Add a factory test for AUTH_PROVIDER=cognito and a TestCognitoIAMManager
class covering read delegation (list_groups, list_users) and that all write
methods raise NotImplementedError.

* docs(cognito): callback/logout URLs, group seeding, and IAM limits

- Step 4 now covers both callback and sign-out URLs (the /login logout URL is
  easy to miss and breaks logout otherwise), with console + CLI instructions
  and the CloudFront-domain-change caveat.
- Add console/CLI commands for creating groups, users, passwords, and
  assignments under Create groups.
- Add a section on seeding group-to-scope mappings in DocumentDB: the
  bootstrap registry-admins group is seeded by the DB-init step per surface;
  all other groups are created via the IAM UI.
- Note that Cognito IAM management in the UI is read-only.
- Troubleshooting: logout error, 'Unable to list IAM groups', and the
  empty-admin-permissions case.

Batch per-scope reads on the auth hot path to cut /api/auth/me latency (#1230)

A user's many groups map to many scopes, and authorization derivation
issued one serial find_one per scope, three times per request:

  - resolve_scope_access:        one find_one({_id: scope}) per scope
  - get_ui_permissions_for_user: one find_one({_id: scope}) per scope
  - the /me handler then re-ran get_ui_permissions_for_user a third time

On a local Mongo each round-trip was sub-millisecond, so the fan-out was
invisible; on Atlas each round-trip is tens of milliseconds, so the same
serialized calls multiplied into seconds. The migration didn't add work,
it made each round-trip expensive.

Fix:
- Add get_server_scopes_bulk / get_ui_scopes_bulk to ScopeRepositoryBase.
  The base class ships a default that loops the existing per-scope getters,
  so the file backend (which reads an in-memory dict and was already free)
  needs no change. DocumentDB overrides both with a single $in query,
  collapsing N serial round-trips into one.
- resolve_scope_access prefetches all rules in one call, then iterates
  user_scopes in original order against the prefetched map. Iteration order
  is preserved deliberately: the sticky-wildcard and tool-union semantics
  depend on user-scope order, not DB return order.
- get_ui_permissions_for_user does the same single-call prefetch.
- The /me handler reuses user_context["ui_permissions"] (already derived by
  _derive_user_context on every auth path) instead of re-querying the scope
  repo — removing the duplicate third fan-out entirely.
- Extract the server_access flatten logic into _flatten_server_access so the
  single and bulk DocumentDB paths produce byte-identical rule lists.

Error semantics: the bulk call fails closed. A backend error now yields an
empty UserAccess / empty permissions rather than the old per-scope behavior
that skipped only the failing scope. For an authorization path this is the
correct posture — partial results could grant a permission set that doesn't
match the configured scopes.

Tests:
- New tests/unit/repositories/test_scope_repository_bulk.py covers the $in
  query shape, dedup/sort of inputs, empty-input short-circuit, empties
  omitted from the result map, error-returns-empty, the shared
  _flatten_server_access helper (both on-disk formats), and the file
  backend's inherited default.
- test_access_resolver.py and test_dependencies.py fixtures wire the bulk
  mocks to delegate to the per-scope getters, mirroring the base-class
  default contract so all existing scope-semantics cases stay valid.

feat(connect-config): IDE OAuth login follow-ups (CSRF + PRM scopes fixes, surface wiring, docs, IdP scripts) (#1235)

* fix(csrf): resolve session_id in verify_csrf_token_header_only

verify_csrf_token_header_only validated the CSRF token against the raw
session cookie blob instead of the resolved session_id. The token is
signed with the resolved session_id (generate_csrf_token), so the
comparison always failed, returning 403 on every cookie-authenticated
GET. connect-config is the only endpoint using this dependency, so the
bug surfaced there as a silent fallback to the static-token Connect
config.

Resolve the cookie to the session_id first (mirroring verify_csrf_token
and verify_csrf_token_flexible), and skip the check when the cookie is
unresolvable. Add regression tests covering the happy path that was
previously uncovered.

* fix(oauth): default PRM scopes_supported to basic OIDC scopes

derive_supported_scopes() advertised every _id in the mcp_scopes
collection (registry group/scope names like 'registry-admins',
'tla-consumer-*') as OAuth scopes in the PRM document. IDEs then
requested those from the IdP, and any scope-validating IdP (Keycloak
without DCR, Okta, Entra, Auth0) rejected the authorization request with
invalid_scope.

Default to the basic IdP-universal OIDC scopes (openid email profile
offline_access) instead. Access is derived from the token's groups
claim, not the requested scopes, so this does not reduce access.
Operators can still override with MCP_ADVERTISED_SCOPES.

Update the wellknown/integration tests that patched the now-unused
reload_scopes_config and asserted the old group-name behavior.

* feat(connect-config): wire IDE OAuth client_id across surfaces + docs

Follow-up hardening for the IDE OAuth login feature (PR #1224):

- Surface wiring: add IDE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID + MCP_ADVERTISED_SCOPES to
  .env.example, the podman/prebuilt compose variants, and Terraform
  (ide_oauth_client_id variable + ecs-services env + tfvars.example),
  so the unified parameter reference matches the actual wiring.
- Frontend: render connect-config fetch errors (the connectConfigError
  state was set but never displayed) with an actionable 403 message,
  instead of silently falling back to the static-token config.
- Docs: add docs/connection-methods/ (client-id, DCR, CIMD) and a
  three-methods overview in ai-coding-assistants-setup.md.
- Scripts: add public-client setup scripts for Keycloak, Entra, and
  Okta; fix the Entra appId read-back; pin a fixed callback port and
  document the groups-claim requirement for Okta.
- Tests: add append_mcp_path round-trip coverage; minor code comments.

* feat(connect-config): IDE_OAUTH_CALLBACK_PORT for strict-IdP OAuth login

IdPs that match the OAuth redirect_uri literally including the port
(Okta, Entra, Cognito) reject the IDE's random loopback port. Add an
IDE_OAUTH_CALLBACK_PORT setting: when set, the Connect dialog emits the
matching --callback-port in the Claude Code command so the IDE uses a
fixed port that matches the registered redirect URI. 0 (default) omits
it, which is correct for Keycloak (wildcard redirect) and DCR flows.

Only Claude Code supports --callback-port; Codex (no such flag) and
Cursor cannot pin the port, so the dialog shows a warning in the Codex
tab when a callback port is configured.

Wired across all surfaces (.env.example, all docker-compose variants,
Terraform root->module->ECS env, Helm values + deployment + reserved
list + index test) and documented in the unified parameter reference and
docs/connection-methods/client-id.md. Also promotes IDE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID
to a first-class Helm value (was extraEnv-only).

* fix(cognito): accept access tokens (no aud) via client_id allowlist

Cognito access tokens have no 'aud' claim (they carry client_id +
token_use=access), but the provider always validated with verify_aud=True,
so every access token was rejected with 'Token is missing the aud claim'.
MCP IDE clients send the access token, so IDE OAuth login failed on
reconnect for Cognito.

Branch on token_use: id tokens stay audience-bound; access tokens skip
aud and validate the client_id claim against an allowlist (the web
client plus the optional public IDE client from IDE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID).
Wire IDE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID into the auth-server env (docker-compose +
Terraform). Adds unit tests for the access-token / allowlist paths.

Update checker (#1247)

* Update checker

Signed-off-by: omrishiv <327609+omrishiv@users.noreply.github.com>

* address PR review: wire UPDATE_CHECK params across surfaces + cleanups

- docs/unified-parameter-reference.md: add Group 13c for UPDATE_CHECK_ENABLED
  and UPDATE_CHECK_INTERVAL_HOURS (Docker + Helm columns filled; Terraform marked
  pending with extraEnv workaround note)
- .env.example: document both update-check vars with defaults and air-gap note
  so Docker/ECS operators can opt out
- registry/api/config_routes.py: add update_check group to CONFIG_GROUPS so the
  settings surface in GET /api/config/full and the System Config UI
- pyproject.toml + uv.lock: declare packaging as a direct dependency (was imported
  directly in update_check.py but only available transitively)
- registry/core/update_check.py: ruff format; move 'import json' to module top

* fix(lock): regenerate uv.lock so 'uv sync --locked' passes in Docker builds

The committed lockfile still carried a stale '[options] exclude-newer'
line that current main had already dropped (removed in #1197, which
predates this branch's base). With uv 0.11.14 pinned in the server
Dockerfiles, 'uv sync --locked' re-resolves without that global
constraint, finds the lock inconsistent, and fails the build for every
server image (currenttime, realserverfaketools, fininfo, metrics).

Regenerate the lock normally so the exclude-newer line is gone (matching
main) while keeping the packaging>=23.0 dependency added for the update
checker. 'uv lock --locked' now passes with no env constraint.

* fix(lock): align per-server uv.lock files with main so --locked builds pass

The currenttime/realserverfaketools/fininfo/metrics-service Dockerfiles run
'uv sync --locked', which re-resolves and verifies lock consistency. Each of
these per-server lockfiles still carried the stale '[options] exclude-newer'
line (and wrong-venv drift) that current main had already dropped, so uv
0.11.14 in the images re-resolved without that constraint and failed the build.

Restore all five server/service lockfiles to their origin/main state (the
server pyproject.toml files are byte-identical to main, so no functional
change). Verified: the four --locked images now pass 'uv lock --locked' and
'docker compose build currenttime-server' succeeds. mcpgw uses --frozen so it
was never affected, but its lock is realigned for consistency.

* fix(update-check): accept Bearer JWT on the endpoint; clarify dev-skip docstrings

Switch GET /api/system/update-check from enhanced_auth (cookie-session only)
to nginx_proxied_auth so it works with BOTH a browser session cookie AND a
Bearer JWT (validated by nginx, forwarded as identity headers). This matches
the sibling /api/stats and /api/system/telemetry-detection routes and lets
CLI / token-file callers reach it like the rest of /api/*. The is_admin 403
gate is unchanged, and the browser banner (cookie auth) is unaffected.

Verified live against a rebuilt registry: Bearer admin token -> 200 with the
real payload (was 401 before), unauthenticated -> 401, non-admin -> 403.

Also clarify the dev-skip docstrings: local builds never show the banner via
TWO independent guards. _is_dev_build() catches a plain 'docker compose up'
(BUILD_VERSION unset), while build_and_run.sh DOES set BUILD_VERSION but to a
non-semver git-describe string that the unparseable-version skip in
_run_check_once catches instead. Confirmed via container logs.

* feat(terraform): wire UPDATE_CHECK params into the ECS/Terraform surface

The update-check feature was only wired into Helm; the PR description noted the
other deployment surfaces still needed their variables. Add update_check_enabled
(bool, default true) and update_check_interval_hours (number, default 24, min 1)
across the full five-file Terraform pattern, mirroring custom_entity_types_enabled:

- terraform/aws-ecs/variables.tf: root variable declarations (+ interval validation)
- terraform/aws-ecs/main.tf: passthrough into the mcp-gateway module
- modules/mcp-gateway/variables.tf: module variable declarations
- modules/mcp-gateway/ecs-services.tf: UPDATE_CHECK_ENABLED / UPDATE_CHECK_INTERVAL_HOURS
  container env entries on the registry task definition
- terraform.tfvars.example: commented example block

Update docs/unified-parameter-reference.md Group 13c: fill the Terraform column
with the real variable names (was 'pending - use extraEnv') so all three
surfaces (Docker, Terraform, Helm) are now first-class. Verified with
'terraform validate' (Success) and 'terraform fmt -check' (clean).

* fix(lock): minimize root uv.lock diff to packaging + litellm pin only

The earlier 'uv lock' run drifted ~30 packages forward (aiohttp, fastapi,
cryptography, starlette, etc.) and added narwhals - unvetted churn the
supply-chain quarantine exists to avoid. Rebase the root lock on origin/main
and re-resolve so the only changes are:
  - packaging promoted to a direct dependency (needed by update_check.py)
  - litellm 1.83.14 -> 1.89.0, satisfying this branch's existing
    'litellm>=1.88.0' pin (inherited from #1246)
No other package versions move. Passes 'uv lock --locked'.

build(deps): restore exclude-newer supply-chain quarantine in uv.lock files (#1250)

Re-add the [options] exclude-newer cutoff to every uv.lock via the canonical
'make uv-update-locks' target (7-day quarantine), so a fresh resolve cannot
pull dependency versions newer than the vetting window. All locks pinned to a
single unified cutoff (2026-06-09T02:12:58Z).

The catch: 'uv sync --locked' re-resolves and FAILS when the lock pins
exclude-newer but the build environment lacks the matching global cutoff
(uv reads it as drift). The four Dockerfiles that use 'uv sync --locked'
(mcp-server-light, mcp-server-cpu, registry-cpu, metrics-service) now extract
the cutoff from their own uv.lock and re-export it as UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER right
before the sync, mirroring .github/workflows/uv-lock-check.yml. This keeps the
build self-sufficient (no build-arg threading, no build_and_run.sh change) and
cannot drift from the lock. The --frozen images (registry, auth, mcpgw) need
no change since --frozen does not re-resolve.

Verified: 'docker compose build --no-cache' succeeds for currenttime-server
(mcp-server-light) and metrics-service; all four --locked projects pass
'uv lock --locked' with the extracted cutoff; the merged 'packaging' direct
dependency is preserved; validate-dockerfiles.sh passes.

fix(auth): warn loudly when scopes collection is empty (#1248) (#1251)

An empty scopes collection makes every authenticated user fall back to
read-only access regardless of group membership, but startup only logged
it at INFO ('0 group mappings'), so a skipped post-deployment seeding step
was hard to diagnose.

Emit a WARNING with actionable remediation when 0 group mappings are
loaded, pointing at run-documentdb-init.sh / load-scopes.py:
- registry/common/scopes_loader.py: the shared repository load path.
- auth_server/server.py: new _log_scopes_loaded() helper used by both
  startup paths (lifespan + legacy startup_event), replacing the duplicated
  INFO log lines.

No change to seeding behaviour or access-control logic; the populated case
still logs at INFO unchanged. Backend-agnostic (the empty check is on the
loaded dict). Adds 3 unit tests; full auth-server server suite passes (119).

feat(connect-config): persist per-server oauth_client_id and append_mcp_path (#1241)

* feat(connect-config): persist per-server oauth_client_id and append_mcp_path

The connect-config GET and ServerInfo schema added in the IDE-OAuth-login work
expose per-server oauth_client_id and append_mcp_path, and the frontend reads
them, but there was no API write path: neither register handler nor the edit
form accepted the fields, and the PUT/PATCH models are extra="forbid" (so a body
carrying them 422s). Per-server overrides could therefore never be set — the
connect-config always returned None, so e.g. root-endpoint servers like AWS
Knowledge always got the auto-detected trailing /mcp.

Wire the write path consistently with existing connect fields (mcp_endpoint):

- register_service (POST /register), register_service_api (POST /servers/register)
  and edit_server_submit (POST /edit/{path}): accept both as optional Form fields
  and persist into the server entry when provided (None = unset/auto-detect).
- ServerUpdateRequest (PUT) and ServerCardPatch (PATCH): add both fields. They are
  not registrant-only, so the merge keeps them; PATCH stays exclude_unset.

Tests: register persistence for both register handlers, omitted-when-unset, and
PUT/PATCH model acceptance (extra="forbid" still rejects unknown fields).

Closes the per-server override gap from the IDE OAuth login feature (#1224).

* test(connect-config): cover edit_server_submit override persistence

Codecov flagged the edit_server_submit branch: existing edit tests only
exercised the omit path (partials on the two `if ... is not None` guards) and
nothing sent the fields (the two assignments were uncovered). Add a remote-edit
test that supplies oauth_client_id + append_mcp_path and asserts they land in the
updated server entry, completing patch coverage for the write path.

fix(build): restore docker/Dockerfile.mcp-server-light still referenced by compose (#1257)

PR #1254 removed docker/Dockerfile.mcp-server-light as 'unused', but
docker-compose.yml still references it for three services (currenttime-server,
fininfo-server, realserverfaketools-server), so 'docker compose build' and

* fix(nginx): declare $backend_url at http scope so nginx starts with no MCP servers

$backend_url is referenced in the shared 'location = /validate' block (to forward
X-Resolved-Upstream) but only 'set' inside the generated /mcp-proxy/ location blocks.
When no such block renders -- no healthy MCP server, or registry-only mode -- the
reference is an UNKNOWN variable and nginx fails to START:
  [emerg] unknown "backend_url" variable

Declare it at http scope via 'map $host $backend_url { default ""; }'. A map default
declares the variable globally; a location-level 'set $backend_url ...' still overrides
it per-request. Unlike a server-scope 'set' (which the auth_request subrequest re-runs
and clobbers), a map is evaluated lazily and is not clobbered -- safe for /validate.

Caught by through-nginx integration testing on a stack with no healthy MCP server.
Adds a regression test asserting the http-scope map declaration in both confs.

feat(auth): filter IdP groups to scope-relevant set at login (#1279)

Users with very large IdP group memberships (e.g. Entra ID accounts in
hundreds of AD groups) hit two failures that scale with group count on every
request: the X-Groups response header from /validate overflows nginx buffers
(500s on /scan and /ratings, intermittent login loops), and map_groups_to_scopes
issues one DocumentDB query per group.

Filter the group list at login, before the session store write, so the stored
set is bounded by scope-relevant groups instead of total membership. The filter
runs once at the single create_session chokepoint, covering all OAuth providers.

- Design C (default, ALLOWED_IDP_GROUPS empty): intersect the user's IdP groups
  with the set of groups mapped to any scope (new repo method
  get_all_mapped_group_names, live query). Lossless for authorization: unmapped
  groups never produce scopes.
- Design B (ALLOWED_IDP_GROUPS set): intersect with that explicit exact-name
  allowlist instead; takes precedence over Design C.
- Fail-open only when Design C cannot run (repo error or no scope mappings).

Adds get_all_mapped_group_names to the scope repository interface plus DocumentDB
and file backends. Wires ALLOWED_IDP_GROUPS across Docker (compose + podman +
prebuilt), Terraform/ECS, Helm (registry + auth-server + stack, reserved-env
lists), the System Config page, and the unified parameter reference.

Does not reuse IDP_GROUP_FILTER_PREFIX, which is UI-list filtering only.

perf(auth): collapse per-group scope lookup into one bulk query (#1281)

map_groups_to_scopes resolved a user's groups to scopes by awaiting one
DocumentDB query per group, serially, inside validate_session_cookie and the
nginx /validate subrequest. Scopes are not cached on the session, so every
authenticated request re-paid the full per-group fan-out — N round-trips that
dominated latency for users with many groups on a remote cluster.

union) mirroring the existing get_server_scopes_bulk pattern: non-abstract
default on the interface loops the single getter (file backend inherits it for
free), DocumentDB overrides with one query. Swap map_groups_to_scopes to call
it once: N round-trips -> 1.

Also add the missing multikey index on mcp_scopes_default.group_mappings via an
ensure-index hook; without it each group_mappings filter was a full collection
scan, so the bulk $in is now an index seek.

host.identifier and assert identity via the https trust manifest only
(proven by the existing TLS certificate). did:web returns with the signing
follow-up.

[options] block: uv reports the lockfile as out of sync because the global
exclude-newer is missing at sync time. Read the pinned exclude-newer from the

Follow-up to #1285: fix scopes_init build break, dangling calls, docs sweep, metrics rename (#1309)

* fix: remove scopes_init build artifacts that COPY deleted scopes.yml

The scopes_init image (Dockerfile.scopes-init) COPYs auth_server/scopes.yml,
which was deleted in #1285, breaking 'make build-push'. Remove the image and
its build wiring (build-config.yaml, buildspec.yml, codebuild.tf), the
run-scopes-init-task.sh helper, and the container-security test reference.
The scopes_init image only delivered scopes.yml to EFS for the file backend;
mongo backends seed scopes from JSON files at init time.

* fix: remove dangling verify_scopes_yml and dead verify_faiss_metadata calls

#1285 deleted verify_scopes_yml but left two callers in each of
cli/service_mgmt.sh and terraform/aws-ecs/scripts/service_mgmt.sh, which would
fail with 'command not found' during register/remove. Remove those calls plus
verify_faiss_metadata (which greps a service_index_metadata.json that no longer
exists), and the dead FAISS index block in build_and_run.sh.

* docs: correct STORAGE_BACKEND row in unified parameter reference

The 'file' backend is rejected (not deprecated) as of v1.24.8. Update the row
to drop 'file', mark mongodb-ce as the default, and note the removal.

* feat: migrate federation config and peer state in file-to-mongo migrator

Extend migrate-file-to-mongodb.py to also carry federation config
(/app/config/federation/*.json) and peer state (peer configs +
peer_sync_state.json) into DocumentDB. This data is operator-entered and not
regenerable. Security and skill scans are intentionally not migrated (they are
regenerable by re-running a scan). Adds --federation-dir, --peers-dir,
--peer-sync-state-file, and --federation-only flags.

* docs: replace deleted scopes.yml references with DocumentDB scope model

Sweep documentation that still referenced the removed auth_server/scopes.yml.
Scopes now live in the mcp_scopes collection (DocumentDB), seeded from JSON
files in scripts/ at init time and managed via the scope management API.
docs/scopes.md gets the substantive rewrite; operational steps that cat/copy/
validate the file are updated to the DocumentDB-backed flow. Historical/legacy
design-doc references are kept with a removal note where appropriate.

* refactor(metrics): rename faiss_search_time_ms to vector_search_time_ms

Align the metrics-service discovery_metrics column and client with the
registry's renamed telemetry key (vector_search_time_ms). Adds an in-place
ALTER TABLE RENAME COLUMN migration for existing databases and a backward-compat
fallback that accepts the legacy key for in-flight payloads. Test now asserts
the value lands in the renamed column.

* docs: announce file backend + FAISS removal in README What's New

Add a breaking-change entry at the top of the What's New section documenting
the removal of the file storage backend, FAISS search, and scopes.yml (the
DocumentDB-only migration). Update the older DocumentDB storage entry that
still described file storage as 'deprecated and will be removed' to reflect
that it is now removed.

* fix(terraform/aws-ecs): defer secret rotation to avoid create-time DB desync

Enabling rotation on the keycloak/database and documentdb credential secrets
triggered an immediate rotation on the first apply, racing with cluster
provisioning: the rotation Lambda advanced the Secrets Manager value before the
database was reachable, so the stored secret no longer matched the actual DB
password. For Keycloak this left it crash-looping with 'Access denied for user
keycloak' and the post-deployment Keycloak init timing out.

Set rotate_immediately = false on both rotation resources so the first rotation
runs on the 30-day schedule against a healthy, reachable database.

Also document this failure mode (and the related stale mcp-gateway-web client
secret requiring an auth-server/registry restart after Keycloak init) in the
terraform-setup skill's troubleshooting section.

* docs: add read-write non-admin group examples and guide

Add two example group scope definitions for non-admin read-write users
that can list and register servers and run health checks, but cannot
toggle, modify lifecycle status, or delete servers:

- read_all_register_new.json: sees all servers
- read_select_register_new.json: sees only a select list; an admin must
  add a newly registered server to the group with add-to-groups

Both use register_service: ["*"] (not ["all"]) to avoid the admin
auto-promotion in _user_is_admin(). The guide documents the two-layer
access model and this gotcha.

* docs: convert read-write non-admin group guide into FAQ entry

Move docs/read-write-non-admin-groups.md into docs/faq/ in the FAQ
question style used by the other entries, register it in the FAQ index,
and add an IdP Independence section noting the flow is tested with
Keycloak but the concept is IdP-agnostic: create the group scope in the
registry and a matching group of the same name in your IdP (via the CLI,
the IdP admin console, or the Registry UI).

fix(security): enforce authorization on External API management endpoints (#1333)

* fix(security): enforce authorization on /api/servers/* management endpoints

The External API endpoints under /api/servers/* authenticated callers via
nginx_proxied_auth but skipped the authorization checks their legacy UI/internal
equivalents enforce. Any authenticated low-privileged user could call
POST /api/servers/groups/import with a ui_permissions payload mapping their IdP
group to a mutating action with "all" access, gaining admin on the next request.

Enumerating the full write surface showed the gap covered the whole
/api/servers/groups/* family plus several server-mutation routes, not just the
import endpoint.

Changes:
- Add a _require_admin helper to server_routes.py (mirrors management_routes.py)
  and gate all five group routes: import, create, add, remove, delete.
- POST /api/servers/toggle now requires toggle_service permission plus a
  per-server access check for non-admins, matching the legacy toggle route.
- POST /api/servers/register (remote) now requires register_service permission,
  matching the legacy register route. Local registration already required admin.
- PATCH /servers/{path}/auth-credential, PUT /servers/{path}/versions/default,
  and DELETE /servers/{path}/versions/{version} now require modify_service.
- Defense in depth: scope_repository.import_group refuses to persist
  admin-conferring ui_permissions (mutating action granted "all") unless the
  caller passes allow_privileged=True. Admin-gated IAM management callers pass
  it; the public import path never does. _grants_admin mirrors _user_is_admin
  exactly: "all" confers admin, "*" does not (issue #663).

Tests:
- 24 new unit tests covering admin gates, toggle/register/modify permission
  checks, and the repository content guard (incl. agreement with _user_is_admin).
- Updated management_routes tests for the new allow_privileged kwarg.

* fix(security): extend authz fix to federation and agent-toggle (same class)

A cross-family audit found the /api/servers/* authorization gap is one
instance of a broader class: External API routes that mirror admin-gated
/internal/* (or peer-management) operations but never re-applied the gate.
Two more confirmed gaps are closed here under the same disclosure.

federation_routes.py (HIGH): all 10 mutating routes had only
Depends(nginx_proxied_auth) and no authz at the endpoint, service, or
repository layer. Any authenticated low-privileged user could point the
registry at an attacker-controlled federation source / peer registry and
trigger a sync (data-exfil + content-injection). Add
_check_federation_management_scope (admin OR federation/peers scope,
mirroring peer_management_routes.py) to save/update/delete config,
add/remove anthropic server, add/remove asor agent, add/remove aws
registry, and sync.

agent_routes.py: POST /agents/{path}/toggle checked toggle_service
permission but, unlike the server toggle, skipped the per-resource access
check for non-admins. Add the access check (accessible_agents membership or
ownership) so the agent surface matches the server surface.

Tests:
- New tests/unit/api/test_federation_routes_authz.py: non-admin rejected on
  delete/sync; admin and federation/peers-scope allowed.
- New agent-toggle tests: rejects permitted-but-no-access caller; allows
  owner not in accessible_agents.

(fix) mcp session id hardening (#1357)

* fix(virtual-router): bind MCP sessions to authenticated user to prevent hijacking

An authenticated MCP client who presented another user's Mcp-Session-Id
(format vs-<uuid4hex>) could hijack that session: the Lua router validated
the session by existence only, never checking it belonged to the caller.
Backend sessions, keyed solely on client_session_id, were reachable through
the hijacked client session.

Bind validation to the authenticated identity, enforced before any session
context is loaded:

- Repository: validate_client_session and get_backend_session add user_id to
  the find_one_and_update filter (atomic owner check, no check/use gap);
  store_backend_session pins user_id in the upsert filter and refuses a
  cross-owner collision; delete_backend_session scopes to the owner.
  validate_client_session also binds virtual_server_path so a session minted
  for one virtual server cannot be replayed against another.
- Internal endpoints forward the authenticated user_id (and virtual_server_path)
  to the repository.
- Lua router: resolve the authenticated identity once (normalizing the empty
  string nginx yields for an absent X-User to nil, so the fallback chain does
  not lock onto a truthy "") and fail closed with 401 when absent; allowlist
  the session ID to ^vs-[0-9a-f]+$ before it reaches any internal subrequest
  (closing a query-param injection that could shadow the owner check) and
  escape it into subrequest URIs as defense in depth; scope the L1 cache key
  by user and virtual server path; surface a session-creation failure as 503
  instead of a misleading 200 with no Mcp-Session-Id.

Ownership remains optional at the repository/endpoint layer to preserve legacy
callers; the router always supplies it.

Tests cover owner binding and virtual-server binding at the repository and
endpoint layers (validate/get/store/delete), including wrong-owner and
wrong-path rejection and the legacy no-owner paths.

* fix(internal-routes): require user_id on session ownership endpoints

The validate / get / delete session endpoints took user_id as an optional
query param, so a caller that omitted it silently fell back to existence-only
validation -- the original session-hijacking behavior -- with no error. Make
user_id a required query param on all three: a request without it now fails
with 422 instead of silently dropping the ownership check.

The Lua router already always supplies user_id, so this is no behavior change
on the live path; it converts a latent "forgot the arg" footgun into a loud
failure. The repository layer keeps user_id optional (a generic data-access
primitive where None legitimately means "no owner filter"); virtual_server_path
also stays optional (a missing path widens the match but never drops the owner
check). store_backend_session is unchanged -- its user_id comes from the request
body and is set by the router to the authenticated owner.

Adds endpoint tests asserting 422 when user_id is omitted (with the correct
internal secret, so the failure is the missing param, not the auth gate) and
that supplying it forwards correctly to the repository.

* fix(session-models): require user_id on session request bodies; document owner-filter guard

Follow-up to the required-user_id endpoint hardening, applying the same
fail-loud principle to the request-body path.

- StoreSessionRequest.user_id and CreateClientSessionRequest.user_id are now
  required (was default="anonymous"). The router always sets them to the
  authenticated owner, so this is no behavior change on the live path; it stops
  a future caller silently storing an "anonymous"-owned session document that
  no real (always-authenticated) lookup could ever read back. virtual_server_path
  stays defaulted -- it is not the ownership control.
- Document the `is not None` owner-filter guards in the repository: only None
  means "no owner filter"; an empty-string user_id must add an always-
  non-matching filter, not skip it. A truthiness check (`if user_id:`) would let
  an empty owner reopen the existence-only hijack gap. Empty user_id cannot
  occur on the live path (the router normalizes ""->nil and 401s), but the guard
  must stay fail-safe regardless.

Updates the model tests to assert user_id is required rather than defaulting.

fix(security): separate internal service tokens from user tokens (#1359)

Internal service-to-service tokens and end-user access tokens were
cryptographically interchangeable HS256 JWTs (same SECRET_KEY, same
issuer, same audience). validate_internal_auth checked only iss, aud,
token_use, and the signature, so any authenticated user's token from
POST /api/tokens/generate was accepted as a trusted internal service
credential on every /api/internal/* route, enabling privilege
escalation to admin (Security Finding 1, CVSS ~9.1).

Root cause: auth_server/server.py imported _INTERNAL_JWT_AUDIENCE and
reused it as the user-token audience, collapsing the trust boundary.

Fix (three independent controls, deployed together):
- Internal tokens use a distinct audience (mcp-internal); user tokens
  keep mcp-registry via a new explicit _USER_JWT_AUDIENCE constant.
- Internal tokens carry a mandatory token_kind=internal-service claim,
  enforced in _validate_bearer_token (denies user/resource kinds).
- Internal tokens are signed with a key derived from SECRET_KEY via
  HMAC-SHA256, so a user token signed with the raw SECRET_KEY fails
  signature verification on the internal path.

Also enforce SECRET_KEY and AUTH_SERVER_NGINX_MARKER_SECRET minimum
length of 32 bytes (Security Finding 28); the derived internal key
inherits SECRET_KEY entropy.

Tests: new tests/unit/auth/test_internal_token_separation.py pins all
three separation controls plus key-derivation properties; the
reload-scopes success test now mints via generate_internal_token so it
exercises the real contract instead of a hand-rolled old-style token.

HTTP 500. GET /api/tokens and GET /login were both affected.

login form) to TemplateResponse(request, name, context). Add a
regression test that renders the token generation page and asserts 200.

feat(nginx): derive mcp-proxy proxy_read_timeout from MCP_PROXY_TIMEOUT (#1361)

The generated /mcp-proxy/ nginx location blocks previously set no
proxy_read_timeout and inherited nginx's implicit 60s default, so
raising MCP_PROXY_TIMEOUT above 60s had no end-to-end effect unless an
operator also hand-edited nginx: nginx would cut the request before the
inner auth-server hop timed out.

Derive the nginx read/send timeout for these blocks from
settings.mcp_proxy_timeout (MCP_PROXY_TIMEOUT) plus a fixed 30s buffer,
so a single knob raises the whole proxy chain and the inner hop always
times out first (clean 504 rather than an nginx cutoff). The default
30s upstream timeout yields 60s here, matching nginx's historical
implicit default, so behavior is unchanged unless the timeout is raised.

The derivation approach was contributed by @go-faustino in PR #1321
(closed as superseded by the MCP_PROXY_TIMEOUT work in #1356/#1358);
this lands the nginx piece on top of the existing mcp_proxy_timeout
field, with credit.

this prevents any off-lock install from selecting a vulnerable one.

fix(metrics-service): require per-deployment secret for API-key hashing and close rate-limit oracle

Replace the hard-coded public HMAC key used to hash stored API keys with a
required per-deployment secret (METRICS_KEY_PEPPER), validated fail-closed
(reject unset/empty/whitespace/known-weak/placeholder/<32 chars). The service
refuses to start without a strong pepper, and every hashing entrypoint denies
rather than falling back to a predictable key. Deployment-scoped hashing keeps
the UNIQUE key_hash lookup working while defeating offline and cross-deployment
brute force of a leaked hash.

Throttle the /rate-limit endpoint per client IP before any key work and return
a uniform 401 for unknown and inactive keys so it can no longer be used as a
key-validity oracle. Return static text on retention admin validation errors so
responses do not leak the table allowlist. Add a constant-time hash comparison
helper.

harden Docker Compose stacks against insecure defaults

Bind all published service ports except the nginx front door (80/443) to
127.0.0.1 so internal databases, the secret vault, the IdP admin console,
dashboards, and backend app servers are reachable only from the local host.
In-container peers use service DNS, so intra-stack connectivity is unchanged.

Fail fast on required secrets via ${VAR:?} (OPENBAO_TOKEN, KEYCLOAK_DB_PASSWORD,
KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD, and DOCUMENTDB_PASSWORD for the authenticated prebuilt
MongoDB) instead of shipping working defaults, and drop the PingFederate vendor
password default. Reject known-weak literals in the build_and_run.sh preflight.

Make host AWS credentials opt-in: mount a single file only when
AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE is set (default /dev/null) instead of bind-mounting
the whole ~/.aws into the internet-facing registry container.

Pin floating image tags (pingfederate, alpine, prometheus, openbao dev helper),
remove SECRET_KEY/POLYGON_API_KEY build args from the root Dockerfile so secrets
do not persist in image history, and default the Helm mongodb-configure password
to empty so it auto-generates a strong random value. Ship .env.example DB and
vault secrets as commented placeholders.

ssrf url validation (#1363)

* fix: validate and pin outbound URLs against SSRF and nginx config injection

Add a shared, fail-closed URL guard for every user- and registry-controlled
URL the registry stores or fetches server-side, and wire it into all outbound
fetch sinks, registration write paths, and nginx config generation.

- New registry/utils/url_guard.py: validate_url plus proxy_pass_url, agent-URL,
  and server-path validators. Only http/https schemes are accepted; hosts that
  resolve to private, loopback, link-local, reserved, multicast, unspecified, or
  cloud-metadata addresses are rejected. IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses are unwrapped
  before the range check. guarded_client / guarded_async_client resolve, validate,
  and pin a validated public IP per request and per redirect hop while preserving
  the Host header and TLS SNI, eliminating the DNS-rebinding window. Operators can
  opt internal targets in via SSRF_ALLOWED_HOSTS / SSRF_ALLOWED_CIDRS; the cloud
  metadata endpoint is never allowlistable.

- Validate server proxy_pass_url, server path, and agent URL at the service
  chokepoints before persistence (covers dashboard/API, internal registration,
  CLI, and federated-peer import).

- Health checks validate proxy_pass_url before decrypting or sending backend
  credentials and fetch through the pinned client.

- Skill fetches, the skill scanner, the security scanner, the agent card fetch
  and pull-card, the agent reachability probe, and the MCP tool-discovery paths
  are routed through the guard; MCP SDK connections are validated before any
  credential header is built.

- Escape backend URLs, upstream Host headers, and paths before interpolating them
  into generated nginx directives.

- Return HTTP 400 for a rejected URL.

Adds unit tests for the guard, the pinned transport (including a simulated
rebind between validation and connect), registration rejection, credential
non-exfiltration on blocked health checks, MCP-client refusal of private
targets, and nginx escaping.

* fix: validate generated nginx config before persisting and pin ARD catalog fetches

Prevent a malformed generated nginx config from surviving on disk and taking
down the gateway on the next cold start, and close a DNS-rebinding window in the
ARD catalog crawler.

- nginx config generation now backs up the live config, promotes the candidate,
  runs 'nginx -t', and restores the last-known-good config on failure (or removes
  the file when there was no prior config), so a config that cannot pass 'nginx -t'
  never persists for a container restart to load. Both the direct write path and
  the debounced reload scheduler use this flow. When the nginx binary is absent,
  single-container/local-dev deployments promote as before; split deployments can
  set NGINX_CONFIG_VALIDATION_REQUIRED=true to refuse an unvalidated config
  before it is written, failing closed with the last-good config intact.

- The ARD ai-catalog crawler now fetches through the shared SSRF-guarded client
  (public-only, redirects disabled), pinning the connection to a validated public
  IP inside the transport call and re-validating each hop, so a host that rebinds
  to a private or metadata address between validation and connect is blocked.
  Redirect responses are refused rather than parsed, and an error on one nested
  catalog entry skips that node instead of aborting the whole crawl.

authz and ownership (#1365)

* fix: enforce fail-closed authorization and server ownership across privileged endpoints

Restrict virtual server CRUD to administrators instead of any user holding a
per-server execute scope, so tools cannot be aggregated across backends a caller
was never granted.

Attach the server's shared GitHub credentials only on an explicit,
administrator-gated opt-in. The credential provider now returns no headers
unless the caller opts in, and only the global_credentials auth scheme opts in;
selecting or repointing a global_credentials skill requires an administrator.

Enforce owner-or-administrator authorization on server-mutating endpoints that
previously checked only the modify_service permission: registration overwrite,
auth-credential update, version removal, and default-version change. Fix the ANS
link/unlink ownership check, which read the owner via attribute access on a dict
and therefore never denied anyone, and add matching route-level guards plus a
fail-closed service-layer check. Tighten the ANS admin check so a per-server
access scope is no longer treated as registry-administrator rights.

All checks fail closed on missing identity, missing ownership metadata, or an
unrecognized signal.

* fix: key server-removal delete permission on stored server name

The POST /servers/remove handler checked the fine-grained delete_service
permission against the raw URL path token (path.strip("/")) rather than the
server's stored name. Every other server-mutating handler keys its permission
check on the stored server_name, so this was an inconsistent trust key: a grant
recorded against the server name did not authorize a legitimate deleter, and a
grant recorded against a path string that differs from the server name could.

Key the check on server_info["server_name"] via the shared
user_has_ui_permission_for_service helper, matching the other handlers. The
server is resolved first, so the check fails closed when the server does not
exist. The administrator bypass and the guard blocking deletion of federated
read-only servers are preserved.

idtoken signature (#1366)

* fix: verify OIDC id_token signatures against IdP JWKS before trusting claims

Decode the id_token returned from each provider's token endpoint with real
signature verification against the provider's JWKS, enforcing issuer, audience,
and expiry before any claim is read. Previously the callback decoded the
id_token with verification disabled and trusted its identity and group claims,
allowing a compromised or misconfigured IdP (or a tampered token response) to
inject arbitrary identity and elevated group memberships into the session.

- Add a shared JWKS-backed verifier on the provider base class that rejects
  non-RS256 algorithms, unknown signing keys, unexpected issuer/audience,
  expired tokens, and malformed input, and implement it for Keycloak, Entra ID,
  Okta, PingFederate, and Auth0.
- Verify a present id_token through a single fail-closed path in the OAuth2
  callback: any verification failure denies the login and never falls back to
  an unverified identity source. The userInfo endpoint is used only when no
  id_token is present.
- Add tests using a real RSA keypair and JWKS covering acceptance of a valid
  token and rejection of forged/unsigned/expired/wrong-issuer/wrong-audience
  tokens, and callback-level tests confirming a forged id_token denies login
  and never persists claims.

* fix: bind OIDC login with a nonce and add PKCE to the authorization-code flow

The OAuth2 authorization-code login flow verified the id_token signature but
did not bind the token to the specific login: it sent no OIDC nonce, so a
correctly-signed id_token minted for a different login could be replayed or
injected, and it used no PKCE, so the authorization code was not bound to the
client that started the flow.

Generate a per-login nonce and a PKCE code_verifier at /oauth2/login, send the
nonce and a S256 code_challenge on the authorization request, and persist the
nonce and verifier in the signed, integrity-protected OAuth2 flow cookie next to
the existing state. On callback, deny before any token exchange when the PKCE
verifier is absent, send the verifier on the token exchange, and after id_token
signature verification require the token's nonce to equal the value bound to
this login. The nonce check runs after signature verification through the shared
JWKS verifier, so a forged nonce on an unsigned token cannot reach it. Enforced
across Keycloak, Entra ID, Okta, PingFederate, and Auth0; fails closed on a
missing or mismatched nonce and on a missing verifier.

secret key hardening (#1367)

* fix: enforce strong SECRET_KEY and remove weak defaults

SECRET_KEY signs internal JWTs and session cookies and derives the
credential-encryption key. Startup previously accepted a short or
well-known value, several auth providers hardcoded a development
fallback, and .env.example shipped a functional default key.

Add a shared validator that rejects unset, empty, whitespace-only,
too-short (<32 chars), and known-placeholder keys, and wire it into the
auth server startup, the registry settings, and the login CLI so each
fails closed before constructing any signer or cipher. Remove the
hardcoded provider defaults and replace the .env.example value with an
empty placeholder.

* refactor: generalize signing-secret validation to any named secret

Extract the min-length and weak-value checks from validate_secret_key into a
reusable validate_signing_secret(value, name, required) so every signing or
marker secret can be held to the same fail-closed bar instead of growing a
bespoke check that drifts from the SECRET_KEY one. validate_secret_key becomes
a thin wrapper pinning the SECRET_KEY name and its always-required semantics,
leaving existing callers and error messages unchanged.

The required=False mode returns empty only for a genuinely unset secret; a
present but short or well-known value is always rejected, so an optional secret
can never be silently accepted in a weak state.

remove hardcoded placeholder secrets (#1368)

* fix: remove hardcoded default credentials and fail closed on missing secrets

Resolve the PingFederate admin API password through a single helper that
raises when the value is unset, blank, or set to the well-known development
default, so no code path can authenticate with a default credential:

- registry/utils/pingfederate_manager.py: add _get_pf_admin_pass() (with a
  denylist of the known-weak value) as the sole chokepoint used by _pf_auth;
  surface the configuration error from the public client-creation entry point
  instead of masking it as a generic admin-API error.
- registry/api/iam_user_groups_routes.py: resolve the password lazily via the
  shared helper and return HTTP 500 when it is not configured.
- terraform/aws-ecs: drop the weak default for pf_admin_pass and reject the
  known-weak value with a plan-time validation.

Replace realistic-looking Okta/Auth0 client IDs and secrets in the M2M
credential-provider help text, schema examples, and docs with unmistakable
placeholders so they are not mistaken for live credentials. No functional
change to the credential-provider behavior.

Add unit tests covering the fail-closed password resolution and a regression
guard that the example credentials are placeholders.

* fix: verify TLS on PingFederate admin API connections

The PingFederate admin API clients constructed their HTTP client with TLS
verification disabled, allowing a network man-in-the-middle to intercept the
admin credentials carried on those requests. Route both clients through a
single helper that verifies TLS by default. A private or self-signed admin
certificate can be trusted explicitly via PF_ADMIN_CA_BUNDLE (fails closed if
the bundle is missing or unloadable), and verification can only be disabled
through an explicit, default-off, clearly logged development opt-out.

fix(terraform): honor checkov suppressions and abort incomplete S3 uploads

The ~94 checkov:skip comments in terraform/aws-ecs were placed on the line

- CKV_AWS_136 (x2): AES256 default encryption is sufficient for the ECR

fix(egress): treat client auth headers as ingress-only, strip on egress (#1266) (#1369)

* fix(egress): treat client auth headers as ingress-only, strip on egress (#1266)

Client-sent auth headers (Authorization, X-Authorization, Cookie) authenticate
the caller to the GATEWAY and are ingress credentials. They are now stripped on
the auth-server egress hop and never forwarded to an upstream MCP server, closing
the ingress-token leak (a third-party backend could previously receive the
gateway's Keycloak JWT). Upstream credentials come exclusively from the egress
vault (oauth_user/3LO today; PAT and a custom-header mode via #1268).

The single exception is the built-in, same-trust-domain registry-tools server:
a hardcoded, non-configurable constant (_INTERNAL_INGRESS_RELAY_SERVERS =
{airegistry-tools}) relays Authorization to it. X-Authorization and Cookie are
never forwarded, even for that server. The decision keys on the verified,
path-validated server claim, never a forgeable header. This is internal plumbing,
not a user-facing relay feature, so a server registrant cannot enable it.

- _forward_headers gains relay_authorization (default False); strips
  X-Authorization/Cookie always and Authorization unless relaying.
- mcp_proxy computes relay_authorization from claims[server].
- The oauth_user vault-inject path is unchanged.
- Adds .mcp to .gitignore (local connect command holds a bearer token).

or egress vault), not from relaying the client's gateway token. The sole

works as an ingress header; the other X-Authorization references in the docs

* docs(egress): note SSRF allowlist adjustment for added internal MCP servers

Document the operational gotcha: the outbound SSRF guard fails closed on private
targets, so internal same-cluster MCP servers (reached via private hostnames)
need SSRF_ALLOWED_HOSTS / SSRF_ALLOWED_CIDRS entries or their health checks show
UNHEALTHY_URL_BLOCKED. mcpgw-server (airegistry-tools) is trusted by default;
additional first-party internal servers must be allowlisted (unioned, not

* fix(ssrf): trust the bundled registry-tools MCP host by default in the proxy SSRF guard

The proxy SSRF guard (#1363) fails closed on private/internal targets, which
blocked the health check for the gateway's OWN bundled registry-tools server
(airegistry-tools -> mcpgw-server:8003) since it resolves to a private
container/service IP. On upgrade to an SSRF-guarded build airegistry-tools went
UNHEALTHY_URL_BLOCKED unless the operator manually set SSRF_ALLOWED_HOSTS.

{mcpgw-server}) into the proxy allowlist so airegistry-tools stays healthy with
ZERO config. Operator-supplied ssrf_allowed_hosts are unioned in, never replaced.

enable_demo_servers and are intentionally NOT trusted by default -- operators who
enable them add them to SSRF_ALLOWED_HOSTS. The cloud metadata endpoint remains
unreachable regardless.

Tests: mcpgw-server bypasses with no config; demo servers are NOT trusted by
default; operator allowlist unions with (does not replace) the built-in.

* fix(secrets): fall back to AWS_REGION for the secrets-manager store region

honors AWS_DEFAULT_REGION), so egress connections 500'd with 'Could not load
connections' when only AWS_REGION was set. Fall back to AWS_REGION /
AWS_DEFAULT_REGION when AWS_SECRETS_REGION is unset; an explicit
AWS_SECRETS_REGION still wins. Only errors when no region is resolvable at all.

Tests: no-region error; AWS_REGION fallback; AWS_DEFAULT_REGION fallback;
explicit AWS_SECRETS_REGION precedence.

* fix(ecs): allow auth-server -> registry:8080 for the egress-token vend hop

The auth-server mcp_proxy vends a user's per-user egress token from the registry

allowed inbound 8080 only from the ALB and mcpgw, not the auth-server, so the

docs: stop instructing sslRequired=none; external is correct (#1384)

* docs: stop instructing sslRequired=none; external is correct (SA-8)

The setup guides told users to lower Keycloak's realms to sslRequired=none,
which is exactly the weakness SA-8 removed: none disables TLS enforcement for
external requests too, allowing admin login and OIDC/token traffic over
plaintext HTTP.

plaintext allowed from loopback). The setup commands reach Keycloak over
http://localhost, so they work unchanged. Replaced the disable-ssl steps in
complete-setup-guide.md, installation.md, quickstart.md, and macos-setup-guide.md

steps and a step-table row that would re-introduce the plaintext-HTTP weakness.

reachability) and removed the duplicate disable-ssl block in Phase 10.

Also removed internal audit-ID references (SA-8) from the macOS setup guide and
skill; the security rationale is kept in plain language.

fix(security): enable MongoDB auth by default; drop weak admin password (SA-11) (#1386)

* fix(security): enable MongoDB auth by default; drop weak admin password (SA-11)

.env.example shipped an active DOCUMENTDB_PASSWORD=admin (copied verbatim to
.env), and the default docker-compose.yml ran MongoDB with no authentication at
all. Together these seeded a weak/absent DB credential on every local install.

  compose fails closed instead of falling back to a weak default.

No application code change: registry/utils/mongodb_connection.py already builds
a SCRAM auth URI when username+password are set.

Adds tests/security/test_mongodb_auth_default.py. Validated on a fresh MongoDB
volume: unauthenticated access is rejected, authenticated access succeeds,
mongodb-init and registry/auth-server connect cleanly, and compose fails closed
when the password is unset.

* docs(faq): add local-dev MongoDB auth migration guide (SA-11)

Documents both a recreate-volume path and an in-place createUser path, and
