Sibling FAQ pages use one line per paragraph (no hard wrapping). Rewrapped
the MongoDB auth migration guide prose to match; code blocks and list items
are unchanged.

fix(security): drop unused python-jose (removes CVE-bearing deps) (SA-13) (#1387)

auth_server/pyproject.toml pinned python-jose[cryptography]>=3.3.0. The range
<3.4.0 is affected by CVE-2024-33663 (ECDSA algorithm confusion) and
CVE-2024-33664 (JWE DoS), and python-jose pulls in ecdsa, affected by the
unfixed CVE-2024-23342 (Minerva). Only the uv.lock resolution was safe; the
floor still allowed vulnerable installs off-lock.

python-jose is imported nowhere in the codebase (from jose / import jose has
zero occurrences); the auth server already uses pyjwt for all JWT mint/verify
(HS256 internal tokens, RS256 Cognito/Keycloak JWKS verification). So rather
than bump the floor, remove python-jose entirely:

- auth_server/pyproject.toml: drop python-jose; pin pyjwt[crypto]>=2.10.0 so
  the RS256 crypto backend is explicit (cryptography was already a direct dep).
- Regenerate auth_server/uv.lock: removes python-jose, ecdsa, rsa, pyasn1.
- Add tests/security/test_no_python_jose.py to prevent regressions.

Validated: `jose` no longer importable, pyjwt RS256 backend works, and the
full auth_server unit suite passes (418 passed).

fix(security): add access control to GET /servers/{path}/versions (SA-19) (#1388)

The versions endpoint (get_server_versions) ran no authorization and no
backend-URL redaction: nginx_proxied_auth only authenticates, so ANY
authenticated user -- including one with no access to the server -- could
read every version's internal proxy_pass_url for any server. Its siblings
(GET /servers/{path}, server.json, connect-config) all guard this; the
versions endpoint was missed.

Fix mirrors GET /servers/{path}:
- Resolve the server (404 if the path is unknown).
- For non-admins, run user_can_access_server_path (403 if no access).
- Strip proxy_pass_url per version for non-admins in with-gateway mode;
  retain it in registry-only mode and always for admins.

Adds tests/unit/api/test_server_versions_endpoint.py (404, 403-no-access,
admin-bypass, per-version redaction with-gateway vs registry-only vs admin).
Mutation-checked: the redaction/authz tests fail without the fix. No
regressions across the server-routes/authz/service suites (209 passed).

fix(security): make peer federation_token write-only in responses (SA-24) (#1389)

federation_token (the static bearer token this registry uses to authenticate
against a remote peer) was serialized in GET /api/peers and
GET /api/peers/{peer_id} responses -- both used response_model=PeerRegistryConfig.
These are reachable by any principal with the federation/peers scope (not just
admin), so a non-admin could enumerate peers, harvest their plaintext tokens,
and impersonate this registry against the remote peers.

Add PeerRegistryConfigResponse (subclass of PeerRegistryConfig) that excludes
federation_token, and use it as the response_model for every endpoint that
echoes a peer config back: list, get, create, update, enable, disable. The
request bodies still use PeerRegistryConfig so the token remains settable, and
PATCH /{peer_id}/token stays the dedicated write path. No service/DB change --
the token is still stored and used for sync, just never serialized out.

Adds regression tests asserting list/get responses contain no federation_token
even when one is stored (mutation-checked). Full peer suites pass (124).

fix: enforce CSRF validation on IAM management and federation endpoints (#1390)

The IAM management and federation configuration routers were the only routers
whose state-changing endpoints did not apply the server-side CSRF dependency,
and there is no global CSRF middleware. This left high-privilege mutations
(IAM user/group CRUD, M2M account creation, federation source add/modify/delete)
reachable cross-origin using an authenticated operator's session cookie.

Apply the existing verify_csrf_token_flexible dependency to every mutating
endpoint in both routers, matching the pattern used across the other routers.
Browser requests carrying a session cookie must now present a valid signed CSRF
token; missing or invalid tokens are rejected with 403. Non-browser
(Bearer-token) clients and read-only GET endpoints are unaffected.

Add tests covering all mutating endpoints: rejection without a token and
acceptance with a valid token.

fix: stop relaying caller credentials to untrusted MCP/A2A upstreams (#1391)

The MCP proxy and the nginx virtual-backend location forwarded the caller's
Authorization header and session cookie to registrant-controlled upstream MCP
servers, letting a malicious registrant capture and replay a caller's
registry-scoped credential.

- auth_server: drop a sensitive-request-header blocklist (authorization,
  x-authorization, cookie, proxy-authorization) in _forward_headers before
  forwarding to the untrusted upstream.
- nginx: clear Authorization and Cookie on the internal location that proxies
  directly to a registrant-controlled backend (the Lua subrequest inherits the
  parent request headers, so Cookie must be cleared explicitly).
- a2a travel-assistant sample: stop forwarding the registry token to discovered
  remote agents (accept only an explicit per-target delegation token); validate
  the agent-card URL with a fail-closed SSRF guard (blocks private/loopback/
  link-local/metadata addresses, http(s) only, post-DNS-resolution check),
  disable redirects, and lower the outbound timeout.

docs(egress-vault): fix mermaid render of placeholders (#1383)

feat: gate LLM tool execution behind confirmation and authenticate A2A agents (#1392)

Enforce human-in-the-loop approval and a deny-by-default executable allowlist at
the CLI agent's tool-execution boundary, and require JWT authentication in front
of the A2A agent servers, so LLM output steered by untrusted context cannot drive
destructive or state-changing actions.

CLI agent tool loop:
- Add a tool-safety policy that classifies each invocation read vs. mutate and
  validates shell commands against a deny-by-default allowlist of read-only
  diagnostic binaries. Reject unknown executables, path-qualified executables,
  and shell metacharacters before execution.
- Require explicit operator confirmation for every mutating action (all shell
  commands, mutating registry slash-commands, MCP call). Fail closed: deny when
  no confirmation channel is available and treat anything not provably read-only
  as mutating.
- Run allowlisted shell commands with a scrubbed environment so read-only
  commands cannot read credential-bearing variables and echo them back.
- Surface the confirmation as an interactive prompt in the CLI.

A2A agents:
- Add reusable JWT-validation middleware that verifies signature, issuer, expiry,
  and (when configured) audience against the Keycloak realm JWKS on every request
  before it reaches the LLM tool loop; only health probes are unauthenticated.
- Fail closed on missing/invalid tokens and on JWKS unavailability; install the
  middleware before the A2A mount so it wraps every route.
- Default the bind address to loopback and refuse to start when authentication is
  disabled while binding to all interfaces.

Adds unit tests for the allowlist, classification, fail-closed confirmation,
environment scrubbing, and the authentication middleware.

mcp proxy integrity (#1393)

* fix: authorize the exact forwarded body on the MCP proxy path

The MCP proxy path authorized scope/tool access on a separately-captured
copy of the request body (the X-Body header built in nginx) while
forwarding a potentially different copy upstream. When the copies diverge
-- e.g. a body larger than client_body_buffer_size spills to a temp file,
so ngx.req.get_body_data() returns nil and no X-Body is captured -- the
auth server defaulted the method to the unprivileged "initialize" and
authorized on that, while the full (potentially privileged) body was
forwarded and executed unauthorized.

Re-authorize the exact bytes being forwarded inline in the proxy hop,
before any outbound call, using the same scope-key derivation as the edge
validation (only a trailing mcp/sse/messages transport segment is
stripped; federated peer/server keys are preserved). Fail closed when the
scope-relevant body cannot be captured or parsed: capture_body.lua marks
requests whose body spilled to disk and clears any client-supplied
markers, the edge validation rejects an uninspectable (413) or unparseable
(400) body instead of defaulting to initialize, and the proxy hop rejects
(403) any body it cannot parse to determine the method/tool. The
virtual-router path, which reads and authorizes its own body, is
unchanged.

* fix(auth): strip internal X-Body capture headers before forwarding upstream

_forward_headers forwarded the gateway-internal X-Body / X-Body-Uninspectable
headers (set by capture_body.lua for the /validate hop) to the upstream MCP
server. Their value is the raw request body, which is not a legal HTTP header
value (braces/spaces), so httpx rejected every proxied request that carried a
body: "Illegal header value b'{...}'" -> the /mcp-proxy hop returned 502 for
tools/call on every server.

Strip x-body and x-body-uninspectable in _forward_headers, same as the existing
x-upstream-url internal-header strip. tools/call now succeeds (200), tools/list
still works, and the large-body spill still fails closed (413) so the proxy
body-authorization hardening in this branch is unaffected.

frontend xss hrefs (#1394)

* fix: validate URL scheme on dynamic frontend links to block script-scheme XSS

Dynamic href and window.open targets were rendered without checking the URL
scheme. React does not block javascript:/data:/vbscript: URLs in an href, so a
link whose URL comes from a server-registration payload or from ARD federation
discovery could execute script in a viewer's authenticated session when clicked.

- Add a single shared URL guard (isSafeUrl/safeHref) that allowlists only
  http/https/mailto, strips control characters and whitespace before parsing,
  lowercases the scheme, and fails closed on empty, relative, and scheme-relative
  values so obfuscated payloads cannot bypass it.
- Add a SafeLink component that renders a live anchor only for safe URLs and
  inert text otherwise, plus a react-markdown anchor override so links inside
  server-supplied markdown are guarded at render time.
- Route every dynamic link that renders a server- or federation-supplied URL
  through the guard (agent/skill/server cards, ANS metadata, agent details,
  semantic search results and its window.open call, markdown renderers) and
  replace the single-component scheme check with the shared utility.
- Add the react/jsx-no-script-url ESLint rule for both anchors and SafeLink,
  with a lint script, to catch regressions.
- Add unit and component tests covering safe schemes, rejected script/data
  schemes, obfuscation, and the markdown override.

* fix: guard server-supplied navigation URLs surfaced during upstream merge

Extend the URL-scheme guard to two programmatic navigation sinks that arrived
with the per-user egress feature and the login flow: the Connected Accounts page
opens the egress consent authorize URL (from the consent API, derived from
per-server OAuth config) and the login page navigates to the configured
auth_server_url (from /api/auth/config). Both are server-supplied, so route them
through isSafeUrl before window.open / window.location and fall back / refuse on
a non-http(s) scheme.

fix(podman): repair fresh-deploy path in docker-compose.podman.yml (#1377, #1378, #1379) (#1395)

Three independent bugs broke a fresh Podman Compose deployment:

#1379 mongodb-init defaulted DOCUMENTDB_USERNAME/PASSWORD to admin/admin, but
the paired mongodb service runs without auth. init-mongodb-ce.py then builds a
SCRAM connection and fails ("Authentication failed") against a Mongo with no
users. Default both to empty to match the no-auth service.

#1378 KEYCLOAK_EXTERNAL_URL and MCP_HTTPS_REQUIRED are documented in .env.example
and read by the code (wellknown_routes / keycloak provider) but were not wired
into the registry/auth-server environment blocks, so setting them in .env had no
effect: /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource 500s (enforce_https) and OAuth
discovery advertised the internal keycloak:8080. Wire both into registry and
auth-server (Keycloak already has its 18080 host port mapping in this file).

#1377 The realm was never imported (no --import-realm) which the reporter hit,
but the intended flow does not use import at all: keycloak/setup/init-keycloak.sh
creates the realm/clients/users via the admin API for every compose variant, and
keycloak/import/realm-config.json is not --import-realm-compatible on this KC
version. Rather than wire up the broken import, document that realm setup is done
by init-keycloak.sh so nobody adds --import-realm expecting it to work.

Verified via `docker compose -f docker-compose.podman.yml config`: parses; mongo-init
resolves empty creds; registry + auth-server carry both new vars. Podman runtime
repro to be confirmed by the reporter / CI (no Podman on the dev box).

fix(egress): route OAuth token calls through the SSRF guard and escape callback HTML (#1396)

The per-user egress credential vault lets a server registrant configure a
custom OAuth provider whose authorize/token URLs the registrant supplies. The
token endpoint receives the operator client_secret (and the user refresh_token
on refresh), but the outbound POST used a plain httpx client and the URLs were
never validated, so a registrant could point custom_token_url at the cloud
metadata address or an internal host and exfiltrate those secrets. The OAuth
callback page also interpolated the server path and provider into HTML without
escaping, and validate_server_path does not block angle brackets.

- oauth_engine._post_token now uses guarded_async_client(PROXY_PROFILE): every
  request and redirect hop is validated and pinned to a resolved public IP, so
  a private/loopback/link-local/metadata target is refused before the secret is
  sent (closing the DNS-rebinding window). A guard rejection is surfaced as
  OAuthEngineError, so the credential is never transmitted.
- configure_egress_auth validates custom_authorize_url and custom_token_url for
  a custom provider with validate_url(require_https=True) before persisting;
  non-https, private/metadata IPs, and bad schemes are rejected with 400. This
  is the only write path for a server's egress_oauth. Built-in providers are
  unaffected.
- The egress callback success and error pages now html.escape the interpolated
  provider, server path, and error text.

Adds unit tests for the fetch-time guard, the registration-time validation, and
the callback escaping.

readonly info restriction (#1397)

* Restrict backend URLs and group configuration on read endpoints

Non-admin users in with-gateway deployments could read internal backend
URLs (proxy_pass_url, mcp_endpoint, sse_endpoint) through several read
endpoints, and any authenticated user could read the full group
access-control model that only admins may modify.

Add a shared redaction primitive (should_redact_backend_urls plus
redact_server_backend_fields) and wire the server read surface to it:

- GET /servers/{path}/versions now enforces per-server access for
  non-admins and redacts per-version backend URLs.
- GET /servers/groups and GET /servers/groups/{group_name} now require
  admin, matching their write siblings.
- Semantic search redacts raw backend URL fields for non-admins while
  keeping the computed connect URL.
- GET /servers, the dashboard render, GET /server_details/{path}, the
  Anthropic-compatible /v0.1/servers endpoints (where the URL is
  re-projected as transport.url), and the unauthenticated well-known
  discovery URL are brought into the same redaction contract.

Redaction fails closed: a missing or non-admin context is redacted;
raw URLs are returned only to admins or in registry-only mode where
clients connect directly. Admin and registry-only behavior is
unchanged.

* Redact the derived endpoint_url in semantic search for non-admins

The semantic search response nulled the raw backend URL fields
(proxy_pass_url/mcp_endpoint/sse_endpoint) for a redacted caller, but the
derived endpoint_url still echoed a server's mcp_endpoint override verbatim
(_compute_endpoint_url returns it at Priority 1 regardless of gateway mode), so
a non-admin in with-gateway mode could still read an internal backend address
via endpoint_url.

_compute_endpoint_url now takes redact_backend_urls: when set it returns only
the constructed public gateway URL (or None), never the mcp_endpoint override or
the proxy_pass_url fallback. The semantic search handler computes the redaction
decision once and passes it to every _compute_endpoint_url call site. Also
corrects a stale comment on GET /servers/{path}/versions that described a 404
access-deny while the code returns 403 (consistent with GET /servers/{path}).

* assert registry only still gets the proxy mcp url

* fix: make federation tokens write-only and SSRF-validate peer endpoints

Peer read/list endpoints returned the full peer configuration including the
federation_token, exposing the bearer credential in plaintext to any principal
with the federation/peers scope. Introduce a token-redacted read model
(PeerRegistryConfigResponse) returned by list/get/create/update/enable/disable;
the token stays write-only (accepted on input, stored encrypted, used for sync,
never serialized back). Surface only a has_federation_token boolean, and stop
logging the raw peer-update body.

Peer endpoints were not SSRF-validated, so sync attached the token as a bearer
header and connected to an attacker-chosen host (private/loopback/metadata),
enabling SSRF and token exfiltration. Validate the endpoint with the shared URL
guard at create, on endpoint-changing updates, and again immediately before each
sync and at the outbound request chokepoint and health check. Federation
additionally requires the host to resolve only to public addresses so the guard's
trusted-domain allowlist cannot reach a private target. All checks fail closed.

* fix(federation): route peer sync through pinned SSRF-safe transport

The federation client attaches the peer bearer token to server-side requests
but connected through a plain httpx.Client, so the SSRF endpoint check was only
a pre-fetch validation with a DNS-rebinding TOCTOU window: a peer endpoint that
resolved to a public IP at check time could rebind to a private, loopback, or
cloud-metadata address before connect, exfiltrating the token. The pre-check
also used the skill-fetch allowlist, which could re-permit a private host that
the write-time endpoint guard (empty allowlist) rejected.

Build the client via guarded_client with a new FEDERATION profile whose
allowlist is empty (no bypass). Every request and redirect hop is now resolved,
validated, and pinned to a public IP inside the transport at connect time, so
there is no rebinding window and write-time and fetch-time validation share one
trust boundary. The retained pre-checks use the same FEDERATION profile.

log redaction (#1405)

* fix: redact credentials and PII from application logs

Route header dumps, request/body/user-context dicts, and decoded OIDC
id_token claims through a shared redaction layer so tokens, session
cookies, federation tokens, and user PII are never written to logs.

- add registry/common/log_redaction.py (redact_headers, redact_mapping)
- add safe_identity_summary() for OIDC claims/userInfo: masked sub,
  group count, and claim names only (never claim values)
- stop logging raw request headers and full user_context in the agent
  and server list endpoints; move diagnostics to DEBUG behind redaction
- log peer-update field names, not the token-bearing updates payload
- drop partial Authorization and session-cookie prefixes from the
  nginx-proxied auth diagnostics

* fix: write CLI-issued credentials to owner-only files instead of stdout/logs

Command-line helpers that mint credentials were exposing them: the metrics
API-key helper wrote the full key to a file with the process umask, the M2M
account command printed a fragment of the new client secret to stdout, and the
credential-cache writers created their token files with a plain open() before
chmod'ing to 0600 (a brief window where other local users could read them).

Create every credential file atomically with owner-only (0600) permissions via
os.open(..., O_CREAT | O_TRUNC, 0o600), and surface a freshly minted M2M secret
by writing it to a 0600 file and printing only the path rather than a stdout
fingerprint. Exclude the one-time secret dump files from version control.

* fix: stop logging captured OAuth subprocess stdout and auth-code prefix

The egress OAuth helper runs the generic OAuth flow as a child process and
captures its stdout, which carries the access/refresh token JSON as a deliberate
IPC channel. The consumer logged that captured stdout on both the success and
failure paths, writing the tokens to logs in clear text; drop those log calls
and keep only stderr (diagnostic, no token). Also stop logging a prefix of the
single-use authorization code. Document why the stdout print is intentional so
the IPC contract is not mistaken for a leak, and add a guard test that fails if
captured stdout is ever logged again.

* fix: stop logging JSON-RPC payloads, OAuth error bodies, group PII, and raw cookies

Close sensitive-logging sinks that landed in code developed alongside the
original redaction sweep:

- auth_server/server.py: the raw + parsed JSON-RPC request payload was logged at
  DEBUG; a tools/call carries user-supplied tool arguments (credentials, API
  keys, PII). Log only the byte size and the method name + request id.
- auth_server (server.py, keycloak.py, entra.py) and registry/auth/dependencies.py:
  full IdP group-name lists (organizational PII) and scope lists (the authz model)
  were logged at INFO/DEBUG. Log counts only; mask the subject in keycloak.
- credentials-provider OAuth flows (generic_oauth_flow, ingress_oauth, okta/auth0
  get_m2m_token): token-endpoint error bodies (response.text / full error JSON)
  were logged/raised; they can echo the client_id or partial credential context.
  Log only the standard OAuth error code.
- credentials-provider okta/auth0 get_m2m_token: the full decoded JWT claim dump
  to stdout now prints claim NAMES only.
- registry/health/routes.py: the raw WebSocket Cookie header (session cookie
  value) was logged at DEBUG; log presence only.

* fix: redact token bodies and token prefixes across IdP flows, agents, and CLIs

Second sweep across the merged tree closed further sensitive-logging sinks:

- Token-endpoint error bodies (response.text / full error JSON) logged or raised
  in registry/utils/auth0_manager.py, registry/services/registration_gate_service.py,
  registry/services/github_auth.py, registry/services/scope_service.py,
  credentials-provider/{entra,okta,auth0}/get_m2m_token.py, agents/registry_client.py,
  and the a2a travel-assistant discovery client. They can echo the client_id or
  partial credential context; now log only the status code / OAuth error code.
- Access-token prefixes logged (10-50 chars of a bearer) in agents/client.py,
  cli/agent_mgmt.py, cli/scan_all_servers.py, and a full plaintext token print in
  get_asor_token.py — replaced with a length indicator (the .env export line the
  helper exists to produce is kept).
- registry/services/federation/asor_client.py logged the first 10 chars of the
  ASOR token; log presence + length only.

* fix: do not print the metrics test API key in clear text (CodeQL 734)

add_test_key.py printed the API key value to stdout, which lands in CI/container
logs (py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data, alert #734). Mirror the hardened
create_api_key.py sibling: print a masked form plus the hash only.

* fix: redact group-list PII and stop exposing exception detail in responses

- Log IdP group-name lists as counts, not values, at the remaining sinks
  (registry/auth/dependencies.py enhanced-auth debug line; auth_server
  mongodb_groups_enrichment client + user token/DB enrichment paths). Group
  names are organizational PII.
- Stack-trace / internal-detail exposure (CodeQL py/stack-trace-exposure #731,
  #733): the metrics retention manager returned {"error": str(e)} which flows
  into the admin API response, and the egress OAuth callback reflected the
  EgressAuthError text (which embeds decryption/SECRET_KEY hints and wrapped
  upstream errors) into the browser. Log the detail server-side; return a
  generic error string/message instead.

* fix: stop reflecting exception detail into API responses (stack-trace exposure)

Return generic error messages to callers and keep the exception detail in
server-side logs only, closing py/stack-trace-exposure across the request-facing
handlers an adversarial sweep surfaced:

- auth_server/server.py: token-validation 401s (x2) and the M2M token-generation
  500 echoed the raw exception (issuer/audience/IdP-config internals).
- registry/api/wellknown_routes.py: the PUBLIC PRM and authorization-server
  metadata endpoints echoed provider-init / fetch exceptions in 500/502 bodies.
- registry/api/management_routes.py: _translate_iam_error returned the raw IdP
  (Keycloak/Entra) error string; the group-details 502 echoed the exception.
- registry/api/agent_routes.py: the agent-card fetch 502s echoed the httpx error
  (resolved hosts / internal network detail) — now logged, URL kept in the detail.
- registry/api/server_routes.py: the manual refresh-check 500 echoed the exception.

CodeQL alerts #379, #429, #531 (and #731/#733, fixed earlier) are in this class.

docs: add #1405 (log redaction) to 1.26.0 release notes

docs: add security guidelines and always-on invariants checklist

Add docs/SECURITY_GUIDELINES.md capturing enforceable security invariants and
category-level lessons (fail-closed, signing-secret validation, SSRF/URL
guarding, injection, authorization/ownership, logging). Add a compact
always-loaded invariants checklist to CLAUDE.md that points to the full doc, plus
a standing rule to persist a lesson whenever a new category of security issue is
found or fixed.

docs: expand security guidelines with lessons from ongoing remediation

Fold in category-level lessons surfaced while remediating findings: OAuth
nonce/PKCE flow binding, authorize-the-exact-forwarded-bytes, uniform read
redaction across an entity family, hardcoded-HMAC-key = unsalted hash, write-only
credential response schemas, TLS-verify-on-by-default for privileged egress, a
stricter path not inheriting a looser guard's allowlist bypass, frontend URL
scheme guarding, and a deployment-surface / insecure-by-default section. Add
matching lines to the always-loaded CLAUDE.md invariants checklist for the new
categories.

docs: add canonical security-helper registry to guidelines and checklist

Document the one blessed implementation per concern (SSRF-safe guarded HTTP
clients, CSRF dependency, internal-service auth, signing-secret validation, read
redaction, frontend URL guarding) so changes reach for the existing helper
instead of a new or copy-pasted snippet that reopens a fixed vulnerability. Add a
compact canonical-helpers pointer to the always-loaded invariants checklist.

fix: escape user input in MongoDB regex queries to prevent injection and ReDoS

Treat user-controlled strings as literals wherever they reach a $regex or
$regexMatch operator:

- server delete-with-versions escapes the server path before building the
  version-match regex, so a path with metacharacters can no longer over-match
  or delete unintended version documents.
- hybrid search escapes all query tokens and no longer falls back to the raw
  query as a regex pattern when tokenization yields nothing; the keyword-boost
  and keyword-merge stages are skipped on empty tokens (vector search still
  runs), so no attacker-controlled pattern reaches the database.
- application-log search escapes the search string at the repository sink so it
  is always matched as a literal substring, independent of the caller; the route
  helper now only enforces the length cap (single escape point, no double-escape).

fix: write CLI-issued credentials to owner-only files instead of stdout/logs

Command-line helpers that mint credentials were exposing them: the metrics
API-key helper wrote the full key to a file with the process umask, the M2M
account command printed a fragment of the new client secret to stdout, and the
credential-cache writers created their token files with a plain open() before
chmod'ing to 0600 (a brief window where other local users could read them).

Create every credential file atomically with owner-only (0600) permissions via
os.open(..., O_CREAT | O_TRUNC, 0o600), and surface a freshly minted M2M secret
by writing it to a 0600 file and printing only the path rather than a stdout
fingerprint. Exclude the one-time secret dump files from version control.

docs: fold in logging, credential-storage, upstream-forwarding, query-credential, and LLM-tool-safety lessons

Add canonical log-redaction helper (registry/common/log_redaction.py) and
credential-file 0600 idiom to the helper registry; document: never forward the
caller credential to a proxied/untrusted upstream (and clear inherited nginx
headers), never accept a credential as a URL query parameter, and gate
LLM-emitted tool calls at a fail-closed execution boundary. Update the
always-loaded CLAUDE.md checklist accordingly.

fix: keep CLI credentials off process argv and out of world-readable files

The scan-all-servers helper passed a gateway bearer token and an LLM API key to
the scanner subprocess on its command line (--api-key, --headers with a Bearer
token). Process arguments are readable by any local user via `ps` and
/proc/<pid>/cmdline for the child's lifetime, so a live token or key leaked to
every account on the host while a scan ran. Several credential helpers also
wrote token and MCP-config files with a plain open() (process umask, commonly
0644) and only tightened them to 0600 afterward, leaving a window in which the
token was readable by other local users; one helper never chmod'd at all.

Pass the LLM API key and target-server bearer token to the scanner subprocess
through its environment (MCP_SCANNER_LLM_API_KEY, MCP_SCAN_BEARER_TOKEN) instead
of argv; the scanner reads the bearer token from the environment first and only
places it on the external mcp-scanner's argv because that tool accepts it no
other way. Create every token/credential/MCP-config file that embeds an access
token, refresh token, or Bearer header atomically with owner-only permissions
via os.open(..., O_CREAT | O_TRUNC, 0o600) + fdopen, keeping the chmod to tighten
a pre-existing file. Add unit tests asserting no secret reaches the child argv
and that token files are created 0600.

fix: harden admin user-management, config export, and request-source trust

Add intra-admin safety guards to the IAM management routes: reject an
administrator deleting their own account, refuse deleting or demoting the last
remaining administrator, and emit a distinct audit event when a user
create/update grants administrator-tier group membership. The admin population
is derived from the existing privileged-scope rules and the guards fail closed
when it cannot be determined.

Make GET /api/config/export deny-by-default for sensitive values: exporting
secrets now requires an explicit confirm_sensitive_export acknowledgement in
addition to include_sensitive, otherwise the request is rejected.

Stop trusting the client-controlled left-most X-Forwarded-For entry when
resolving the client IP for audit records; prefer X-Real-IP or the trusted
right-most proxy hop and fall back to the direct peer.

Validate the inbound Host header against a configured allowlist before building
OAuth external URLs, falling back to the deployment's configured host on an
unexpected or missing Host.

docs: fold in m2m-audience, argv-secret, admin-safety, and forwarded-metadata lessons

From the m2m-audience-allowlist, cli-secret-hygiene, and admin-safety-guards
work: never derive verify_aud/issuer from an unverified claim (enforce audience
against a config allowlist, fail closed); never auto-grant groups/admin from a
code-shipped mapping; protect the admin population from lockout/self-delete;
never put a secret on subprocess argv (use env/stdin); trust forwarded client-IP/
Host only from the proxy hop and allowlist Host before building a redirect_uri;
escape regex at the sink not the caller. Update the always-loaded CLAUDE.md
checklist to match.

fix: scope skill list visibility exemption to admins only

The skill list endpoint decided whether to skip per-skill visibility
filtering based on an agent-scoped access grant, so a non-admin holding
broad agent access was served every skill including other users' private
and group-restricted skills. Base the fast-path exemption on administrator
status only; all non-admins are filtered through the skill-scoped
visibility check (public / private-owner / group).

feat(nginx): add inbound rate limiting to bound the auth-validation fan-out

Every authenticated /api, Anthropic-API, A2A-agent, /mcp-proxy and
virtual-server request triggers an auth_request subrequest to a single
/validate endpoint. With no nginx-layer rate limiting, a flood could exhaust
/validate for all users, and rapid server registration could drive unbounded
DB writes and index churn.

Add per-source limit_req/limit_conn zones (a generous edge limit plus a
stricter cap keyed to the registration endpoints) and apply them at the inbound
edge locations in both the http-only and http+https templates, plus the
dynamically generated /mcp-proxy and virtual-server blocks. Limits sit on the
edge, never on the internal /validate subrequest, so legitimate authenticated
traffic is unaffected. Return 429 when a limit trips.

Default the Terraform WAF on so ALB-fronted deployments get true per-source
per-IP limiting, where the nginx per-source zones otherwise collapse to a
single bucket.

fix: enforce OAuth CSRF state and make discovery metadata non-cacheable

Validate the OAuth callback state before exchanging the authorization code
in the credential-provider flow. The callback handler previously performed the
token exchange inline before any state check, and the calling flow only logged a
warning and continued on a state mismatch, which effectively disabled CSRF
protection. The generated state is now published to the flow and compared against
the browser-echoed state before token exchange; a missing, mismatched, or absent
state fails closed (no exchange, HTTP 400), with a hard-fail backstop in the
calling flow.

Serve the OAuth discovery documents (RFC 9728 protected-resource and RFC 8414
authorization-server metadata) with Cache-Control: no-store instead of
public, max-age=300 so a shared or CDN cache cannot hold or serve a poisoned copy
that redirects clients to a malicious authorization server. The FastMCP root
well-known redirect is also marked no-store.

fix: enforce single-use on internal service tokens to prevent replay

Internal service-to-service JWTs carried only iat/exp with a short TTL and
had no per-token identifier or server-side tracking, so a token captured on
the internal network could be replayed any number of times within its TTL
window.

Add a unique jti claim to every minted internal token and record consumed
jti values in a shared MongoDB/DocumentDB collection (unique index on jti
plus a TTL index that reaps entries once the token can no longer be valid).
The internal-auth gate now atomically claims the jti on each request: the
first presentation is accepted, a replay of the same token is rejected. The
check fails closed on a missing jti, an already-seen jti, or an unreachable
store, and the shared store makes the guarantee cluster-wide across replicas
of both services.

fix(audit): make audit trail durable-by-default and per-instance attributable

Require a durable audit sink by default: when audit logging is enabled but no
durable store (MongoDB/DocumentDB) is available, refuse to start instead of
silently degrading to non-durable log lines. Governed by the new
AUDIT_LOG_REQUIRE_DURABLE setting (default true); an explicit dev opt-out is
permitted with a loud startup warning.

Attribute audit records to a specific replica: internal service tokens now embed
a per-instance identifier in the subject (<service>@<instance_id>) plus service
and instance_id claims, and every API audit record carries the producing
replica's instance_id. Resolved from AUDIT_INSTANCE_ID, then HOSTNAME, then the
host name via a single shared helper.

Surface record loss loudly: a transient durable-write failure at request time is
logged as a distinct CRITICAL 'AUDIT RECORD DROPPED' event (identifying context
only, never the record body) rather than a quiet error, without failing the
request.

docs: fold in oauth-state, replay, rate-limit, audit, cross-resource-access lessons

From oauth-hardening, internal-token-replay, dos-rate-limiting, audit-hardening,
and skill-visibility: validate OAuth CSRF state at the token-exchange point (not
a post-hoc dead check) + no-store on discovery metadata; internal tokens need
jti + single-use (unless verified twice per flow); rate-limit at the inbound edge
not the shared /validate subrequest; audit durable-by-default + attributable; one
entity type's access grant must not gate another (cross-resource confusion). New
Availability & audit section + CLAUDE.md checklist lines.

fix: honor disabled flag in auth-server group enrichment

The auth server enriches a token's empty groups claim from the
idp_user_groups and idp_m2m_clients collections. Both enrichment paths
returned stored groups without checking the record's enabled flag, so a
disabled user-group mapping or a disabled M2M client kept granting its
groups (and therefore scopes) on every request.

Exclude records with enabled explicitly False at the query level and
re-verify the returned record in code (defense in depth). Records missing
the enabled field are treated as active for backward compatibility, matching
the registry service-layer read semantics. On a database error the
enrichment returns the caller's empty group list, which yields empty scopes
and a denial downstream (fail closed).

fix: require authentication for the registry configuration endpoint

GET /api/config returned deployment mode, registry mode, the active auth
provider, feature flags, coding-assistant list, and UI title to any anonymous
caller, aiding reconnaissance. Gate the endpoint behind the standard
authenticated-session dependency so anonymous requests fail closed with 401,
matching the already-gated /full and /export siblings.

The pre-login UI does not consume this endpoint (login reads /api/version and
/api/auth/*), so gating it does not affect the login flow.

fix: scope AgentCore federation IAM policy to least privilege

The registry federation client is read-only against the bedrock-agentcore
control plane (list registries, list records, get record) and only assumes
operator-configured cross-account roles. Replace the bedrock-agentcore:*
grant on Resource=* with the three read actions scoped to an account-bound
ARN, and gate sts:AssumeRole behind an explicit list of configured role ARNs
that defaults to empty (no cross-account trust unless configured). Apply the
same scoping to the Terraform aws-ecs module and the CDK infra stack, add
plan-time/synth-time ARN validation, and add regression tests asserting the
policy stays least-privilege.

fix: enforce scope-based server and tool access on the tool catalog

The tool catalog endpoint applied a parallel, weaker access check than the
rest of the registry, comparing each server document's stored required_scopes
against the caller's raw token scopes. This let a user enumerate tools on
servers they had no scope to access.

Reuse the shared access helpers instead, enforcing two layers that both fail
closed: server access via user_can_access_server_from_doc (keyed on
accessible_servers) and per-tool access via filter_tools_for_user (keyed on
accessible_tools). A missing user context, empty server grant, or missing tool
allowlist all return nothing; admins and wildcard grants pass through. The
route now forwards the full user context rather than a raw scope list.

docs: fold in honor-disabled-flag and IAM-least-privilege lessons

From user-group-disabled (#31) and agentcore-iam (#30): honor the
disabled/inactive flag on every request where access is derived (enrichment/
validate), filter in query + re-check doc, fail closed; IAM policies least
privilege — no wildcard Action/Resource, cross-account AssumeRole behind an
explicit default-empty list, Terraform+CDK parity. tool-catalog/federated/
unauth-config were instances of existing lessons (cross-resource confusion,
uniform reads, deny-by-default auth). Update CLAUDE.md checklist.

docs: note the parallel-feature SSRF gap and OAuth token-endpoint as a secret-bearing sink

A hardening PR that routes "every outbound URL" through the SSRF guard only
covers files on its branch; a feature developed in parallel ships an unguarded
sink the PR never saw. Adds guidance to re-audit concurrently-merged features
after a hardening wave, and to treat an OAuth token_url as a credential-bearing
outbound sink (validate at registration, pin at fetch).

docs: redact the derived field, not just the raw source field, on read redaction

Nulling proxy_pass_url/mcp_endpoint is insufficient when a computed field
(endpoint_url / connect URL / transport.url) is built from the same internal
value and returned alongside — the URL builder often echoes an explicit
endpoint override as its top-priority branch. Make the builder redaction-aware
and assert the internal host is absent from the derived field in tests.

docs(security): match placeholder-secret markers as substrings anywhere, not just prefix
docs(security): harden every secret reference, generate required secrets, case-insensitive placeholder denylist
docs(security): sweep every manifest for dep floors, guard-test all manifests, relock via make target

skill credential handling (#1412)

* fix: accept skill-parse credential via header and redact credentials in logs

Move the plaintext credential used by POST /api/skills/parse-skill-md out of
the query string and into the X-Auth-Credential request header. Query
parameters are captured in web-server access logs, proxy logs, browser history,
and the audit log's recorded query parameters, so a credential supplied that way
was persisted in cleartext. The endpoint now reads the credential only from the
header; a credential passed in the URL is ignored. The frontend registration
form sends the credential in this header.

Harden audit-log query-parameter masking with case-insensitive substring
matching (token/secret/credential/auth/api-key/key/password) in addition to the
exact-match set, so credential-shaped parameters are masked by default.

Introduce a single shared, fail-closed header redactor
(redact_sensitive_headers) and route every diagnostic header dump through it:
the auth dependency's DEBUG header dump, the agents-endpoint header dump, the
health monitor's outbound-probe header trace, the MCP client's server-header
trace, and the auth server's request-header masking. The skill scanner no longer
echoes a raw headers string (which can carry a bearer token) into an error
message.

* Emit no part of a credential in audit records

mask_credential previously returned the last six characters of a bearer token
or session cookie into the audit log's credential_hint and masked query
parameters. Those trailing bytes are real key-space -- for short tokens a large
fraction of it -- so persisting them contradicts the zero-emission rule the
header and token redactors follow. It now returns a fixed marker with no
substring of the value; the credential type (session vs bearer) remains on the
audit identity, so no diagnostic value is lost.

* test(redaction): pin the duplicated header-substring lists; document intent

Addresses review follow-ups on the credential-header hardening:

- Add test_header_substrings_match_shared_redactor: the credential-bearing
  header substring list is duplicated in auth_server.server and
  registry.common.log_redaction (separate deployables that cannot import each
  other), and nothing caught the two drifting. The test asserts they are
  identical, so weakening one copy without the other fails CI.
- Document that the audit query-param substring list intentionally differs
  from the header lists (header-only markers like cookie/jwt/bearer/session)
  and that 'key' is deliberately broad (fail closed) so it is not narrowed
  later and made to under-redact.
- Cross-reference the two header lists with KEEP IN SYNC comments pointing at
  the guard test.

Enforce M2M token audience against an explicit allowlist (#1418)

* fix: enforce M2M token audience against an explicit allowlist

Okta and PingFederate providers previously decoded the incoming token
without signature verification to read its cid/aud claims and disabled
audience validation (verify_aud=False) for tokens that looked like M2M
tokens whose aud was not the gateway client_id. This made the audience
check depend on an unverified claim, so any genuinely-signed token from
the same issuer minted for a different resource in the tenant was
accepted (cross-audience / confused-deputy).

Both providers now always verify the audience against a config-built
allowlist (client ids + application_id_uri + operator-supplied M2M
audiences via OKTA_M2M_ALLOWED_AUDIENCES / PINGFEDERATE_M2M_ALLOWED_AUDIENCES).
The verification decision is never derived from unverified claims and
fails closed when the allowlist is unconfigured (only the configured
client ids are accepted).

Also removes the hardcoded client-id-to-groups mapping in the Okta and
Auth0 M2M sync services, which auto-granted admin RBAC. Group assignment
is now driven by OKTA_M2M_CLIENT_GROUPS / AUTH0_M2M_CLIENT_GROUPS (JSON,
fail-closed to no groups when unset or malformed), so an injected client
id cannot be auto-granted privileges.

* chore(deploy): wire M2M audience-allowlist and client-group env vars across all deployment surfaces

The M2M audience allowlist and client-group mapping variables were only
documented in .env.example. Add them to every deployment surface so operators
can configure them wherever the other provider variables live:

- Docker Compose (default, prebuilt, podman): ${VAR:-} passthrough in the
  service blocks that already carry the sibling provider variables.
- Helm (auth-server, registry, and the umbrella stack): new okta/auth0/
  pingfederate values rendered into the provider Secret or the PingFederate
  env block, added to each chart's reserved-env-names list, and persisted
  across upgrades in the umbrella oauth-provider Secret. Adds unittest
  coverage asserting each value renders only when set and is rejected as a
  reserved name via extraEnv.
- Terraform/ECS: module and root variables, both task-definition environment
  blocks, and commented terraform.tfvars.example entries.

All four variables are optional and default to empty (fail closed).

OKTA_M2M_ALLOWED_AUDIENCES, PINGFEDERATE_M2M_ALLOWED_AUDIENCES,
OKTA_M2M_CLIENT_GROUPS, AUTH0_M2M_CLIENT_GROUPS.

fix: pass egress OAuth client secret via child environment, not subprocess argv

The per-config egress OAuth flow invoked generic_oauth_flow.py with
--client-secret <value> on the command line. Process arguments are readable by
any local user via `ps` / /proc/<pid>/cmdline for the child's lifetime (up to the
5-minute flow timeout), so the client secret was briefly exposed host-wide.

Hand the client secret (and, for consistency, the client id and redirect URI) to
the child through its environment under the names generic_oauth_flow.py already
resolves (EGRESS_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, etc.), and invoke subprocess.run with that
environment. The built command line now carries no per-config credentials. The
non-config code path already relied on the inherited environment and is unchanged.

  per-request cost and needs wafv2:* IAM permissions, so it should be opt-in.
  Documented in the variable description, terraform.tfvars.example, and the ECS
  README how and when to enable it (recommended for ALB-fronted / production,
  where the container nginx per-source zones collapse to a single bucket).

* harden obo_exchange egress mode

Hardens the obo_exchange feature against the branch's own egress security
practices.

nginx directive injection (HIGH):
- Sanitize the per-server PRM URL through _sanitize_for_nginx_set before it is
  interpolated into `set $mcp_resource_metadata "..."` (registry/core/nginx_service.py);
  it was the only interpolation in that file skipping the escape.
- Systemic guard: ServerInfo.path now has a slug field_validator rejecting nginx/
  URL metacharacters (quotes, semicolons, braces, whitespace, newlines, $), so the
  class of injection is impossible at the source, not only escaped per render site.

target_audience confused-deputy (HIGH):
- Reject an obo target_audience that is a shared first-party IdP resource (Microsoft
  Graph, ARM, Key Vault, ...) at registration (_is_forbidden_obo_audience). An obo
  target must be an internal MCP server's own app; a delegated token for a broad
  first-party API would be exfiltrated to the server's upstream.

subject-token binding (MEDIUM):
- Before exchanging, verify the raw ingress JWT's principal (preferred_username/sub)
  matches the /validate-authorized principal carried in the internal mcp-proxy token
  (_obo_subject_matches_principal). Removes reliance on the implicit "nginx forwards
  the same header to both hops" invariant.

defense-in-depth / consistency:
- Route the OBO IdP token POST through the SSRF-guarded client (guarded_async_client),
  matching the 3LO path, so a future discovery-derived token_url can't become an SSRF.
- Gate _obo_extra_audiences on egress_auth_enabled so the accepted-audience surface is
  not widened on non-egress deployments.
- Extend the same-app audience guard to the gateway's own resource URL (registry_url).
- Set egress_token_injected on the obo branch so a foreign upstream 401
  WWW-Authenticate is dropped rather than relayed (cross-resource PRM protection).

validator, forbidden-audience + gateway-own-resource-URL rejection, subject-principal
mismatch rejection, and SSRF-guard block/happy-path.

* harden obo target_audience with a positive allowlist

An exact-string host denylist is the wrong model for the target_audience control
and was bypassable many ways (:443, path/.default suffix, trailing dot,
api://<guid>, and every sovereign-cloud Graph/ARM/Key Vault host). Replace it with
a positive control:

- EGRESS_OBO_ALLOWED_AUDIENCES (new, optional): when set, an obo_exchange server may
  only use a target_audience in that exact allowlist -- authoritative.
- Otherwise a shape rule: an internal MCP server audience is an 'api://' App ID URI
  or a bare client-id/GUID, never an 'http(s)://' host URL. Every shared first-party
  API (Graph/ARM/Key Vault, all clouds) is an https host, so rejecting host-URL
  audiences blocks them by construction regardless of host spelling, port, or path.
  The two well-known first-party app-id GUIDs (Graph, legacy AAD Graph) are also
  rejected in bare and api://<guid> forms.

Also: _sanitize_for_nginx_set now neutralizes '$'. nginx has no backslash escape
for '$' inside a quoted string (it always starts a variable), so a stray '$' --
which no legitimate input carries -- is stripped like newlines. It cannot break out
to a new directive (that needs '"' + ';', both handled); this is defense-in-depth so
the render-site escaper doesn't silently depend on the path allowlist for
nginx-variable safety.

Tests: TestDisallowedOboAudience covers the canonical shared resources and their
bypass variants, legit api:// targets, GUID-in-api:// form, and the
operator-allowlist authoritative mode.

* close two obo target_audience bypasses + wire EGRESS_OBO_ALLOWED_AUDIENCES

Closes two remaining bypasses in the target_audience control and wires the new
allowlist knob through every deployment surface.

Bypass 1 -- non-Graph first-party GUIDs (ARM/Key Vault/Storage/SQL): the shape rule
allowed bare GUIDs (internal Keycloak/Entra client-ids can be GUIDs), and the
GUID denylist only held the two Graph GUIDs, so any other first-party resource
GUID (e.g. ARM 797f4846-..., Key Vault cfa8b339-...) passed and resolved via
'<guid>/.default'. Fix: reject ANY GUID-shaped target under the shape rule (the
first-party set is not safely enumerable); a target that legitimately is a GUID
must be pinned via EGRESS_OBO_ALLOWED_AUDIENCES.

Bypass 2 -- unvalidated scopes override the target: the exchange engine sends
egress_oauth.scopes verbatim, ignoring target_audience, so
scopes=["https://graph.microsoft.com/.default"] with a benign target minted a real
Graph token even under the allowlist. Fix: validate every scope's resource prefix
equals target_audience (matches the documented '<target>/.default' design).

Both are registration-time ValueErrors with tests covering the ARM/Key Vault GUID
targets, the GUID-only-via-allowlist path, and the scope-binding (including under
allowlist mode).

Deployment wiring for EGRESS_OBO_ALLOWED_AUDIENCES (registry owns the feature):
- registry chart: values.yaml (egressAuth.oboAllowedAudiences), configmap-egress.yaml,
  reserved-env-names.txt, + configmap unittest coverage.
- docker compose: registry service in docker-compose{,.prebuilt,.podman}.yml + .env.example.
- terraform/ECS: root + module variable, module passthrough, container env.
- docs: unified-parameter-reference table row + obo-token-exchange security model.

* make obo target_audience shape rule fail closed

The prior shape rule was fail-open: it rejected http(s):// hosts and GUIDs but
ALLOWED any unrecognized form -- other schemes (spiffe://, ftp://, custom://),
braced {guid} / urn:uuid: GUID spellings, and malformed values all passed. That
is backwards for a security control.

Invert to a fail-closed allowlist of exactly two accepted shapes (everything else,
including unknown schemes and every GUID spelling, is dropped):
  a. api://<authority> where the authority is a non-GUID token matching
     [A-Za-z0-9._:-]+ (Entra App ID URI for an internal server; host:port allowed).
  b. a bare, schemeless non-GUID client-id matching [A-Za-z0-9._-]+ (Keycloak).
A GUID (bare or api://<guid>) is still only accepted via the operator allowlist
(EGRESS_OBO_ALLOWED_AUDIENCES), since a GUID could be any first-party resource.

Also fixed:
- _obo_scope_resource split on the scheme's '//' ('api://app' -> 'api:/'), which
  both false-rejected a bare permission-less scope equal to the target and left a
  residual 'api:/'-collision bypass. Now splits the scheme off first.
- Reject a malformed scheme target (api://, api:/, api:) with a clear error.
- Reject empty/whitespace scope entries.

Tests: fail-closed cases (unknown schemes, urn/braced GUIDs, malformed authorities),
api:// host:port acceptance, bare permission-less scope acceptance, malformed-target
and empty-scope rejection.

* allow api://<app-guid> as an obo target without an allowlist entry

The fail-closed shape rule rejected every GUID-shaped target, including the
'api://<app-guid>' form. But that is the standard Entra auto-generated App ID URI
for a custom app registration, so requiring an EGRESS_OBO_ALLOWED_AUDIENCES entry
per server was unreasonable for the normal case.

Distinguish the two GUID forms:
- api://<guid> is ACCEPTED by shape. Entra only resolves an 'api://' string to a
  custom (tenant-local) app that advertises it as an identifierUri; no Microsoft
  first-party resource does, so it can never address Graph/ARM/Key Vault.
- a BARE guid is still REJECTED by shape (that IS how first-party resources are
  directly addressable) and must be pinned via EGRESS_OBO_ALLOWED_AUDIENCES.

Everything else is unchanged: https host URLs, unknown schemes, braced/urn GUID
spellings, and malformed authorities all still fail closed.

Updated the schema docstring/error message, obo-token-exchange.md, and tests
(api://<guid> now in the allowed set; bare-GUID rejection split into its own case).
Example UUIDs in docs/tests use obviously-fake placeholders; the real Microsoft
first-party GUIDs remain only where the code/tests must block them.

* reject the api:// form of known first-party GUIDs (obo target)

Accepting api://<guid> as an obo target (so servers using Entra's auto-generated
App ID URI need no allowlist entry) made the control's safety contingent on an
Entra-internal assumption: that api://<appId> never scheme-normalizes to a
bare-GUID first-party service-principal-name match. That assumption is not
verifiable from the code, and if it is wrong then api://<graph-appId> +
.default would mint a broad Graph delegated token forwarded to the upstream --
the exact confused-deputy this control exists to stop.

Defense-in-depth: reject the api:// form of the KNOWN first-party app-id GUIDs
(Microsoft Graph, Azure AD Graph, ARM, Key Vault) in addition to their already-
rejected bare form. The generic api://<guid> custom-app case still works with no
allowlist entry (the user's requirement); only the enumerated first-party GUIDs
are blocked in both spellings, removing the dependency on Entra's SPN-matching
semantics for those documented targets. A bare GUID (any) remains allowlist-only.

Tests: known first-party GUIDs rejected in api:// form; generic api://<guid> and
named api:// URIs still accepted without an allowlist entry.

* make first-party resources an always-on obo floor; drop hop-1/hop-2 framing

Two refinements to the obo_exchange target_audience control and its docs.

Always-on first-party floor:
- Microsoft Graph, Azure AD Graph, ARM, and Key Vault are now rejected as an obo
  target unconditionally -- matched by app-id GUID (bare or api:// form) and by
  canonical https host (including sovereign clouds) -- and the check runs BEFORE
  the operator allowlist, so EGRESS_OBO_ALLOWED_AUDIENCES can no longer re-enable
  them. There is no supported configuration that OBO-exchanges into these
  resources and forwards the delegated token to an MCP server's upstream.
- The allowlist remains authoritative for everything else (e.g. an internal
  audience that is a bare GUID). Generic api://<guid> custom-app targets still
  pass by shape with no allowlist entry.
- Documented the narrow, double-admin-gated residual (a first-party resource
  outside the floor set expressed as api://<its-guid>) and how to eliminate it.

Terminology:
- Removed the "hop 1 / hop 2" framing from code and the conceptual parts of the
  docs. obo_exchange is a single gateway exchange that produces a token audienced
  to the MCP server's app; whether the server exchanges that token again for a
  downstream resource is the server author's optional choice, not a step the
  gateway performs or requires. The verification runbook still refers to the
  example echo server's own downstream exchange where it literally occurs.

Tests: first-party floor rejected in every form and not re-enablable via the

* feat(registry chart): expose SSRF allowlist for internal MCP-server upstreams

The registry's health checker and proxy validate each server's proxy_pass_url
through the SSRF guard, which blocks private/cluster IPs by default. An in-cluster
MCP server (private ClusterIP, e.g. <svc>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local) is therefore
marked unhealthy, its nginx location is commented out, and requests to it return
405 -- with no way to permit it from Helm values.

Make the guard's operator bypass first-class chart values:
- registry.app.ssrfAllowedHosts  -> SSRF_ALLOWED_HOSTS
- registry.app.ssrfAllowedCidrs  -> SSRF_ALLOWED_CIDRS
Both default to "" (unchanged behavior). Set the cluster service CIDR (e.g.
172.20.0.0/16) to cover all in-cluster servers at once, or list exact hostnames
for least privilege. The cloud metadata address is never permitted by either.

Wiring:
- deployment.yaml: two new env entries after MCP_ADVERTISED_SCOPES.
- values.yaml: documented app.ssrfAllowedHosts / app.ssrfAllowedCidrs.

* fix(registry chart): include openid in default advertised scopes

The chart default for MCP_ADVERTISED_SCOPES was "profile email offline_access",
which omits openid. Entra rejects an authorize request whose scope lacks openid
(AADSTS70011), so MCP-client OAuth login against an Entra-backed gateway failed
out of the box. openid is a standard OIDC scope present in every Keycloak realm
too, so adding it works for both providers and matches the code default
(DEFAULT_ADVERTISED_SCOPES already lists openid).

Default is now "openid profile email offline_access"; the matching helm unittest

* serve the per-server PRM for oauth_user (3LO) on Entra, not just obo_exchange

3LO (oauth_user) servers log the MCP client in at the gateway just like
obo_exchange does, so on Entra they hit the same resource/scope alignment
constraint: the ingress login must target a path-qualified per-server App ID URI,
never the bare-origin gateway PRM (which Entra rejects with AADSTS9010010/500011).
Previously the per-server PRM was served only for obo_exchange, so an MCP client
connecting to a 3LO server on Entra fell back to the broken root PRM and could not
complete OAuth login.

- New server_needs_per_server_prm(egress_auth_mode): True for obo_exchange (any
  provider) and for oauth_user only when auth_provider == entra. Keycloak/Cognito

  OIDC scopes), so their existing, working flow is unchanged.
- wellknown_routes: the per-server PRM route uses the predicate.
- nginx_service: the 401 WWW-Authenticate per-location resource_metadata override
  uses the predicate, so a 3LO-on-Entra server advertises its per-server PRM.
- egress_auth_routes: /api/egress/obo-identifier-uris lists these servers too, so
  the operator knows which per-server URLs to register in the gateway app's
  identifierUris.
- auth_server _obo_extra_audiences docstring: clarify it accepts the per-server aud
  for any egress-enabled server (the audience-acceptance side already works for
  oauth_user; keyed on egress_auth_enabled, not a specific mode).

Tests: oauth_user returns a per-server PRM on Entra; oauth_user 404s on Keycloak
(regression guard for the working root-PRM path); non-egress servers still 404.

* fix(egress): key per-user vault on OIDC sub, not preferred_username

The per-user egress vault key derived user_id from the session/token
username (preferred_username || sub). Entra ACCESS tokens omit
preferred_username, so a DCR client's bearer vend keyed on sub while the
browser-consent path keyed on email -> the vaulted token was written and
read under different ids and the vend always missed (no tools).

Key the vault on the OIDC sub instead, which is present in both id_tokens
and access tokens across providers and stable per (user, gateway app):

- session_store.create_session persists the id_token sub as subject;
  resolve_session returns it so the cookie path exposes it in validation
  data.
- _canonical_egress_user(validation_result) resolves the canonical id
  (data.sub -> data.subject -> sub -> username fallback).
- Both internal tokens carry an egress_user claim; the registry consent-
  write and vend paths key the vault on it (falling back to username).

Existing Entra vault entries keyed on email require a one-time reconnect.
Non-OIDC callers fall back to username and are unaffected.

* fix(egress): derive egress_user on the cookie path (consent callback)

The egress OAuth callback carries no X-Internal-Token-Registry, so
nginx_proxied_auth falls through to enhanced_auth (raw cookie session).
That path did not derive egress_user, so it fell back to username (an
email for Entra), while initiate_consent — reached through nginx with an
internal token — bound the consent state to egress_user (the OIDC sub).
The account-swap guard then saw sub != email and failed the callback with
'state user mismatch' (surfaced as 'Connection failed'), so the token was
never stored and the vend still returned no tools.

- registry session_store.resolve_session now returns the persisted subject
  (the auth_server writes the id_token sub into the shared oauth_sessions
  record at login).
- enhanced_auth passes egress_user=session.subject into the context, so the
  cookie path derives the same canonical id as the internal-token path.

Both consent-write and vend now key the vault on the OIDC sub.

fix(a2a): stop relaying caller credentials to registrant-controlled agent backend

Clear Authorization and Cookie on both the A2A agent-card and JSON-RPC
location blocks so a malicious registered agent cannot capture and replay
the caller's gateway bearer token or registry session cookie. Mirrors the
MCP-side fix in #1391 for the parallel A2A route. Adds a render-level
regression test asserting the caller credential is not forwarded.

feat(a2a): implement A2A egress trust model (spec-native passthrough)

The gateway is a policy gate for A2A, never a credential broker. Split the
two credential roles by header:

- X-Authorization carries the caller's gateway/ingress token: validated at
  /validate, enforces the invoke_agent scope, then stripped on egress (with
  Cookie) so it never reaches the registrant-controlled agent backend.
- Authorization carries the target-agent credential the calling agent
  obtained out-of-band (per the A2A spec and the target card securitySchemes);
  forwarded end-to-end untouched for the target agent to authenticate.

This supersedes the interim strip-both B1 fix. It resolves the B1 credential
relay by construction (the forwarded credential is aud-scoped to the agent,
useless against the registry) while honoring the A2A spec's out-of-band
credential model, since the A2A caller is an agent, not a human user (unlike
the MCP egress OBO path in #1420).

/validate now authenticates agent-path requests on X-Authorization only (no
Authorization fallback, which would authenticate on and leak the target
credential) and rejects a request that duplicates the gateway token into both
headers. Adds render-level and /validate unit tests for all three rules.

Design doc: .scratchpad/pr-1355/a2a-egress-trust-model.md

fix(audit): record raw human-readable identity across all audit streams

Audit records represented one user three incompatible ways: token-mint
stored hash_username(...) (user_<8hex>), while MCP-access and Registry-API
stored a mix of raw email and opaque OIDC sub depending on the auth path.
The same human could not be correlated across streams, and a sub-only row
gave an operator no one to contact (there is no durable sub->email map).

Standardize on the raw, human-readable identity (email -> preferred_username
-> sub) everywhere identity enters an audit record, WITHOUT changing the
`sub`-keyed value that the egress vault and OBO principal-binding depend on:

- Add `_audit_identity_display(validation_result)` in auth_server: the
  human-readable counterpart to `_canonical_egress_user` (which stays sub-keyed
  for vault/OBO). Use it for the MCP-access Identity and the OBO mint display.
- TokenMintAuditRecord: add a raw `username` field; keep populating (now
  deprecated) `username_hash` for back-compat. `_emit_token_mint_audit` gains
  `display_username`; all mint call sites (token-gen + OBO) pass the readable
  identity, resolving email off the self-signed/ingress token claims.
- Thread `email` through the registry `user_context` (`_derive_user_context`,
  `_resolve_context_from_groups`, `enhanced_auth`, `_context_from_internal_token`,
  middleware session fallback); middleware + direct-Identity route sites prefer it.
- Audit read layer + frontend: switch the token_mint stream's query/filter/
  statistics fields and the table/detail display from `username_hash` to the
  raw `username` (frontend falls back to username_hash for old records).

fix(request-source,admin-safety): close spoofable /validate IP, admin-safety fail-open, and realip catch-all

Non-spoofable client IP on the auth_request /validate path.
An nginx auth_request subrequest does not inherit the parent location's
proxy_set_header directives, and the /validate block set neither X-Real-IP nor a
sanitized X-Forwarded-For while enabling proxy_pass_request_headers on. A client
sending "X-Real-IP: 8.8.8.8" therefore had it forwarded verbatim to the
auth-server and recorded as the source in the MCP tool-invocation audit
(get_client_ip prefers X-Real-IP). Set X-Real-IP $remote_addr +
X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for inside both /validate blocks so the
recorded value is nginx's realip-resolved peer, not a client-supplied header.

Admin-safety now fails closed on an empty admin population.
resolve_admin_group_names() returned a valid-but-empty set on predicate/catalogue
drift, and list_admin_usernames() could return an empty set when a user listing
didn't surface group membership; assert_not_last_admin then treated the target as
"not an admin, nothing to guard" and allowed deleting the last admin. Both now
raise AdminSafetyError(503) on an empty result, matching the module's
fail-closed contract.

realip: reject catch-all ranges and scope recursion to stacked proxies.
_render_real_ip_config() accepted 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 (which make nginx trust
every peer, so the spoofable left-most X-Forwarded-For entry wins) and always
emitted real_ip_recursive on. Now reject prefixlen==0 ranges with a warning, and
emit real_ip_recursive on ONLY when more than one trusted CIDR is configured
(stacked proxies, e.g. CloudFront in front of an ALB); a single ALB hop needs no
recursion.

Clarify the loopback --forwarded-allow-ips rationale.
Reworded the registry/auth entrypoint comments to state the flag governs only the
request.client (tier-3) fallback in get_client_ip; the audit IP normally comes
from the X-Real-IP / X-Forwarded-For headers (tiers 1-2), whose trustworthiness
depends on nginx overwriting those headers on every path that reaches
get_client_ip (including the /validate subrequest). Also documented the
"nginx shares the app's network namespace" assumption and its graceful
degradation if nginx is ever run in a separate pod.

Tests: fail-closed on empty admin group set and empty admin user set;
single-CIDR emits no recursion, multi-CIDR enables it, 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0
rejected, catch-all-plus-valid keeps only the valid CIDR. Full affected suites
and the helm registry suite pass.

Third /validate block on the HTTPS (:8443) listener was left unpatched.
docker/nginx_rev_proxy_http_and_https.conf has TWO location = /validate blocks

X-Forwarded-For override, leaving the client-IP spoof open on the primary TLS

Count M2M service-account admins in the admin population.
list_admin_usernames() only inspected the IdP user listing, so an admin whose
group membership lives solely in the MongoDB idp_m2m_clients store (the case for
non-Keycloak IdPs) was invisible. Combined with the empty-set fail-closed added

whose only admins are M2M clients. Merge idp_m2m_clients into the count

fix(admin-safety): count admins by identity, not identifier, so M2M aliases don't mask a last-admin delete

The M2M admin merge indexed each admin by a single username in a flat set. That
had two mutually-exclusive failure modes and no single-set representation could
satisfy both:

- Index by one key only -> a delete targeting the OTHER key (M2M clients are
  deletable by client_id OR name, and for Okta/Auth0 those differ) slips past
  the guard's membership check -> last admin removed (fail-open).
- Index by BOTH keys in a flat set -> the sole M2M admin appears as two entries,
  so `remaining = admins - {target}` still leaves the sibling alias -> guard
  thinks another admin remains -> last admin removed (same fail-open).

Model the population as one entry PER ADMIN, each a frozenset of that admin's
aliases (a lone username for an IdP user; {name, client_id} for an M2M client).
Rename list_admin_usernames -> list_admin_identities returning
list[frozenset[str]], and add _would_empty_admins(admins, target): the target is
matched if it is any admin's alias, and removal empties the population only when
no OTHER alias-set remains. This makes membership-by-any-alias and
distinct-admin counting both correct, so a two-alias M2M admin is recognised by
either key AND counted once. Keycloak (name == client_id) collapses to a single
alias and is unaffected.

Tests: an M2M admin's two aliases are ONE entry; deleting the sole M2M admin by
EITHER alias is refused; deleting it is allowed when a second distinct admin
remains.

fix(a2a): honor X-Forwarded-Proto in card rewrite + drop hardcoded Host in discovery

Two bugs surfaced testing agent-to-agent discovery+invoke through a
TLS-terminating gateway (CloudFront/ALB in front of ECS):

   'http' when TLS is terminated upstream and forwarded to nginx over http. The
   served card then advertised http://.../agent/<path>/, so an A2A client POST
   got a 307 http->https redirect that the client (follow_redirects=false for
   SSRF safety) refused -> invoke failed. Prefer X-Forwarded-Proto (validated to
   exactly http/https to reject a spoofed value), fall back to ngx.var.scheme for
   direct-TLS deployments. No effect when the header is absent (compose/local).

2. registry_discovery_client sent a hardcoded 'Host: localhost' on the semantic
   discovery call, which a real CDN/ALB rejects with 403 (host mismatch). Let the

feat(egress): add RFC 8707 resource indicator for custom OAuth providers

Thread an optional resource indicator (RFC 8707) through the egress OAuth
engine so the gateway can obtain per-user tokens bound to a specific
protected resource.

When a custom provider is configured with `custom_resource`, the value is
sent as the `resource` parameter on the authorize request AND on both token
grants (code exchange + refresh). Built-in providers carry no resource, so
their flows are unchanged.

Motivation: resource servers that mint per-resource tokens reject the flow
without it. Atlassian's Rovo MCP (https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp/authv2)
fails the authorize step with "Invalid context provided" when the indicator
is absent, and rejects a token whose audience is the generic api.atlassian.com
REST API instead of the MCP resource itself.

- schemas: OAuthProviderConfig.resource (optional)
- oauth_engine: emit resource on build_authorize_url / exchange_code /
  refresh_token
- providers: resolve_provider threads custom_resource onto custom configs
- api: EgressConfigRequest.custom_resource persisted + exposed in the GET
  view; validated as an absolute https URI without a fragment (it is
  reflected into the authorize 302 and token body, not a request target, so a
  structural check applies rather than the SSRF guard)
- docs + unit tests covering all three legs

security guidelines:

- Disabled/inactive flag: a schemaless store can hold a non-boolean enabled
  value, so the re-check must be 'is True' (fail closed on anything not provably
  active), not 'is not False' which passes 0/null/empty/"false".

fix(rate-limiting): surface throttle as 429 through nginx auth_request (#295)

of 429.

authorization 403 (marker absent) still returns 403. The $rl_* vars are
declared at http scope via a map with an empty default so control-plane
and registry-only-mode locations that never capture them still resolve
the references.

fix(rate-limiting): classify human tokens as user, not agent (#295)

The limiter derived caller_type from validation_result['client_id'], but for
Keycloak (and other OIDC providers) that field is the token's azp (the OAuth
client, e.g. mcp-gateway-web) and is present on EVERY token, including a
human's browser/password-grant token. So every human was misclassified as an
agent: the limiter picked the group's agent_max_requests (usually unset) and a
user caller limit never fired, and all web users shared one mcp-gateway-web
counter.

as an agent only when the token carries a top-level client_id CLAIM (emitted
by OIDC only for client_credentials/M2M tokens), else a user keyed on
username. This does not touch the widely-used validation_result['client_id']
field (auth/audit depend on it) - it only corrects what the limiter keys on.

fix(rate-limiting): provider-aware caller classification (fixes Cognito) (#295)

The caller-type resolver treated a token as an agent whenever it carried a
client_id claim. That is correct for Keycloak/Entra/Auth0 (only a
client_credentials token has a top-level client_id claim), but WRONG for
Cognito: every Cognito access token -- user AND M2M -- carries a client_id
claim, so every human user was misclassified as an agent (the user caller
gate never fired; verified live against the ECS/Cognito deployment: a
25/60s user limit did not throttle a 30-call burst).

Make _resolve_rate_limit_caller provider-aware (branch on validation_result
['method']):
- Cognito: agent iff a client_id claim is present AND there is no end-user
  'username' claim (M2M client_credentials tokens have no username).
- Keycloak/Entra/Auth0: agent iff a top-level client_id claim is present OR
  the subject is a service-account-* principal.

service-account cases; the existing Keycloak password-grant / M2M tests still
pass.

feat(auth): Cognito M2M (client_credentials) support for agent callers (#295)

The Cognito provider only trusted the web + IDE client ids, so a machine
(client_credentials) access token from any dedicated M2M app client was
rejected at /validate -- Cognito was the only IdP with no M2M support (vs
Keycloak/Okta/Auth0/PingFederate). That blocked Cognito agents entirely,
including per-agent rate limiting.

Add COGNITO_M2M_CLIENT_IDS: a config-driven, default-empty (fail-closed)
allowlist of app-client ids whose client_credentials tokens are accepted.
Cognito access tokens are not audience-bound, so the client_id claim is
checked against this list. The single value '*' is a wildcard scoped to
MACHINE tokens only (no username claim) -- it accepts any client in the pool
without enumerating each (Pattern B: one M2M client per agent), while
user/login tokens stay restricted to the web + IDE clients, so '*' can never
be abused to forge a login. Authorization for M2M callers comes from the
token's own scope claim, as before.

Wired across all surfaces: factory env, Terraform/ECS (auth-server container),
Helm (auth-server secret + values + reserved-env-names), docker-compose,
.env.example. Unit tests cover explicit allowlist accept/reject, fail-closed
default, the M2M wildcard, and the security case that the wildcard does NOT
accept a user token from an unknown client. 569 auth-server unit tests +
